interventions.speaker_label: Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, on 3 June the European Commission adopted the technological sovereignty package. This is a crucial step for Europe: we are positioning ourselves for the future of digital technologies and addressing our strategic dependencies. Europe needs to be in a position to make its own choices, avoiding dependence on single dominant suppliers.

Because we live in a world where geopolitics and technology go hand in hand, those who lead technological innovation will shape the future. We must ensure that Europe plays the leading role. The recent US export control directive on Anthropic's most advanced AI models is a case in point. We are seeing a new generation of highly capable AI models reach the market. These models offer significant benefits, including for cyber defence, but they also raise serious cybersecurity concerns that need to be addressed. This is not only about single jurisdiction or single companies: it is a shared challenge. We believe that contingency measures taken in this light should not be discriminatory against partners.

With our Tech Sovereignty package, we are taking concrete steps to address such challenges. The package has three main objectives: to transform our economy by driving the adoption of new technologies and AI in Europe, to reinforce the resilience of our supply chains, and to promote the European way for tech sovereignty.

The package is designed to deliver through four key elements. First, the Chips Act 2.0 that builds on the success of the European Chips Act. It includes a set of demand-side measures to stimulate the uptake of chips made in Europe, bringing chip manufacturers closer to growth sectors like AI, cloud services and data centres. It also reinforces European supply-side capabilities across the entire value chain, including through strategic projects with strong EU added value focusing on advanced manufacturing, design and packaging.

Following the AI Continent Action Plan, the Cloud and AI Development Act turns the vision of tripling Europe's data centre capacity within the next five to seven years into reality, and doing so in a sustainable manner. Very importantly, the Act also encourages tech sovereignty in our public sector: it establishes clear criteria for sovereign cloud and also strengthens support for the development of AI services – notably EU frontier models – while using its buying power to boost EU security and resilience.

Here the Commission's own internal digital sovereignty action plan is paving the way: from migrating our core IT systems to EU-based cloud infrastructure, to deploying sovereign AI tools in our daily operations, we are proving that strategic autonomy is not just an aspiration, it is a very concrete action. With the open-source strategy, we are making and working to ensure that European companies and public administration are never again locked into a handful of platforms controlled elsewhere.

In all of this, I want to underline that technological sovereignty does not mean isolation or protectionism. It's about making Europe stronger, more resilient and less exposed to critical dependencies. We will remain open to trade, investment and cooperation with trusted partners, but Europe must also be able to develop, deploy and protect the technologies that our economy, public services and security depend on.

Honourable Members, two more points before I conclude. Firstly, our Tech Sovereignty package takes its climate and environmental footprint very seriously. Europe's structurally higher energy costs are a genuine competitive constraint, particularly for technologies that consume power at scale. This is precisely why the package also includes the Strategic Roadmap for digitalisation and AI in energy.

Secondly, technological sovereignty also requires investments. Other tech-leading countries have invested massively, while Europe continues to suffer from a huge gap in equity and high-risk financing to tech. This is a clear market failure to be addressed, especially for large-scale ventures and scale-ups. Just for the initiatives of this package, the total investment needs are estimated up to EUR 450 billion in the next 10 years. We know that public funding is very crucial, but it will in no way be sufficient to bridge such a big investment gap, so we need ways to crowd in large amounts of private investments.

The reform of the EU's capital markets under the savings and investments union will improve how the EU's financial system channels savings to productive investments. At the same time, the Commission is now launching a consultation with our Member States and with the European Investment Bank Group and other key stakeholders on the idea of setting up a European equity capacity. In other words, we aim to create a mechanism managing a portfolio of equity investments in advanced technologies and infrastructure that are critical for our economic security, such as digital, but also clean energy and biotechnologies.
This can be a true game changer for Europe, and I count on your support.

interventions.speaker_label: Ana Miguel Pedro, em nome do Grupo PPE.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, Senhora Comissária, uma decisão tomada fora da União Europeia foi suficiente para pôr em causa o acesso de empresas, investigadores, administrações públicas e aliados a modelos avançados de inteligência artificial.

Estamos a falar da tecnologia que começa a suportar a cibersegurança, a investigação científica, os serviços públicos, a indústria e a energia, a saúde e a defesa. É uma questão estratégica, geopolítica e de segurança. E a pergunta que temos de fazer é se pode a Europa aceitar que o acesso às capacidades críticas do século XXI dependa de uma autorização política de terceiros.

Pode uma pequena e média empresa europeia, que integrou modelos avançados de inteligência artificial nos seus processos, descobrir de um dia para o outro que deixou de ter acesso à tecnologia de que depende? Pode uma administração pública construir serviços essenciais sobre sistemas que podem ser limitados, suspensos ou condicionados por interesses estratégicos externos? Pode a Europa ambicionar liderar a transição digital se não controlar as infraestruturas, os modelos, os dados, a capacidade computacional e a cadeia de valor que tornam essa transição possível?

A resposta tem de ser «não». Temos regras, temos valores, mas a Europa não pode ser uma potência regulatória com dependência tecnológica crítica. Não basta dizer ao mundo como a inteligência artificial deve ser governada; temos de ter capacidade para a desenvolver, alojar, auditar, proteger e disponibilizar em solo europeu, sob jurisdição europeia e com infraestruturas europeias. Não basta sermos fortes na norma se formos fracos na capacidade.

Por isso, Senhora Comissária, o pacote de soberania tecnológica apresentado pela Comissão é bem‑vindo. A Europa tem de produzir mais semicondutores, ter mais centros de dados, mais supercomputadores, mais cloud europeia e maior capacidade para treinar os seus próprios modelos de inteligência artificial.

Uma dependência tolerável em tempos normais pode tornar‑se uma vulnerabilidade grave em tempos de crise. A Europa aprendeu com a energia que a dependência estratégica tem custos: custos económicos, custos políticos, custos de segurança. Não podemos repetir o mesmo erro na inteligência artificial.

interventions.speaker_label: Alex Agius Saliba, on behalf of the S&D Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the S&D Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, is there anyone left who believes that Europe can put its economy in the hands of Donald Trump and his big tech oligarchs? We have seen what happened to the international court judges being cut off from essential digital services because of sanctions. Just try to imagine living without Microsoft, Mastercard and other American technologies – good luck! But you can't. Therefore, Europe cannot ignore its tech dependency.

A kill switch to turn off technology is not only a risk today; it's a reality. On Friday, the US Administration decided to turn off the most powerful AI models of Anthropic for the EU. This is a watershed moment. Europe needs to control its own tech infrastructure if it wants sovereignty. If we want to stop the blackmail, we need to build our own solutions using the tech talent that we have in Europe. We can build them cheaper and provide services that do respect our rules, so let's make more use of them.

The Tech Sovereignty package needs that ambition if it wants to play into the hands of EU companies and truly make a difference. Part of the solution is swift and strict enforcement of our tech rules. Our legislation protects our citizens and our market from online abuse, but big tech is not abiding by it.

Being sovereign means that our citizens and this Parliament decide on the rules of the game, and not the almighty big tech companies. If they want to enter our internal market, they need to respect our rules and respect them in full.

interventions.speaker_label: Ernő Schaller-Baross, a PfE képviselőcsoport nevében.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Úr! A digitális szuverenitás erősítése fontos és támogatandó cél. Az infrastruktúra fejlesztése, a munkahelyek teremtése pedig különösen.

Európa digitális versenyképességét ugyanakkor nem önmagában a nagy összegű beruházások fogják meghatározni, hanem az, hogy képesek vagyunk-e egy olyan környezetet teremteni, amely ösztönzi az innovációt, támogatja a vállalkozásokat, és teret ad a technológiai fejlődésnek.

Biztos asszony! A világ vezető technológiai központjai nem központi tervek alapján váltak sikeressé. Előbb megszületett a piaci kereslet, az infrastruktúra pedig ezt követte. Éppen ezért ott kell fejlesztenünk, ahol arra valóban szükség van, és ahol a fejlesztések a legjobb ár-érték arányban szolgálják Európa és Magyarország jövőjét is.

Különösen akkor, amikor az uniós költségvetés forrásai végesek, és egyre több területen szembesülünk forráshiánnyal. Miközben az Európai Bizottság újabb milliárdokat talált technológiai nagy projektekre – ez részben helyes is – a kohéziós politika és a vidéki térségek vagy gazdák támogatásai állandó nyomás alatt vannak. Nehéz megmagyarázni a termelőknek, hogy az ő forrásaik szűkösek, miközben a Bizottság újabb és újabb milliárdokat mozgósít olyan technológiai fejlesztésekre, amelyek megtérülésére még egyelőre korántsem egyértelmű válaszokat látunk.
Ezért olyan digitális politikára van szükség, ami az emberek igényeiből indul ki, felméri a piacot. Ez nem ideológiai kérdés, hanem versenyképes teljesítménnyel és innovációval kell megteremtenünk.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señora comisaria, hay algo que me llama la atención cada vez que hablamos de soberanía digital: queremos liderar la inteligencia artificial, queremos liderar las tecnologías del futuro, queremos reducir nuestras dependencias estratégicas, pero seguimos dependiendo demasiado de tecnologías, infraestructuras y cadenas de suministro desarrolladas fuera de Europa.

A veces me da la impresión de que algunos creen que la solución pasa por aislarnos de quienes hoy lideran la innovación tecnológica mundial. Creo que sería un error, porque Europa necesita desarrollar capacidades propias, pero también necesita seguir colaborando con nuestros socios y aliados tecnológicos. La soberanía tecnológica no puede convertirse en un aislamiento tecnológico.

Si queremos liderar la inteligencia artificial necesitamos centros de datos, semiconductores, ingenieros y energía asequible y fiable. Porque no existe la soberanía digital sin soberanía energética. También debemos reconocer una realidad fundamental: no existe la soberanía cibernética sin industria.

Gran parte de las infraestructuras críticas que queremos proteger son construidas, operadas y defendidas cada día por empresas privadas. Por eso, nuestra tarea no debe ser crear nuevos obstáculos, nuestra tarea debe ser crear las condiciones para que las empresas puedan invertir, innovar y crecer en Europa. Porque la verdadera pregunta no es cuánto regulamos la tecnología, la verdadera pregunta es si dentro de diez años seguiremos dependiendo de la tecnología de otros o habremos sido capaces de desarrollar la nuestra. Y ese es el desafío que Europa debe empezar a afrontar desde hoy.

interventions.speaker_label: Helmut Brandstätter, im Namen der Renew-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Technologie ist Macht. Technologie ist die Macht. Technologie heißt unsere Wirtschaft ordnen, unser soziales Gefüge. Technologie als Macht ist auch wichtig für unsere Sicherheit. Und wir haben gelernt: Donald Trump will uns dominieren. Er will nicht, dass wir Macht haben. Er möchte Macht über uns haben, und deswegen müssen wir uns wehren.

Und wir müssen uns mehr wehren, Frau Kommissarin. Sie haben einige wichtige Sachen gesagt, aber wann haben wir endlich den Kapitalmarkt? Nur ein einiger europäischer Kapitalmarkt gibt uns die Chance, auch große Unternehmen hier aufzubauen. Ich bitte Sie auch, fahren Sie in die Vereinigten Staaten. Dort gibt es Forscherinnen und Forscher, Unternehmen, die wollen dort nicht mehr leben in diesem Land, das eher schlechter wird; die wollen zu uns nach Europa kommen.

Und noch etwas: Es gibt ja komische Leute in der Politik, die sagen, ein kleines Land – Österreich – müsste souverän werden. Das ist ja absurd! Wir als Europäische Union können souverän werden, und dafür müssen wir jetzt handeln. Das machen wir für unsere Bürgerinnen und Bürger, gegen die Mächte von außen, für unser Europa.

interventions.speaker_label: Virginijus Sinkevičius, on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues, the recent restrictions on access to Anthropic's latest AI models should be a final call for Europe to wake up because this is exactly how digital dependence looks like.

Whatever the exact security concerns, the political lesson is very clear. A technology that European companies, researchers and public authorities may need tomorrow, it might be just limited by a decision taken outside of Europe.
It does not always come as a crisis. Sometimes it comes as a very simple update to terms of access and export control decision, or a model that suddenly is just no longer available.

The Commission's new tax sovereignty package is therefore a necessary step. Europe needs stronger capacity in AI, cloud, semiconductors and open source. But we should be honest: announcing a package is not enough. We need implementation, investment and public procurement that, first of all, helps European solutions to scale.

And no, this is not about closing Europe. We need partners, including in the United States, but partnership cannot mean a structural dependence. If we want resilience, we must first of all build it ourselves. If we want sovereignty, we must be ready to pay for it, organise it and defend it.

interventions.speaker_label: Pernando Barrena Arza, on behalf of The Left Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of The Left Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, the European technological sovereignty package means good news, as it is allegedly aimed at strengthening Europe's digital autonomy and resilience. However, the package mainly supports a market‑led expansion of data centres and artificial intelligence infrastructure, risking either market fragmentation between Member States or the shift from third country dependencies, like China or the USA, to dependency on European oligopolies.

Please be aware that the problem is not only that Europe takes sufficient chips, cloud and artificial intelligence infrastructure. The political problem is that the Commission risks defining sovereignty mainly as an industrial and market objective, instead of a democratic, social and ecological objective.

Our concerns are so far: the balance between technological sovereignty and democratic control; simplification cannot be a synonym for deregulation, as we are seeing in the AI Omnibus; the open-source strategy must not remain symbolic, but seriously taken; and the energy dimension of the package. We will reject any revival of nuclear power‑based solutions.
So good intentions in the headlines, but a lot to be improved in the fine print.

interventions.speaker_label: Siegbert Frank Droese, im Namen der ESN-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, verehrte Kollegen! Digitale Souveränität ist ein richtiges Ziel. Europa darf bei der digitalen Infrastruktur, bei Halbleitern, bei Cybersicherheit nicht dauerhaft von den USA oder von China abhängig sein. Aber was die Kommission daraus macht, ist nahezu immer das Gegenteil von echter Souveränität: immer neue Regulierung, immer neue Zentralisierung, immer neue Kontrollinstrumente und neue Behörden. Souveränität entsteht durch innovative und starke Unternehmen, fairen Wettbewerb ohne Green Deal-Fesseln, technologische Offenheit und nationale Handlungsfreiheit, aber eben nicht durch Bürokratie und Planwirtschaft aus Brüssel.

Negatives Beispiel dafür ist der digitale Euro. Der wird uns als Modernisierung verkauft, wird aber tatsächlich von niemandem verlangt oder gebraucht und birgt für das Bargeld und für die finanzielle Freiheit der Europäer erhebliche Risiken. Der digitale Euro ist erstens ein Experiment, zweitens ein staatlich kontrolliertes Zahlungsmittel und wird drittens der Einstieg in Überwachung und programmierbares Geld sein.
Wer digitale Resilienz haben will, muss die Freiheit der Menschen Europas beachten. Der Kommission dagegen geht es immer zuerst und überall um absolute Kontrolle – genau das Gegenteil von Freiheit.

interventions.speaker_label: Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, I very much agree with what many of you said, that Europe has everything that is needed to be competitive in technologies. So, I think it is important that we are building to our own strengths.

It is good to also underline that we have world‑class science and research in Europe. We have a very strong industrial base in Europe. We have also huge potential in our start‑ups – we have 45 000 start‑ups with great ideas – but now we have to ensure and make sure that our start‑ups are able to scale up their businesses in Europe.

That is why we have to focus very much on our single market, to remove the barriers between Member States, to accelerate our savings and investments union to attract investments, and also to make Europe easier and faster for businesses by cutting red tape and bureaucracy from our businesses. At the same time, we also have to use much more actively public procurement to boost our own home‑grown technologies in Europe. And of course, by using open source, we can do that.

It is important also to underline, like many of you said, that tech sovereignty is not about isolation or protectionism, but we see certainly that we have to build up our own capacities in critical fields, like in AI, semiconductors, quantum computing, cybersecurity technologies and in space technology. These are very critical technologies where we have to have our own capacity, but at the same time, we want to work very closely with our trusted partners because nobody can be competitive alone. We always need our partners.

So, this package is very much about the resilience and security of the European Union because we want to be sure that at the same time that we are open for investments, open for trade, that these very long global supply chains cannot be weaponised against us. That we have also our own capacity, we have alternatives and nobody has the so‑called kill switch element to our critical technologies.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señora vicepresidenta, quiero comenzar compartiendo tres noticias recientes.

En primer lugar, hace unos días, uno de los principales desarrolladores de IA en el mundo restringió formalmente el acceso a sus modelos más avanzados. En segundo lugar, la semana pasada, China anunció una inversión de casi 300 000 millones de dólares en una red nacional de centros de datos, exigiendo que al menos el 80 % de la tecnología utilizada proceda de proveedores nacionales. Y, en los últimos meses, hemos visto cómo Irán señalaba infraestructuras de computación en la nube en Baréin y Dubái como objetivos militares.

Tres ejemplos diferentes que hablan de una misma realidad: la soberanía tecnológica no es solo una cuestión de competitividad —que también—, sino que es, asimismo, una cuestión estratégica y de seguridad.
Por eso, es fundamental que la ambición de esta propuesta se traduzca en resultados concretos.

En primer lugar, el objetivo de triplicar nuestra capacidad computacional para 2030 no puede admitir retrasos. En segundo lugar, reducir nuestra dependencia de proveedores externos de semiconductores exige algo más que identificar vulnerabilidades, necesitamos objetivos claros y mecanismos que permitan medir los avances realizados. Por último, la coordinación entre política energética y tecnologías digitales no es una opción, es un imperativo.
Esto es un primer paso. Estamos en la buena dirección, aunque el futuro no depende de las intenciones, sino de los resultados.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señora vicepresidenta, por fin tenemos sobre la mesa el tan esperado paquete de soberanía digital, en un momento en el que Europa sigue dependiendo en más de un 80 % de infraestructuras digitales controladas fuera de la Unión, lo que también supone un coste estimado de 264 000 millones de euros.

La Ley de desarrollo de la computación en la nube y la inteligencia artificial es su pieza central, pero creemos que su enfoque sigue siendo demasiado débil. El diseño por niveles de esa soberanía en la nube no reduce de forma real la dependencia y deja en manos de grandes proveedores extranjeros amplias partes del sector público que van del 70 % al 99 %.

En la práctica, los hiperescaladores siguen dominando la nube, la inteligencia artificial y la infraestructura de centros de datos que sostienen nuestra economía digital. Y eso es clave. Los centros de datos no son solo infraestructura técnica, son el núcleo físico del poder digital europeo donde se decide quién controla los datos, la continuidad del servicio y nuestra resiliencia ante crisis o presiones externas.
Si queremos una soberanía digital real, este paquete debe pasar de la gestión del riesgo a la construcción de la propia capacidad europea.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Mr President, when it comes to digital sovereignty and innovation in the digital sector, the EU is lagging far behind the United States and increasingly behind China, too. And this has been the case for very long now.

In Europe, we lack enough software and hardware engineers, chip manufacturing is limited, expensive energy makes investing in data centres in Europe unattractive, and so does overregulation. At best, the EU is copying innovation in tech to have European alternatives. The problem is that the way innovation works is that those who pioneer innovation usually grab the largest market share. Copying digital innovation does not result in digital sovereignty. Therefore, the Commission's usual strategy of throwing money at the problem won't work either.

Let me give you an example of how serious we are about digital sovereignty. This is an email we all received in our mailboxes. Do you remember? As of 4 June 2026, Qwant will replace Google as default search engine on European Parliament computers, in line with the Parliament's commitment to digital sovereignty and the protection of users' personal data. The problem is the tutorial video added to the email explains to you how to go through your different browsers and switch back your search engine to Google. That's how serious we are.

But let me give you also an example about the Commission's tech savviness and commitment. President von der Leyen deletes her messages with Pfizer CEO, and after investigation and pressure, what is the Commission's spokesperson saying? That she had to free up space on her phone. This is not serious – this is embarrassing incompetence.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signora Commissaria, la sovranità digitale si raggiunge quando si possiedono tre cose: i dati, le infrastrutture e le capacità di difendere le infrastrutture e i dati. Oggi l'Europa si pone l'obiettivo ambizioso di raggiungerli tutti e tre.

Io personalmente, mera opinione personale, sono molto convinto del terzo e un po' più scettico sul primo, sulla sovranità dei dati. Ma ne aggiungerei un quarto: noi dobbiamo individuare una via europea all'intelligenza artificiale e alle nuove tecnologie. Se noi partiamo per copiare o inseguire quello che gli altri fanno da vent'anni, partiamo sconfitti.

Noi abbiamo dei settori in Europa in cui già primeggiamo: penso alla sanità, alla manifattura, all'artigianato, all'agricoltura. Ecco, l'applicazione dell'intelligenza artificiale e delle nuove tecnologie a questi settori deve essere la nostra via alla sovranità, non inseguire e copiare ciò che fanno gli altri.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear Commissioner, sometimes it takes a political stunt to get things moving. Kennedy's moonshot speech, of course, the creation of Airbus – bold declarations that precede the reality they eventually created.
So did the first European Chips Act. It was ambitious, but it did not get things moving yet because it forgot to address the demand. Who was going to buy those advanced chips?
I am glad the new Cloud and AI Development Act nudges European governments away from American cloud providers and towards European alternatives, but this at least puts some demand at the table.

But real demand, colleagues, does not come from governments. Real demand comes from the market, and right now, building and training European large language models with the most advanced AI chips is currently effectively impossible within the EU, at least if you intend to follow laws and rules like the Copyright Directive or the GDPR.
So, here is the stunt. Here is the moonshot. Here is the Airbus moment of our time. Clear the runway for European AI to grow on European soil and get things moving. Deregulate.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Gestern hat die US-Regierung Anthropic verboten, ihr KI-Spitzenmodell für Nichtamerikaner anzubieten, Europa eingeschlossen; das Modell übrigens, das Anthropic den europäischen Behörden wochenlang nicht einmal zur Prüfung vorgelegt hat. Für diese US-Regierung sind wir keine Partner, sondern Feinde. Und spätestens jetzt müssen doch alle verstehen, wie gefährlich unsere Abhängigkeit von ausländischer Technologie ist.

Vorletzte Woche hat die Kommission endlich das Paket zur technologischen Souveränität vorgelegt, für die sich dieses Parlament lange eingesetzt hat. Aber dieses Paket enttäuscht, denn ein klares Bekenntnis zu Innovation und Sicherheit made in Europe fehlt in diesem Paket.

Wir müssen doch endlich den Elefanten im Raum angehen: US-Tech-Konzerne sind keine trusted partners mehr. Sie streben gemeinsam mit US-Präsident Trump nach der Weltherrschaft des Stärksten und der Abschaffung einer regelbasierten Weltordnung und Wirtschaft. Unsere Bürgerinnen und Bürger in Europa verdienen etwas Besseres, aber dafür müssen wir, muss dieses Parlament jetzt kämpfen.

Do you want our citizens to subsidise that energy in order to have American AI? So Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg and a lot of other US companies can make money? This is what is happening in the US. Az Anthropic például július 8-tól új adatvédelmi rendelkezés léptet életbe, amely lehetővé teszi, hogy jogi megkeresés nélkül átadja beszélgetési adatainkat külföldi kormányzati ügynökségeknek, megsértve ezzel a GDPR 6. és 48. cikkét.

A Nagy Testvér tehát figyel, és mi a polgáraink magánélethez való jogát sem tudjuk garantálni az etikus szabályainkkal. A szuverenitást azzal kell kezdeni, hogy rászorítjuk a BigTech cégeket a törvényeink betartására.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Madam Commissioner, colleagues, well, we are serious about competitiveness. Building state-of-the-art digital infrastructure is a necessity but is not enough. Europe does not need fibre, 5G, cloud capacity only to tick targets on a scoreboard. We need them to be used at full capacity for our businesses, researchers, hospitals, industry and public services.

Too often when the Commission is bold, the Council becomes mellow. Too often when we promise simplification, we multiply reporting. And too often when we say we deliver for consumers, we reduce the debate to low prices for entertainment. But serving citizens means building a vital digital economy that produces value, multiplies jobs and keeps innovation in Europe.
Decoupling from the rest of the world is not possible. Unlocking our own market potential is possible, as well as helping market forces work across borders or giving predictability to investment.
Europe does not need isolation or overregulation to be sovereign. Europe needs a digital infrastructure that is built, scaled and put to good use.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, "Su ogni epoca incombe il rischio di costruire un mondo disumano e più ingiusto": con queste parole si apre l'enciclica di Papa Leone XIV "Magnifica umanità".

L'allarme non è certo verso l'innovazione digitale o l'intelligenza artificiale, ma verso chi la crea, chi la governa e a quali fini la utilizza. Se il controllo è in mano alle democrazie per il bene comune e la dignità dell'umano o ai privati per il dominio di pochi ed esclusivamente per il profitto.
L'Europa è in ritardo, regola tecnologie che non ha creato e non possiede a sufficienza i dati e gli strumenti utili. Ora abbiamo iniziato. Bene, ma dobbiamo correre.
L'autonomia strategica richiede unità, grandi investimenti comuni, mercato unico, garanzia di una diffusione dell'innovazione dal laboratorio fino al territorio e quindi partecipazione.
Allora, e solo allora, l'Europa potrà trovare anche su questo il suo ruolo nel mondo per difendere anche nel futuro i suoi valori: libertà, uguaglianza e la democrazia.

paragraphs.text: Pane předsedající, aktuální americký zákaz přístupu k nejpokročilejší modelům AI ukazuje, jak závislí jsme na zahraničních technologiích a jaké důsledky pro naši konkurenceschopnost to může mít. Je pozitivní, že Komise přichází s kroky pro rozvoj umělé inteligence v Evropské unii. Pro vlastní bezpečí potřebujeme evropská řešení, evropskou digitální infrastrukturu a evropské pokročilé čipy.

Ale dovolte mi tři poznámky. První poznámka, potřebujeme skutečnou geografickou vyváženost a věřím, že podpořen bude i dobře připravený projekt AI Gigafactory v České republice. Za druhé, Spojené státy a Čína už nám ujely o řadu koňských délek a ten náskok budeme stahovat velmi obtížně. Evropská unie si za to může sama. Přehnali jsme to s regulací evropské umělé inteligence. A za třetí, digitální autonomie nesmí znamenat úplné uzavření před světem. Je pro nás klíčové i nadále úzce spolupracovat s partnery, jako je Jižní Korea, Japonsko nebo Tchaj-wan.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Dla wielu koleżanek i kolegów to, co wydarzyło się w piątek w sprawie Anthropic, to szok i niedowierzanie. Przyznam, że sam byłem tym wstrząśnięty. Ale nas, polityków nie wybrano po to, żebyśmy byli zaszokowani, bo widzimy jasno, że ta sytuacja to żaden przypadek. To kolejny przykład, jak polityka transakcyjna wykorzystuje uzależnienia jako broń masowego rażenia. Nie ma znaczenia, czy chodzi o energię, surowce, amunicję czy sztuczną inteligencję. To jest nowy świat, w którym żyjemy, i dla naszego bezpieczeństwa powinniśmy przyjąć, że tak już po prostu będzie.

Naszym następnym krokiem musi być rozmowa o tym, co z tym zrobimy. Europa musi zacząć budować swoją niezależność cyfrową krok po kroku. Propozycje Komisji są być może zbyt słabe, zwłaszcza gdy popatrzymy na przyjętą przez ten Parlament w styczniu rezolucję w sprawie suwerenności technologicznej, której byłem współautorem. Ale od czegoś trzeba zacząć, więc zacznijmy od wsparcia dla otwartego oprogramowania („open source first″) i kreowania popytu na europejskie usługi chmurowe. A potem pójdźmy dalej. W ramach prac nad aktem o sieciach cyfrowych wzmocnijmy europejskich graczy cyfrowych. Tylko tyle i aż tyle, żebyśmy poczuli się trochę bezpieczniejsi.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, in Star Wars, the most powerful machine in the galaxy is called the Death Star. AI may not be the Death Star yet, but it's definitely not a simple digital service anymore. It's infrastructure for our economy, our research and security.
So Trump's decision to block our access to Anthropic's most advanced AI models is no surprise. But if Washington can cut us off, it means we're not on the Death Star; we're in its sights.

But there is a new hope. Although the Empire kept building bigger and louder, it was outflown by rebels in smaller X-wings who were simply smarter and better. For European tech sovereignty, our edge is never going to be bigger and louder; the European way is always going to be smarter and better.
So let's not try to imitate the Death Star. Let's build X-wings. Commissioner, how will you create the conditions that enable Europe to build? I believe we can do it. May the force be with you.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, three races are under way: money, intelligence and biology. The European Union has entered none of them as a builder. The European Union passed the world's first comprehensive AI act and called it 'leadership'. And the result is that American companies are building EU-only product tiers, which are slower, weaker and sometimes even absent from our market.

While the EU is writing the rules, the rails are being built elsewhere. Our stablecoins are American. Our EU data boundary is Microsoft's architecture. Meanwhile, China built mBridge; the US built BioRadar and Stablecoin Dominance. Both are racing to control the rails of money, intelligence and biology, and Europe is racing to control the paperwork.
Sovereignty is not a regulation: it is owning the chips, the models, the payment rails and the biosurveillance networks. That's the actual infrastructure of the next century.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, liebe Frau Vizepräsidentin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Europas digitale Souveränität ist wichtig für die Zukunft. Nicht, weil Europa sich abschotten soll, sondern weil Europa stärker nach außen entwickeln muss, um den kooperativen Ansatz Europas zu leben, auch gegen den konfrontativen Ansatz, den so viele Teile der Welt heute versuchen.

Sie werden von Anthropic gehört haben – möglicherweise die stärkste Applikation der künstlichen Intelligenz, die es heute gibt, und die USA haben erst in der vergangenen Woche entschieden, dass Anthropic nicht mehr außerhalb der USA zum Einsatz kommen darf. Das ist ein weiteres Warnsignal für unsere europäische Innovationskraft und damit für unsere zukünftige Wirtschaftskraft und für die Chancen der jungen Menschen in Europa und auch für die Zivilisation unserer Art mit sozialen Sicherungssystemen.

Alles das hängt davon ab, dass Unternehmen in Europa ihre künstliche-Intelligenz-Applikationen entwickeln können, trainieren können. Es ist auch ein subsidiärer Vorgang, ein Vorgang der Subsidiarität, dass der einzelne Betrieb, die einzelne Organisation, ihre eigenen AI-Applikationen trainiert. Wir müssen junge Menschen, besonders Mädchen und Frauen, für naturwissenschaftliche Fächer begeistern. Wir müssen Regulierung reduzieren, selbstverständlich den ethischen Rahmen für Europa halten, und wir müssen es schaffen, dass in Europa investiert wird, auch durch den Kapitalbinnenmarkt, für künstliche Intelligenz auf unserem Kontinent.

Det er sådan, vi sikrer vores suverænitet og dermed vores demokrati.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, doamnă comisară, inteligența artificială trebuie să fie în sprijinul oamenilor, pentru oameni și nu împotriva lor. Și când spun împotriva lor, asta înseamnă că sub nicio formă nu trebuie să acceptăm ca să existe vreo posibilitate ca inteligența artificială să ducă la pierderea locurilor de muncă, pe de o parte, iar pe de altă parte, să constituie o amenințare la adresa vieților private.

Din acest motiv, acest pachet este binevenit pentru că vine să stabilească niște reguli foarte clare: care este partea de suveranitate și care este partea de integrare în Uniunea Europeană; care este partea de control; care sunt persoanele și oamenii care lucrează în inteligența artificială și centrele de cloud.

Iar pentru toate statele membre, inclusiv pentru România, trebuie să existe această obligație de a avea planuri naționale pentru cloud, pentru inteligența artificială, centre de expertiză și de excelență. Din acest motiv, acest pachet este binevenit pentru că vine să stabilească niște reguli foarte clare: care este partea de suveranitate și care este partea de integrare în Uniunea Europeană; care este partea de control; care sunt persoanele și oamenii care lucrează în inteligența artificială și centrele de cloud.

Iar pentru toate statele membre, inclusiv pentru România, trebuie să existe această obligație de a avea planuri naționale pentru cloud, pentru inteligența artificială, centre de expertiză și de excelență. În același timp, mesajul trebuie să fie foarte clar: și la Galați, și la Iași, ca și la Bruxelles, suveranitatea tehnologică este extrem de importantă.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Mr President, digital sovereignty is not a technical debate: it's a question of power. The decision by the Trump administration to restrict access to advanced AI models must be a wake-up call for Europe.

Artificial intelligence is no longer just innovation: it is a strategic asset, a matter of security, competitiveness and geopolitical influence. So let us stop opposing regulation and innovation. Europe's real weakness is not its new rules, it is the old fragmentation of our markets, the lack of a true capital markets union and the unfinished single market.
If we want sovereignty, we must invest, scale and act together on AI, cloud infrastructure, digital payments, cyber security, defence and digital Europe.
Time is running out. Europe must move from dependence to sovereignty and from sovereignty to power.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, Frau Vizepräsidentin der Kommission, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Europa muss unabhängiger werden; daran besteht kein Zweifel. Wir sind abhängig von IT-Dienstleistungen und -Bauteilen von außereuropäischen Anbietern. Man denke nur zurück: 2021 hatten wir eine große Chipkrise: Bänder standen still, es gab Kurzarbeit in der Automobil- und Zulieferindustrie. Oder die jüngsten Entscheidungen aus den USA: Anthropic muss den Zugang zu seinem besten KI-Modell für alle Ausländer blockieren.
Wer abhängig ist, macht sich erpressbar, und das, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen, dürfen wir nicht hinnehmen.

Die Kommission hat ein Paket zur technologischen Souveränität Europas vorgelegt, mit einer ganzen Reihe von unterschiedlichen Maßnahmen zur Stärkung unserer europäischen Kapazitäten in den Bereichen Halbleiter, KI, Cloud und Open Source. Frau Vizepräsidentin, ich begrüße dieses Paket ausdrücklich. Über Einzelheiten müssen wir natürlich sprechen, aber es ist ein gutes Paket. Wir müssen unsere Kapazitäten aufbauen, insbesondere unsere kritische Infrastruktur, aber wir dürfen dabei nicht protektionistisch sein.

Souveränität ist wie ein Immunsystem: Ist es gesund, schützt es. Überreagiert es allerdings, dann greift es den eigenen Körper an. Wir brauchen die richtige Balance, auch angesichts der hohen Abhängigkeiten, die wir heute haben.

Und, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen: Wir schließen Freihandelsabkommen mit vielen Regionen in der Welt. Wir haben vertrauenswürdige Partner. Diese dürfen wir nicht ausgrenzen, sondern müssen sie bei unserem Aufbau auch entsprechend einbinden.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Was bedeutet digitale Souveränität? Heute kontrollieren einige wenige Konzerne, gedeckt von ihrer Regierung, was wir sehen, wie wir bezahlen, wer Zugriff auf unsere Daten hat. Menschen, ihre Daten, sind der bloße Rohstoff für die Profite großer Unternehmen.

Überwachungskapitalismus ist kein akzeptables Geschäftsmodell. Personalisierte Werbung, undurchsichtige Algorithmen, gezielte Verbreitung extremistischer Inhalte – das sind gewollte Manipulationen, die gezielt gesellschaftlichen Zusammenhalt zerstören.

Europa muss jetzt unabhängiger werden – von Chips über Plattformen, Messenger, Software bis hin zu Zahlungs- und Cloudsystemen. Ein Verbot personalisierter Werbung ist längst überfällig, ebenso die Einführung einer echten Digitalsteuer. Und bei fortdauernder Verletzung unserer Gesetze und Werte muss auch ein zumindest vorübergehender Ausschluss vom europäischen Markt greifen, als Signal für ein starkes Europa, für Vielfalt und Demokratie.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Hr. Formand! Kommissær, kolleger. Europa taler ofte om teknologisk uafhængighed, men uafhængighed, er det virkelig et mål i sig selv? Hvis uafhængighed er lig med isolation, så er intet jo vundet. Ingen moderne økonomi bliver stærk ved at lukke sig om sig selv.
Det afgørende spørgsmål er derfor ikke, hvordan Europa gør sig uafhængigt af resten af verden. Det afgørende spørgsmål er, hvordan Europa gør sig uomgængeligt for resten af verden.

Vi skal skabe virksomheder, teknologier og løsninger, som andre er afhængige af. Vi skal udvikle de chips og den kunstige intelligens og digitale infrastruktur, som verden efterspørger. For Europas udfordring er ikke, at vi er for afhængige. Udfordringen er, at for få er afhængige af os.

Derfor skal vores ambition ikke være digital isolation. Vores ambition skal være europæisk teknologisk lederskab. For et stærkt Europa er ikke et Europa, der står alene. Det er et Europa, som verden ikke kan undvære.

paragraphs.text: A Uachtaráin, whether we like it or not, AI is here to stay. AI will define our competitiveness and cybersecurity for years to come, and it would be naive to simply be AI customers.

President Trump's decision to ban Anthropic's powerful Mythos model underlines the geopolitical importance of this technology. We were punished in 2022 because of our dependency on Russian gas. If data is a new oil, we cannot allow ourselves to be punished again.
Some promote investing vast amounts of European public money in the race to build the dominant frontier AI model. Yet, this would be hugely expensive and likely futile.

Instead, we should focus on adoption in key sectors, investing in European sovereign computing power and providing a stable and welcoming regulatory and investment environment to attract and integrate the leading models on our terms.
This will give us competitiveness, cybersecurity for our critical services and resilience, limiting the danger of worst‑case scenarios. We need to be players, not customers.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear all, what do digital tools in our public services, algorithms shaping public debates and the chatbots we use every day to guide our decisions have in common? All too often they are controlled by non-European actors, and that leaves Europeans as consumers of technology rather than masters of their own digital futures.

As S&D, we support strengthening Europe's digital sovereignty and resilience, but technological prowess alone does not deliver sovereignty. True digital sovereignty means that people remain in control and that technology serves democracy and the public interest.

That is why we must defend and fully implement our digital rulebook rather than push a deregulation agenda that weakens privacy and protection. We need to invest in European innovation and skills and bring key digital infrastructure under European control.

Digital sovereignty must go hand in hand with democratic accountability, sustainability and quality jobs. It will be delivered by a skilled, fairly paid European workforce and not by precarious labour or imported and outsourced expertise.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, ce réveil est tardif, faisons en sorte qu'il soit massif. 1,5 point de PIB, c'est ce qui part chaque année depuis le privé et le public vers les services numériques américains. Plus de 250 milliards. Dans ce contexte, évidemment, les Américains ont un coup d'avance. On dit souvent que les produits européens ne sont pas à la hauteur. C'est entièrement faux et c'est insultant pour nos acteurs du numérique. La plupart du temps, quand on passe commande à des acteurs du numérique, ils n'ont pas encore le produit, mais notre commande va leur permettre de les développer.

Donc c'est de notre rôle, de notre responsabilité, pour être à la hauteur vis-à-vis des Européens, mais vis-à-vis aussi de nos talents qu'on doit protéger, de faire en sorte que la commande publique aille vers nos acteurs du numérique. Et puis pourquoi pas aussi, pour les grandes entreprises, proposer à un moment un seuil vers les acteurs du numérique européen, car il devient très dangereux aujourd'hui de travailler avec certains acteurs numériques américains. Et puis pour financer tout ça, on peut penser aussi à quelque chose qui s'appelle la taxation des géants du numérique.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, mevrouw de vicevoorzitter van de Europese Commissie, Europa is vandaag te afhankelijk van anderen voor microchips, cloud en artificiële intelligentie. Zo domineren de Amerikaanse big tech de clouddiensten waarop Europese bedrijven een beroep doen. We zien telkens hetzelfde patroon: het onderzoek gebeurt hier, de innovatie gebeurt hier, maar de economische meerwaarde verdwijnt naar elders.

Microchips zijn geen gewone producten. Ze zijn even strategisch als energie en grondstoffen. Dat hebben we geleerd tijdens de coronacrisis en leren we bij elke geopolitieke crisis opnieuw. Chips zijn vandaag na olie en voertuigen het meest verhandelde product ter wereld. De markt zal in 2026 de grens van 1 biljoen dollar overschrijden. Maar laat ons eerlijk zijn: volledige onafhankelijkheid voor Europa is een illusie en is ook niet wenselijk. De vraag is niet of we alles zelf moeten doen. De vraag is hoe we Europa onmisbaar kunnen maken in de waardeketen, competitief kunnen zijn, beschermen zonder af te schermen. Daarvoor moeten we vertrekken van onze grootste troef en dat is onderzoek en innovatie.

Europa heeft wereldspelers zoals imec, ASML. Dat is het fundament van een sterke chipsindustrie. Daarom ook een waarschuwing: het is goed dat deze chipsverordening de vraag naar chips stimuleert via datacenters, maar als die vraag wordt ingevuld door producenten buiten Europa omdat we niet competitief zijn, dan versterken we onze chipssector niet. Een sterke chipsverordening bouwt niet alleen de vraag op, maar versterkt ook de Europese innovatie en industrie. Die vraag moeten we invullen.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, Europe needs digital sovereignty. We cannot remain dependent on foreign‑owned platforms, cloud services and critical technologies while speaking about strategic autonomy. But sovereignty is not simply about building more data centres or chip factories; true sovereignty means democratic control over our digital infrastructure. It means protecting citizens' data, defending our public sphere from disinformation, and ensuring that public investment creates public value, jobs and resilience for Europe.

At the same time, we must be honest about the costs. As Europe faces record heatwaves, droughts and water shortages, citizens are asked to save water and farmers struggle to irrigate their fields. Europe's technological sovereignty cannot be built by weakening climate ambition, increasing pressure on our energy grids or competing with citizens for water, which is already happening in some Member States.
It must be sustainable and fair – where digital infrastructure, clean energy, quality jobs and climate action reinforce each other.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, Senhora Comissária, caros colegas, parece evidente, neste debate, que a soberania digital já não é apenas uma necessidade europeia, é mesmo uma urgência estratégica para a Europa.

Dependemos de plataformas que não controlamos, de infraestruturas que não possuímos e de tecnologias desenvolvidas fora da Europa; e quem depende dos outros para comunicar, para inovar ou para proteger os seus dados não é verdadeiramente soberano. Esta dependência, como já aqui foi dito esta manhã, custa‑nos milhões de EUR e coloca em risco a nossa segurança, a proteção dos nossos dados e a nossa autonomia democrática. O Grupo S&D apoia, por isso, uma estratégia europeia ambiciosa para reforçar a soberania tecnológica.

Mas sejamos todos claros neste debate: soberania não significa apenas criar novos mercados ou subsidiar grandes empresas, significa investir na capacidade europeia, proteger as infraestruturas críticas e garantir o controlo democrático sobre tecnologias que moldam a vida de milhões de cidadãos.

Para podermos avançar, é, pois, importante encontrar também os recursos próprios. Por isso, continuamos a defender, e continuo a defender, uma taxa digital, um imposto sobre os serviços digitais, que, de acordo com as contas da Comissão Europeia de 2024, rondariam por ano os 5 mil milhões de EUR.

É, no entanto, imperiosa uma taxação dos lucros das grandes empresas tecnológicas, para conseguirmos verdadeiramente construir esta nossa soberania digital. Porque tratar da nossa soberania digital é tratar da nossa democracia.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, dear Vice-President, I think many don't understand that what we saw just a couple of days ago is serious, it was the first time that the 'kill switch' was used.

If needed, the United States can switch off 90% of the world from its frontier models. And frontier models are no mere business models, they are war models and defence models, and this must be clear to everyone.

So what should we do? Number one: strategy, strategy, strategy. Giga factories: what's happening with them? Do we have special giga factories for defence purposes? How will we deal with the models that will be there at the end?

Number two: compute, compute and equity, equity. I applaud the Commission's efforts. I know about the EUR 800 billion which are planned, but where will we get them? Most of this is private money, and it should be made sure that this money will materialise.

Number three: standards, standards, standards. We don't want the backlash as we see in the United States with computer centres. Yes, we need computer centres, yes, we need more compute, but it should be sustainable.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, thank you for this very encouraging and lively debate, because you have illustrated also very well why tech sovereignty is so crucial at this time and age.

Many of you were very much underlining how important it is to build up our own capacity on AI. And I very much, of course, agree. We have also great strengths here because we have, for example, 30 % more AI engineers per capita than USA. So we have a great talent pool. Also we have 8 000 start-ups which are developing and training AI.

But one big obstacle for these companies has been that they haven't had access to computing capacity. That's why it's so important that now we are investing, together with our Member States, in 19 AI factories, and we are able to open up this computing capacity for our start-ups to train AI models in Europe. In a very short time, we will open also the official call for those gigafactories. Then we will be able to have even much more computing power.

AI factories are not only about computing power; it's also bringing together high-quality data sets to train AI and also talented people. Here I want to encourage Parliament also to proceed with our Digital Omnibus, because we have to also clarify the rules to access to data, because this is needed to train and develop AI models.

Also encouraging developments we have seen in the businesses because our AI uptake among our businesses in Europe was increasing already 50 % in last year. But still we have to work, especially with our key industrial sectors and public sector to support them also to uptake and use AI.

I want to very much assure you that the technological sovereignty package we have proposed is not only about statement of ambition, it is really a concrete action plan and the work is already ongoing.

Just a small also notice about these very capable AI models which are now coming to the markets: we are also working with a concrete list of actions also, which is needed to address the new cybersecurity threats with these new capable models.

paragraphs.text: Poštovani predsjedavajući, poštovana povjerenice, kolegice i kolege, procjene kažu da će nam trebati između pet i deset godina da dosegnemo, zapravo, ovaj zaostatak koji imamo za razvijenijim zemljama u području umjetne inteligencije.

Ja smatram da nam ne treba samo digitalna transformacija, već digitalni suverenitet koji će osigurati i da ključne tehnologije umjetne inteligencije razvijamo, međutim, da oni budu korisni i našem društvu. Jednako tako u skladu s europskim vrijednostima, ali vodeći računa i o našim interesima, o interesima naših kompanija, jer ne možemo graditi digitalnu budućnost samo na pretpostavci da će ključne tehnologije uvijek biti dostupne pod jednakim uvjetima i bez političkog rizika.

Digitalni suverenitet ne znači da Europa mora sve sama. Naprotiv, to znači da u ključnim područjima ne smijemo ostati bez vlastitih mogućnosti i jednako tako ne smijemo dopustiti više da Europa bude nečija digitalna kolonija jer to nije samo tehnološko pitanje, to je pitanje europske otpornosti, gospodarske snage i našeg suvereniteta.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señora vicepresidenta Virkkunen, la proclamada autonomía estratégica requiere autonomía tecnológica, que es la que da cobertura a esa soberanía digital que espera la iniciativa sobre una ley de chips europea, una ley de acceso a la nube que cree un balance adecuado entre competitividad y seguridad con infraestructuras tecnológicas que sean un verdadero bien público europeo.

Pero la parte más importante de todo el paquete y de las iniciativas pendientes es esa movilización de inversión de hasta 150 000 millones euros para cerrar la brecha digital que ha hecho que la Unión Europea sea enteramente dependiente de las infraestructuras tecnológicas y de inteligencia artificial, sea de Estados Unidos, sea de China.

Si queremos realmente que la Unión Europea afirme la autonomía tecnológica y la soberanía digital como un bien público europeo, esos 150 000 millones de euros son absolutamente imprescindibles para darle credibilidad y tiene que tener su reflejo en el próximo marco financiero plurianual y en los presupuestos anuales de la Unión en los próximos siete años.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, oli aika, jolloin Nokian 3310 hallitsi maailmaa. Sen kestävyys ja luotettavuus synnytti legendan, joka elää vieläkin. Sittemmin Nokian matkapuhelinliiketoiminnan kuihduttua Suomen talouden toistuvana teemana on ollut kysymys: mistä saamme uuden Nokian?

Osittain tähän kysymykseen voi löytää vastauksen, kun katsoo, mitä kysymystä lännessä nyt kysytään. Kysymys kuuluu: mistä saamme turvalliset tietoliikenneverkot? Toimittajaksi on tarjolla vakoilupelkoakin herättänyt kiinalaisjätti Huawei. Raaka-aineissa ja tuotannossa olemme antaneet avaimiamme Kiinan diktatuurille. Se on ollut suunnatonta typeryyttä.

Jos sallimme diktatuurilähtöisen verkkoyhtiönkin soluttautua tänne, se on jo hengenvaarallista typeryyttä. Onneksi meillä on myös toinen vaihtoehto: se sama 3310-puhelimen kehittänyt, uuden aikakauden suomalainen verkkoyhtiöksi kasvanut Nokia.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Madame la Vice-présidente exécutive européenne, ça y est, là Washington nous a débranchés. Depuis vendredi, le modèle IA le plus puissant d'Anthropic a été désactivé pour tous les non-Américains, au nom d'une conception floue et arbitraire de la sécurité nationale. Mais soyons honnêtes, la menace du kill switch qu'on redoutait tous est désormais réelle et, face à l'ultra-puissance des géants de la tech, le contrôle de l'État pourrait se justifier. Mais avouons que c'est assez comique, venant d'un gouvernement américain antirégulation de décider de contrôler.

Et c'est inquiétant quand la mesure est prise de façon aussi arbitraire, sans consultation et sans préavis. Et l'Europe dans tout ça? Elle regarde. Elle subit. Elle est en état de vassalisation numérique. Alors la question est simple: jusqu'à quand? Jusqu'à ce qu'on nous coupe toutes les infrastructures pour paralyser nos transports, nos hôpitaux, nos paiements? Pourtant, l'Europe a les talents, l'Europe a le marché, elle a l'argent. Ce qui nous manque, c'est la volonté politique de stopper la perfusion américaine et d'investir dans une IA européenne souveraine et éthique. Alors en 2022, j'appelais à un Buy European Tech Act. Cela faisait sourire. Aujourd'hui, tout le monde parle de préférence européenne. Allons donc plus loin sur l'union de l'épargne et de l'investissement pour booster nos pépites et nos champions avec de l'argent frais.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, Senhora Comissária Virkkunen, a humanidade precisa de mais cooperação e partilha de conhecimento científico e tecnológico para resolver problemas comuns na base do multilateralismo. Não precisa da competição, concorrência e disputa capitalista pela supremacia tecnológica.

A ciência e a tecnologia precisam de um forte suporte e enquadramento públicos e têm de ser orientadas para resolver e superar os problemas que afligem os povos, para elevar as suas condições de vida, para garantir a paz. Em sentido contrário, a entrega do desenvolvimento científico e tecnológico às multinacionais afunila e condiciona o seu aproveitamento, deixa‑o refém das lógicas dos mercados e subordinado ao objetivo de acumulação do lucro, à mercê da aplicação prioritária na indústria da guerra e da morte.

Todos os povos têm o direito soberano ao desenvolvimento científico e tecnológico. Essa é a razão para recusar que países europeus estejam reféns dos Estados Unidos da América ou que países como Portugal fiquem reféns dentro da União Europeia, da Alemanha, da França ou de qualquer outro país mais desenvolvido.

paragraphs.text: Laura Ballarín Cereza (S&D), por escritoLos socialistas españoles hemos acogido positivamente el Paquete de Soberanía Tecnológica presentado por la Comisión, al considerar que supone un paso necesario para reforzar la autonomía estratégica europea en un contexto de creciente competencia geopolítica y dependencia tecnológica. Sin embargo, consideramos que las medidas propuestas son insuficientes para reducir de manera efectiva las dependencias digitales de Europa.Durante el debate se puso de manifiesto que la UE continúa dependiendo en gran medida de infraestructuras digitales controladas desde fuera de la UE, una situación que genera vulnerabilidades económicas, tecnológicas y de seguridad. Por ello, defendimos la necesidad de complementar la gestión de riesgos con una estrategia orientada al desarrollo de capacidades europeas propias.Desde nuestra Delegación consideramos prioritario reforzar la capacidad de centros de datos europeos, indispensables para garantizar la soberanía digital. Estas infraestructuras son clave para el control de los datos, la continuidad de los servicios esenciales y la resiliencia de Europa frente a crisis o presiones externas.Asimismo, hemos expresado reservas sobre la Ley de Nube e IA, al considerar que no reduce suficientemente la dependencia de proveedores extranjeros. La autonomía tecnológica europea debe basarse en una capacidad propia sólida, al servicio de la ciudadanía y de los valores democráticos europeos.

paragraphs.text: András Gyürk (PfE), írásbanEurópa jelentős lemaradásban van a mai korban stratégiai fontossággal bíró technológiák fejlesztésében, illetve gyártásában amerikai és ázsiai versenytársaival szemben. Ezen a Bizottság közelmúltbeli, digitális ágazattal kapcsolatos kezdeményezései sem segítettek érdemben. Ugyanakkor az új, technológiai szuverenitásról szóló csomag lehetőséget jelent a hibák kijavítására és az első valódi lépések megtételére az EU digitális függetlensége felé vezető úton.Először, üdvözlendő, hogy a Bizottság a valóban fontos területeken javasol fellépést. Ilyen elem a szuverenitás erősítése a félvezetők kapcsán, melyek nélkülözhetetlen összetevői az európai versenyképességet meghatározó technológiák következő generációjának. A kereslet és az ipari felhasználás ösztönzése fontos elem lehet az importkitettség mérséklésében és erősítheti az EU részvételét ezen a bővülő piacon.Másodszor, szintén indokolt a felhőalapú szolgáltatások terén a külső kitettség csökkentése. Jelenleg az európai felhőpiac mintegy 85%-át EU-n kívüli vállalatok birtokolják. A megoldást a technológiai függetlenség és az interoperabilitás jelentheti, azonban ehhez fejlesztési forrásokra és a kiberbiztonság javítására lesz szükség.Azonban, nem szabad szem elől téveszteni, hogy minden jogalkotási javaslatnak, így a technológia szuverenitási csomagnak is a polgárokat kell szolgálnia. Ezért is elfogadhatatlanok az olyan javaslatok, melyek a háztartások áramfogyasztását korlátoznák az adatközpontok energiaigényére hivatkozva. Mi, Patrióták, nemet mondunk a társadalmi mérnökösködésre és az embereket helyezzük középpontba a csomagot kísérő jogalkotási munka során.

paragraphs.text: Romana Jerković (S&D), napisanDigitalna suverenost nije pitanje izbora, nego pitanje naše sigurnosti, konkurentnosti i demokratske otpornosti. Digitalna suverenost ne znači samo ulaganje u čipove, podatkovne centre i računalnu snagu. Ona znači sposobnost Europe da razvija vlastite tehnologije, upravlja vlastitim podacima i donosi vlastite odluke u skladu s europskim vrijednostima. Istovremeno, ne smijemo zaboraviti da tehnologiju ne grade strojevi, nego ljudi. Bez kvalificiranih radnika, kvalitetnih radnih mjesta, socijalnog dijaloga i ulaganja u vještine, nema ni uspješne digitalne tranzicije.Naš cilj zato mora biti jasan: izgraditi europski digitalni ekosustav koji je inovativan i konkurentan, ali istovremeno otvoren, demokratski i usmjeren na građane. Samo tako Europa može biti istinski digitalno suverena i otporna u svijetu koji se ubrzano mijenja.

paragraphs.text: Емил Радев (PPE), в писмена формаУважаеми колеги,В свят на остра геополитическа и технологична конкуренция Европейският съюз не може да си позволи зависимост от чужди платформи, несигурни вериги за доставки или режими, които използват данните и цифровата инфраструктура като инструмент за натиск. Критичните технологии вече определят нашата сигурност, конкурентоспособност и икономическо развитие, нашето бъдеще.За Групата на ЕНП дигиталният суверенитет е стратегическа необходимост, сравнима по значение с енергийната независимост. Но ако енергията захранва икономиката, то дигиталните системи управляват нейните процеси.Изправени пред рисковете от ускореното технологично развитие, осъзнахме нуждата от адекватна правна рамка, а сега узряваме, че регулациите сами по себе си не изграждат дигитален суверенитет. Той се създава чрез реален индустриален, изчислителен и технологичен капацитет. Нуждаем се от повече иновации и инвестиции, по-малко административна тежест и по-добри условия европейският бизнес да расте.Най-важният ресурс обаче остават хората. Технологиите са плод на знания, научна работа и предприемачество. Затова конкурентоспособността на Европа започва с качествено образование, силна научна среда и условия талантите да работят, експериментират и реализират идеите си. В крайна сметка дигиталният суверенитет зависи не просто от технологиите, а преди всичко от хората, които ги създават, контролират и задават посоката.

paragraphs.text: Marcos Ros Sempere (S&D), por escritoLos socialistas españoles hemos acogido positivamente el Paquete de Soberanía Tecnológica presentado por la Comisión, al considerar que supone un paso necesario para reforzar la autonomía estratégica de la Unión en un contexto de creciente competencia geopolítica y dependencia tecnológica. Sin embargo, consideramos que las medidas propuestas siguen siendo insuficientes para reducir de manera efectiva las dependencias digitales de Europa.Durante el debate se puso de manifiesto que la UE continúa dependiendo en gran medida de infraestructuras digitales controladas desde fuera de la UE, una situación que genera vulnerabilidades económicas, tecnológicas y de seguridad. Por ello, defendimos la necesidad de complementar la gestión de riesgos con una estrategia orientada al desarrollo de capacidades europeas propias.Desde nuestra Delegación consideramos prioritario reforzar la capacidad de los centros de datos europeos, indispensables para garantizar la soberanía digital. Estas infraestructuras son clave para el control de los datos, la continuidad de los servicios esenciales y la resiliencia de Europa frente a crisis o presiones externas.Asimismo, hemos expresado reservas sobre la Ley de Nube e IA, al considerar que no reduce suficientemente la dependencia de proveedores extranjeros. La autonomía tecnológica europea debe basarse en una capacidad propia sólida, al servicio de la ciudadanía y de los valores democráticos europeos.

interventions.speaker_label: Kaja Kallas, Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, for the past two days, there have been grounds for cautious optimism regarding the situation in the Middle East.

The announcement of the deal between the United States and Iran to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be a breakthrough. It has the potential to create space for deeper talks on other critical issues, including Iran's nuclear programme and regional stability. Once fully implemented, this agreement should also contribute to easing pressures on global energy markets.

While the details regarding the scope and timeline of the MoU are still emerging, one thing is clear: for any settlement to be sustainable, it must be fully consistent with international law and implementation must be verifiable. The Strait of Hormuz has to become open again and toll free.

I commend the mediation efforts led by Pakistan and Qatar, as well as the constructive engagement of Oman, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Egypt. Their diplomacy has been essential in preventing an all‑out war and arriving at the deal.

Honourable Members, in recent days, I have been speaking with many of my counterparts from these countries to explore how the EU can contribute to the next phase. From economic leverage and technical expertise on nuclear issues to broader diplomatic engagement, the EU stands ready to support a sustainable resolution that advances regional stability while protecting our interests and security.

It is evident, however, that the most difficult phase of this process still lies ahead. The EU rejects any measures that would impose additional costs to the maritime shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Moreover, we coordinate with partners worldwide to maintain a cohesive front against any attempt to limit freedom of navigation and weaken international law. Just last week, the Council adopted new listings targeting those involved in Iran's actions threatening freedom of navigation.

In parallel, our defensive naval operation, ASPIDES, continues to protect shipping in the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden – another key area to assert the freedom of navigation. Yemen's Houthis continue to pose a dangerous threat to shipping. This is why we now have a record number of ships on patrol in the area and we will remain vigilant.

Beyond Iran, the situation in Lebanon remains highly fragile and requires continued international attention as a comprehensive deal is implemented. The ceasefire between Lebanon and Israel must hold as it is an opportunity to end the conflict, give diplomacy a chance and create the conditions for sustainable de‑escalation. We will continue to support the Lebanese authorities, in particular in their determination to disarm Hezbollah. Civilian populations in Israel and Lebanon deserve peace and stability.

We must also maintain our full attention on the situation in Gaza and in the West Bank. Israel's latest plan to rapidly expand West Bank settlements are not in line with international law and further undermine the prospects of a two‑state solution.

Regarding the trade with illegal settlements, yesterday, at the Foreign Affairs Council, a large number of Member States called for concrete proposals from the Commission and several said that they would want to work on proposals that give clarity on different possible ways forward.

I will convey this request at the College meeting and ask the Commission to prepare, ahead of the next Foreign Affairs Council, a list of options for possible trade measures, including measures aimed at preventing imports of goods originating from illegal settlements. I will also seek the Commission's assessment on the scope of issues related to the rules of origin – another point raised by the Member States.

The EU remains steadfast in its support for the two‑state solution as the only viable path to the sustainable end of the Israeli‑Palestinian conflict, and to lasting peace and security in the Middle East. The regional normalisation is a powerful incentive and should be accompanied by progress between Israelis and Palestinians. We see no progress in the implementation of the Gaza peace plan, but the humanitarian crisis in Gaza is growing. We cannot wait longer.

That is why the EU calls for the immediate and unhindered flow of humanitarian aid into Gaza and will support early recovery as soon as conditions allow. Hamas needs to decommission its weapons and border crossings need to be reopened fully, in line with the comprehensive plan.

Dear President, honourable Members, from Gaza to Lebanon, from the Red Sea to the Strait of Hormuz, the EU will continue working with all partners to advance peace, security and prosperity for the benefit of our citizens and the people of the Middle East alike. I thank you for your support and look forward to the debate.

It has the potential to create space for deeper talks on other critical issues, including Iran's nuclear programme and regional stability. Once fully implemented, this agreement should also contribute to easing pressures on global energy markets.

While the details regarding the scope and timeline of the MoU are still emerging, one thing is clear: for any settlement to be sustainable, it must be fully consistent with international law and implementation must be verifiable. The Strait of Hormuz has to become open again and toll free.

I commend the mediation efforts led by Pakistan and Qatar, as well as the constructive engagement of Oman, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Egypt. Their diplomacy has been essential in preventing an all‑out war and arriving at the deal.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Madam Vice-President, the markets are happy, the oil industry is happy, but the supporters of the Iranian regime are the happiest.

Let me tell you – in business language that is now so fashionable – what is really happening. We are confronted with a classic 'negative business' model: I create the problem; I give you the solution. Well, I have news for you all: the problem is there and, in this case, the ceasefire is a patch; it's not the solution.

The theocratic regime in Iran is alive and kicking. In classic economic terms, this is unfinished business. Not only they survive, but they have learned how to use the Strait of Hormuz as a hostage. And now, as Internet and communications are open between Tehran and its proxies, a campaign of terrorist attacks is to be expected in Israel, the Gulf countries and, ladies and gentlemen, here in Europe.

For the mullah regime, timing was essential. They don't have mid‑term elections, they don't care about markets and they don't care about human laws. Yes, they have sustained heavy losses. But remember, the real Iranian army is not in Iran; it's with their proxies. Believe me, because I have experience in the fight against terrorism, democratic fight against terrorism in my country Spain. In the fight against terrorism you finish the job or the job will try to finish you and your democracy. There is no middle ground.

This is a wake‑up call for us Europeans, like the Russian invasion of Ukraine. To avoid what is coming to us, we must immediately coordinate our defence, intelligence and security efforts in this new Middle East scenario. We must help our allies in the region, those who understand much better than us that we are facing an existential threat: the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Jordan, Egypt, Lebanon, Israel, etc. We must maintain our sanctions against the terrorist elements of the Iranian regime – this is essential in this fight – and also reduce dramatically our dependence on fossil oil from the Middle East immediately.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PfE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, High-Representative Kaja Kallas, dear colleagues, the announced deal between the United States and Iran is being presented as a possible opening for peace and stability in the Middle East.

But Europe must not confuse an agreement with peace, and it must not confuse diplomacy with weakness. If the European Union wants to play a serious role after this deal, it must begin by naming the real obstacles to peace with political clarity.

Very important: on 5 August 1980, Yasser Arafat, leader of the PLO, made the following statement: 'Peace for us means the destruction of Israel. We are preparing for total war – a war that will last for generations. We will not rest until the day we return to our home and until we destroy Israel.'
This, ladies and gentlemen, is the root of the problem in the Middle East – it is called terrorism. It is called hatred. It is called Hamas. It is called Hezbollah. It is called Muslim Brotherhood.

Peace requires Hamas to be disarmed, Hezbollah to be declared terrorist in its entirety and disarmed and the Muslim Brotherhood to be considered as a terrorist movement. The financing of structures that live off the destruction of Israel must be cut off. Without that, no peace deal can work in the region.

So, yes, Europe should support serious efforts to reduce tensions. But support cannot mean naivety or it means conditionality, transparency and enforcement. Peace will not be born from submission to terror; peace will not be born from lies; peace will begin when Europe says – not one more euro, not one more excuse, not one more inch of legitimacy for those who live off the destruction of some countries.
That is the first step towards peace and that is Europe's duty.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the ECR Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, reports of MoU between the US and Iran are an encouraging sign. Even a rough framework is better than nothing, and we should welcome any step that reduces the risk of wider war. The devil, however, is in the details, and the arrangement with Iran alone will not automatically deliver regional stability. Israel's security cannot be treated as an afterthought in any final deal, and that works both ways. And yes, those who sabotage fragile diplomacy through reckless, unilateral action must be held accountable.

We must equally consider the Gulf states. They are not bystanders. Their cooperation will be essential to any durable order, and the European Union should invest more seriously in those partnerships to protect our shared interest in open sea lanes and regional stability. We are not watching this crisis from a distance, or at least, we have been financially bleeding from this conflict.

So yes, we need de‑escalation – a de‑escalation that protects our allies, keeps vital trade routes open and ensures that Hezbollah, Hamas and other proxies do not use diplomacy as a cover to quietly rebuild.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, dear High Representative, two weeks ago in the West Bank, Sam, a seven-month-old Palestinian baby, was shot in the face by an Israeli soldier.

He is dead and almost no one is speaking his name. Sam is dead because impunity in Israel and the occupied territories has made the lives of Palestinian children expendable. Where soldiers and settlers kill without consequences, another Sam is only a matter of time.

I wish I could stand here and tell you I am proud, but I am not. I am ashamed as a Member of Parliament that we fail to prevent and to punish these crimes. I am ashamed as a politician that there is no justice and barely a complaint raised about it. I am ashamed as a mother that a seven-month-old baby can be shot in his mother's arms. And I am ashamed as a human being that we ignore the cries for help.

Let us be courageous, let us stop looking away. We must ban trade with Israel's settlements and we must expand humanitarian aid for the more than three million Palestinians who are dependent on it in Gaza and the West Bank. We owe it to Sam.
