interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, sometimes honesty is the only way out, dear colleagues, so let's be honest.

With Iran, there is a deal that they will start negotiating a deal. The Strait of Hormuz, which was open before the war, might reopen. In return, the Iranian regime gets sanctions relief and access to frozen assets while they continue to kill their own people.

In Gaza, we have a ceasefire that is no ceasefire. In the West Bank, violent settlers are burning down what remains of the possibility of a two‑state solution. Beirut is being bombed. This is the madness you get when no one cares about international law anymore. And civilians pay the price – in Gaza, Israel, Lebanon and beyond. And Europe remains painfully divided.

Defending international law as we always have; that was Germany's bid during its campaign for the Security Council. No surprise it failed. But why not prove it now, at least in the European Council, Chancellor Merz, by applying international law, consistently, sanction Ben‑Gvir and Smotrich, stop violent settlers from profiting from privileged access to the European market, and keep the sanctions on Iran for as long as this brutal regime remains in power.
International law was not written for the times of harmony. It was written precisely for moments like this.

paragraphs.text: A Uachtaráin, yesterday EUobserver reported that as far back as 2017 the Commission's then top lawyer was very clear that the EU was legally entitled to suspend cooperation with Israel, such as Horizon Europe and Erasmus exchanges, due to Israel's violations of international law. Almost 10 years and the EU has refused to act!

We have witnessed a genocide in Gaza, the annexation of the West Bank, entrenchment of apartheid policies, racialised capital punishment, 1 000 Palestinians killed since the ceasefire and, in the first half of 2026, 88 attacks against Christians and Christian holy sites, not to mention the 1 million displaced civilians in Lebanon.

Yesterday, again, the Foreign Affairs Council took no action because of some Member States. So with all due respect to the German Government, we are tired of hearing about your sensitivities. A heinous genocide against Jewish people perpetrated by an earlier generation cannot be used to justify an Israeli genocide against Palestinians. Your obstruction is making us all complicit.

Finally, I want to raise the issue of a ban on settlement goods and services, because where is Maroš Šefčovič? Where is the proposal from the Commission based on Article 207 of the Treaties? This is the bare minimum that we should be doing. The ICJ confirmed trade with the settlements is illegal. Now we need the Trade Commissioner to turn up, do his job and ban this illegal trade!

interventions.speaker_label: Alexander Sell, im Namen der ESN-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Wir diskutieren heute wieder einmal über die Rolle der Europäischen Union im Mittleren Osten. Diese Debatte können wir uns sparen: Europa spielt keine Rolle; weder in Washington noch in Teheran interessieren die Ratschläge von Frau von der Leyen oder von Frau Kallas. Besser wäre es, wenn Sie, Frau Kallas, sich endlich den Aufgaben widmen würden, die tatsächlich in Ihrem Einflussbereich liegen.

Warum haben Sie es denn in zwei Jahren Amtszeit nicht geschafft, einmal einen europäischen Friedensplan für die Ukraine vorzulegen? Warum sind 5000 Diplomaten in Ihrem Haus nicht in der Lage, eine diplomatische Lösung für den Krieg zu finden? Weil Sie eben keinen Plan haben und niemand Sie ernst nimmt.

Sie sind eine Frühstücksdirektorin, dazu noch eine sehr teure. Über 1 Milliarde EUR kostet uns der Europäische Auswärtige Dienst im Jahr, ohne jeglichen Nutzen. Wir teilen deshalb die Meinung der französischen Regierung, wonach Ihre Behörde verzichtbar ist. Europa braucht keine Außenministerin und kein Außenministerium. Die Bürger in Deutschland und Europa werden gerade überall zum Sparen aufgefordert. Wir sollten mit gutem Beispiel vorangehen und da anfangen, wo es nicht wehtut und wo es auch niemand merkt: bei der Kommission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, thank you for your interventions.

First, on sanctions against Iran. They will remain. This is our economic leverage that we have to very carefully also take into account. Whatever is agreed otherwise, we have to make our own decisions.

Then to Mr Sánchez Amor: I have always represented the European position. It is true that, in the case of Russia, we have a unified position; in the case of Middle East, we also have a unified position on many issues like support for the two-state solution, support for humanitarian aid, that humanitarian aid should not be politicised – all these things. Also our asks to the Israeli Government. But when it comes to the trade issues, we don't still have a common position. And that is what I'm also representing.

To Mr Kohls: I absolutely agree that the fundamental issue of the Middle East is the Israeli–Palestine issue. So it is true that all these other wars are related to this. If we don't have an agreement on this or normalisation of this process, then we will have these wars over and over again.

There I also agree with what Ms Vautmans was saying about accountability. I think these peace agreements do not address two fundamental issues. One is accountability. If you don't see anybody held accountable for the injustice that has been done to your family, then you will seek revenge and retaliation and this vicious circle will just continue.
The other issue is the issue of refugees. All those people who have been driven off the West Bank – they have nowhere to go. So really this needs to be addressed as well.

To Ms Boylan: the EU is 27 Member States. It is also clear that we need to talk about our decision-making procedures, because the current world is showing us that we are not up to our task because we are not able to make decisions.

To Mr Sell: we have a European peace plan for Ukraine. It was discussed with the foreign ministers in Cyprus. It is very clear what our plan is. We are continuing also to support Ukraine and pressure Russia and the peace plan we have in order to have a long and sustainable peace so that Russia would not attack countries. But it is not the topic of this debate, really.

If you don't see anybody held accountable for the injustice that has been done to your family, then you will seek revenge and retaliation and this vicious circle will just continue.

The other issue is the issue of refugees. All those people who have been driven off the West Bank – they have nowhere to go. So really this needs to be addressed as well.

To Ms Boylan: the EU is 27 Member States. It is also clear that we need to talk about our decision-making procedures, because the current world is showing us that we are not up to our task because we are not able to make decisions.

To Mr Sell: we have a European peace plan for Ukraine. It was discussed with the foreign ministers in Cyprus. It is very clear what our plan is. We are continuing also to support Ukraine and pressure Russia and the peace plan we have in order to have a long and sustainable peace so that Russia would not attack countries. But it is not the topic of this debate, really.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, President Trump is selling us his new victory. Let's summarise it.
Iran before the war: an Ayatollah dictator in power, brutal repression of human rights, the Strait of Hormuz open, sanctions in force.
Iran after the war: another Ayatollah dictator still in power, human rights abuses still ongoing, the Strait of Hormuz reopened, sanctions weakened and high energy prices for our citizens.
Do you consider this as a victory? I do not. I consider this a loss for Iranian people and for all of us.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, is the war in Iran really about to be concluded? I'd like to share this question with you, because we don't have to fall into this trap. The agreement on the table is just a memorandum, two pages long, that agrees on a 60-day suspension. Just the right time for Trump – two months – to enter a voting campaign for mid‑term without having to deal with an unpopular war. The same 60 days will be helpful to Iran, as they already have said, to continue to pin down their process in Israel.

Is this a way to continue to defend Hezbollah and to continue to maintain this level of mixing with the Lebanon war? The main issues in this memorandum are not settled, especially the uranium in particular. At the moment, the only use of this agreement is the hope that the oil price will get down. So let's not get so excited. Iran at Trump looks very much in the sense of cynicism. The EU has different values.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidente, el acuerdo entre Washington y Teherán es un acuerdo cuyos términos todavía no conocemos. No sabemos de lo que estamos opinando realmente, pero viene, de hecho, como un alivio para el mundo —baja la gasolina, suben las bolsas—. Sin embargo, este acuerdo nunca superará el juicio de la historia si el régimen de los ayatolás no acaba cayendo y los noventa millones de iraníes no se libran del terror.

Si subsiste este régimen, aún diezmado en lo militar y económico, reforzaría su reputación antioccidental y terrorista. Occidente habría renunciado a acabar con el mayor foco de terror islamista en el mundo. Sería, sin duda, una derrota para Trump y hay mucho necio en Europa que lo celebra ya, sin saber que la derrota es también suya.

Israel sigue en guerra porque tiene que defenderse de sus enemigos. Y sus enemigos siguen allí, incluida la señora Kallas, que ha entrado en este grupo distinguido y tan masivo con esas descalificaciones intolerables que se ha permitido respecto a Israel. ¿Cómo vamos a moderar nada si somos declarados enemigos de una de las partes?

Si subsiste el régimen iraní, persiste su objetivo: el exterminio de Israel y la expansión islamista por Occidente, que la vemos todos los días en Europa, con muchos cómplices, por cierto. Esta guerra, desde luego, termine o no —puede ir a un alto el fuego, pueden ser sesenta días—, es solo un capítulo de una guerra mucho más amplia que no termina y que Europa pronto va a ver librarse en su propio territorio contra el islamismo.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, how naive can we really be?
The Iranian regime won't become a democracy through hope. It will not even stop repressing its own people through hope and the truth is that even a peace deal won't change these facts.

I'll tell you how to achieve a stable Middle East in plain language. It starts by eliminating the source whose entire existence is based on fuelling instability: the IRGC and the network of Islamist terrorist groups it funds, arms, and directs.

If we truly want a peaceful Middle East, Europe has only one real solution: isolate the Islamic regime, expel its diplomats and build a network of sanctions that will squeeze the terrorists' financial flows.
The real risk to global order was never the strikes against the regime, the real threat is the Islamic regime itself.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, High Representative, back in May at the last plenary, you and I – you might recall – had a brief exchange about the problem of the mislabelling of settlement goods. And I raised the question with you as to what the EU customs authorities could do about the fact that so many settlement goods are presented as 'made in Israel'? You replied that exports from Israel are difficult to prevent in circumstances where there is circumvention, unless we go after the suspension of trade with Israel as a whole.

What has happened since then is that Global Echo has published further evidence of widespread mislabelling of settlement goods presented at EU customs authorities as 'made in Israel': of 5 900 shipments that arrived in the EU, 17 % contained settlement goods – far in excess of what has been reported thus far.

So the question is: can we honestly deal with the question of settlement goods without first dealing with the question of the Association Agreement? The sequencing is really crucial here, and I think it's very clear that the expansion of settlements is unlawful, and we must stop supporting settlers through trade.

paragraphs.text: Fru formand! Måske er der en fredsaftale mellem USA og Iran, måske er der ikke. Vi ved det ikke. Måske er vi næsten tilbage, hvor vi var, før det alt sammen startede, blot et langt værre sted. Det er dog meget usikkert, for Israel føler sig ikke som en del af fredsaftalen, og så holder våbenhvilen ikke.
Israels fortsatte bombardementer af beboelsesejendomme i Libanon og civile vil ikke fjerne Hizbollah, og det vil med sikkerhed svække den libanesiske regering.

Israel bryder også dagligt fredsaftalen i Gaza. 1,7 millioner mennesker bor i telte mellem ruiner og affald. Sundhedstilstanden er katastrofal. Israel blokerer fortsat både nødhjælp og adgang for internationale aktører. Samtidig holder Hamas befolkningen i et jerngreb og begår overgreb. Og Israels ulovligheder på Vestbredden er på et historisk niveau.
Vi burde for mange år siden have sanktioneret Israel. Det er tid til at handle nu.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Israël a déclaré ne pas se sentir concerné par l'accord entre l'Iran et les États-Unis et poursuit ses bombardements à Gaza comme au Sud-Liban. Alors, je dois le dire, j'assiste à ce débat sans vraiment savoir à quoi il servira. Nous sommes lassés de monter à cette tribune pour entendre la même langue de bois de la part de ceux qui ne cessent d'invoquer les règles internationales qu'ils refusent pourtant de faire respecter.

Nous débattons aujourd'hui de la situation au Moyen-Orient. Qui, ici, peut encore parler d'apaisement avec un minimum de crédibilité lorsque l'Union européenne est politiquement et économiquement complice de l'État colonial et génocidaire israélien? Qui peut invoquer sérieusement la justice tout en continuant à armer Israël, en maintenant un accord d'association conditionné au respect des droits humains et à accueillir ici même les représentants d'un État qui foule aux pieds le droit international dont l'Union européenne se réclame?

Les dirigeants européens sont aujourd'hui complices et tous ceux qui se mettent à leur service ne cessent de tromper l'opinion publique et de trahir les élus que nous sommes. La vérité est pourtant limpide et elle est sous nos yeux. Il n'y aura aucun apaisement tant que vous continuerez à protéger et légitimer Israël. Et, Madame Kallas, ce n'est pas en off qu'il faut dénoncer le régime d'apartheid israélien, mais ici, à cette tribune.

paragraphs.text: Г-жо Председател, за да се стигне до мирното споразумение между Съединените щати и Иран, големи усилия положиха Китай, Пакистан и Катар. И аз се питам къде е Европейският съюз, къде е Европейската служба за външна дейност, къде са? Европейските граждани плащаме един милиард евро годишно на тази служба, а се оказва, че основната й дейност, а именно постигането на мир, я вършат държави извън Европейския съюз.

А какво прави така наречената външна министърка на Европа? О, да! Кая Калас има много по важна работа от това да работи за мир в Близкия изток. Тя мечтае за това как Русия ще се разпадне. Кая Калас и нейната служба не направиха нищо нито за постигането на мир в Украйна, нито за умиротворяването на Близкия изток. И затова вече на най-високо европейско равнище се говори за премахването на тази служба. Единственото, което прави това ведомство, е да пилее парите на европейските данъкоплатци и да работи за милитаризирането на Европа.
Мирът в Близкия изток беше постигнат пред безпомощните погледи на висшите еврочиновници. Абсолютно ненужни са както тези хора, така и техните безсмислени служби.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, God bless everybody. The louder the American empire proclaims peace in the Middle East, the more obvious it is that the war is on. And what happens is the process of normalisation of violence against Christians in the state of Israel, in the Jewish state located in Palestine.

On a daily basis, Christians, Catholic nuns, priests and even bishops are being harassed or being attacked, physically attacked, humiliated. That is regular; that is not something exceptional for the Jewish community. And this is the problem that this peace agreement – whatever it is – is not going to solve. You can solve it only by restoring the independence and security of Christians in Jerusalem and in the whole region. And the Jewish state is not going to take responsibility for it. We have to take this responsibility.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, even if the US‑Iran framework agreement is signed this Friday, the threats coming from Iran remain.
The regime in Tehran is not only cruel and lawless towards its own people, but also towards the countries in the whole region with its attacks and, of course, with its sponsoring of terrorism.

As Chair of the Delegation for relations with the Arab Peninsula, I would like to express from the European Parliament our heartfelt solidarity for the peoples of the region and full support through all possible means, including through parliamentary diplomacy.
Europe and the world cannot afford a continuation of this war, which affects all our economies. We must urge all parties to exercise maximum restraint and return to meaningful negotiations.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, the Middle East is literally burning. In recent months, ordinary people in Iran, Gaza, Lebanon and beyond have paid a devastating price for the reckless policies pursued by Netanyahu, Trump, the Iranian regime and other autocrats and oppressors.
We have now seen reports of a possible agreement between Iran and the United States. Any step that can, of course, prevent further bloodshed is good, but peace cannot mean forgetting responsibility.

The Iranian people remain hostage to a brutal regime. Palestinians continue to endure immense suffering in Gaza by Israel. Across the region, civilians are paying the price for decisions made by autocrats and extremists, and Europe cannot pretend it has been powerless.

Too often, the EU has hidden behind procedures, claiming that unanimity preventing actions, whether on suspending the EU‑Israeli Association Agreement or designating the IRGC as a terrorist organisation, when what was really missing was the political will. It is time for the EU and the Member States to wake up and take action.

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, vážené kolegyně, vážení kolegové, současná situace na Blízkém východě nám připomíná, že mír není samozřejmostí. Útoky Íránu, trvající nestabilita v Libanonu i narušení lodní dopravy v Hormuzském průlivu ukázaly, jak rychle může regionální konflikt ohrozit bezpečnost celého světa a jak velký dopad může mít na světovou ekonomiku. Právě proto vítám dohodu mezi Spojenými státy a Íránem. Ne proto, že vyřeší všechny problémy v regionu. Nevyřeší. Ale hlavně z toho důvodu, že dokázala zastavit další eskalaci konfliktu a vrátit diplomacii tam, kam patří – do centra mezinárodních vztahů. A právě zde si musíme položit nepříjemnou otázku. Pokud všichni souhlasíme s tím, že diplomacie je klíčem k míru, proč Evropská unie nehrála v těchto jednáních žádnou roli? Evropská unie sice vyzývala k míru, k stabilitě a otevření Hormuzského průlivu, ale ve chvíli, kdy bylo třeba jednat, vyjednávali jiní. A to není problém pouze této krize na Blízkém východě.

Příliš často vrcholní představitelé pouze reagují na dané události místo toho, aby je formovali. I Evropský parlament každý měsíc během plenárních zasedání přijímá několik rezolucí, zatímco skutečná jednání probíhají jinde, a to bez přispění Evropské unie. S oblibou kritizujeme světové lídry v čele s americkým prezidentem Donaldem Trumpem, ale sami nenabízíme žádná řešení. Blízký východ nám dnes nastavuje zrcadlo. Ukazuje nám rozdíl mezi politikou, která jen komentuje dění kolem sebe, a politikou, která může měnit svět. Hodnoty jsou sice důležité, ale samy o sobě rakety nezastaví. Neotevřou ani obchodní cesty, ani nepřivedou znepřátelené strany k jednacímu stolu. Pokud chce být Evropská unie skutečně globálním hráčem, musí být přítomna nejen při oslavách dohod, ale také při jejich vyjednávání.

paragraphs.text: On 28 February, the US began Operation Epic Fury and the goals were clear, as you have mentioned: to isolate Iran, prevent nuclear weapon proliferation and free the people.

From blaming NATO to Vice President Vance yesterday admitting granting EUR 300 billion to Iran if they signed to long term agreements – the same they already had under Obama's JCPOA – Epic Fury became epic failure: 7 000 killed, gas prices peaked and the people of Iran are still under dictatorship.
Can you at least please agree that making America great means making the world terrible?

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signora Vicepresidente, la giornata di oggi penso debba essere salutata positivamente, perché la sottoscrizione di un accordo tra gli Stati Uniti e l'Iran fa gli interessi del mondo, ma fa anche gli interessi dell'Occidente.

Però non penso che noi possiamo lasciare il dibattito di oggi senza una riflessione che riguarda noi. Alcuni colleghi sembrano incerti sul posizionamento che deve avere l'Unione europea. L'Unione europea sta con l'Occidente, e quindi deve lavorare per unire il rapporto tra le due sponde dell'Atlantico, non deve essere felice se questo rapporto si divide.
L'Unione europea, con i suoi Stati membri, è un partner fondamentale dell'Alleanza atlantica. Anche questo va ricordato come obiettivo che deve essere sempre perseguito.

Ma la crisi del Medio Oriente ci segnala un'urgenza, signora Vicepresidente, che è il fronte Sud. L'Europa ha fatto moltissimo a Est: penso alla crisi ucraina e alla volontà che quella guerra di aggressione finisca. Ma c'è un fronte del Sud, che ha al centro il Mediterraneo, nel quale noi vogliamo un'Europa molto più protagonista di ciò che è oggi.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, peace requires courage, peace requires leadership, and peace requires actions. The deal between the US and the regime in Iran might offer an opportunity for peace. But opportunities alone do not create peace; we have to act now.

We have to use our diplomatic influence to reduce the tensions throughout the entire region of the Middle East. We have to use our economic and political leverage to pressure and to support peace, accountability and human rights. And we have to defend international law – always!

Madam Vice‑President, I am tired of watching old men destroy the international rules‑based order. I am furious that they start wars, uphold occupation, weaponise humanitarian aid, while they enjoy wealth, while they enjoy impunity, while they enjoy power. I am furious that it is always the others who are paying the price for this craziness. It's always women, children, persons with disabilities, who never chose these wars, who never were in these rooms where these decisions were made. We have to act now. It's high time for the EU to put these words into actions.

paragraphs.text: A very good question. Thank you for this question. I do believe that the EU and the Member States together in the UN can push further for the reform of the UN, because the UN has not served everyone equally.

We see it in the Global South, the global majority in the South, how they have been underserved, how their interests, their human rights have not been implemented nor have they been guaranteed by all these beautiful declarations. We know that statements, press releases and declarations do not stop bombs from falling. We know that they do not feed the starving children.
We need to reform the UN. It is our only path forward, and the Member States together can actually make a true difference.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Vice-présidente, parfois, il faut savoir dire les choses clairement. Et la vérité, c'est que le président américain est dos au mur. Alors il peut crier à la victoire diplomatique, tordre la réalité, personne n'est dupe. Au mieux, son accord de paix nous ramène onze années en arrière, avec des frais de péage du détroit d'Ormuz en prime. Tout ça pour quoi? Des milliers de morts, des destructions massives, une économie mondiale prise en otage. C'est un non-sens absolu. Un accord flou que l'Europe doit cependant soutenir, car Israël entend déjà le piétiner.

Et que fait-elle exactement pour stopper la fuite en avant guerrière d'Israël? L'Europe est incapable de sanctionner les génocides à Gaza et l'occupation de la Cisjordanie et du Liban, incapable de sanctionner un ministre suprémaciste, incapable de bloquer les produits des colonies sur son marché, incapable d'arrêter les livraisons d'armes, incapable d'arrêter les crimes de guerre sur son territoire. L’histoire regarde. Elle retiendra la lâcheté de nos institutions et de nos gouvernements.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Haute-représentante, chers collègues, nous vivons quand même un moment exceptionnel: c’est que les deux armées peut-être les plus puissantes au monde, l’armée américaine et l’armée israélienne, n’ont pas réussi à venir à bout de l’Iran, qui a résisté à une attaque illégale et qui a imposé maintenant des négociations, ce qui donne une opportunité de paix au Moyen-Orient.

D’ailleurs, que la droite ici pleurniche pour cela, cela me choque, parce que cela peut donner une opportunité de vie, de bonne qualité de vie, aux gens, aux peuples du Moyen-Orient. C’est positif. Et qui veut saboter cela? C’est l’État génocidaire israélien, qui dit ouvertement: «Écoutez, nous, on voudrait que la guerre continue. Nous, on a envahi la Syrie, on va rester là; on a envahi le Liban, on va rester là; on est en train de nettoyer ethniquement la Cisjordanie, la Palestine, on va continuer de le faire – rien à faire!»

Pourquoi est-ce qu’on laisse faire? Nous pouvons les arrêter. Nous avons le pouvoir d’arrêter Israël en sanctionnant, en disant: «Nous arrêtons le commerce avec vous, vous n’aurez plus les privilèges, vous n’aurez plus ni les armes, ni l’argent des Européens.» Si vous faites cela demain, le Moyen-Orient, effectivement, sera un endroit meilleur.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, Frau Vizepräsidentin! Ich frage mich, was wir mit dieser Debatte im Europäischen Parlament überhaupt erreichen wollen. Die EU spielt doch international keine Rolle. Sie hat keine Glaubwürdigkeit und schon gar nicht im Mittleren Osten. Einst wollten Sie, Frau Kallas, mit den arabischen Golfstaaten gegen den Iran und den verbündeten Russland in den Kampf ziehen. Heute reisen alle Golfstaaten, einschließlich Saudi-Arabien, zum Wirtschaftsforum nach Russland in Sankt Petersburg. Saudi-Arabien war sogar Ehrengast bei dieser Veranstaltung.

Und während ein Donald Trump nach vier Monaten Krieg eine Einigung mit dem Iran erreicht, redet die EU nach viereinhalb Jahren Krieg in der Ukraine immer noch nicht mit Russland. Ein deutscher Luftwaffengeneral phantasiert sogar, Luftangriffe auf Kaliningrad, der Kola-Halbinsel und der Krim durchzuführen, womit er mit Sicherheit einen Nuklearkrieg auslösen würde.
Wir brauchen keine EU-Intervention im Persischen Golf, wir brauchen endlich Frieden in Europa. Es ist Zeit umzudenken, und auch dieses Parlament sollte umdenken.

paragraphs.text: W obliczu eskalacji konfliktu na Bliskim Wschodzie konieczna jest skuteczna dyplomacja międzynarodowa, zwłaszcza dyplomacja Unii Europejskiej. Kilka dni temu w ONZ (3 czerwca) odbyło się głosowanie, w którym Niemcy w sposób dramatyczny przegrały wyścig do bycia stałym członkiem Rady Bezpieczeństwa ONZ. Przegrały w nim z Austrią i z Portugalią. Serdecznie gratuluję posłom z tych krajów, że Austria i Portugalia będą reprezentowały Unię Europejską w Radzie Bezpieczeństwa ONZ.

Mam zatem pytanie, czy ten dramatyczny wynik, ta dramatyczna porażka Niemiec (104 głosy w sytuacji, gdy Austria dostała ponad 130 głosów) nie jest wynikiem braku zaufania do dominującego kraju Unii Europejskiej – Niemiec, które od lat prowadzą politykę zagraniczną Unii Europejskiej na manowce. Jak pan ocenia politykę zagraniczną Niemiec, które mają decydujący wpływ na politykę Unii Europejskiej?

paragraphs.text: A Uachtaráin, let's firstly get the facts straight. A peace deal has not been achieved between the US and Iran. There is a memorandum of understanding, a framework for negotiations, and difficult negotiations lie ahead.

Despite President Trump's words regarding what has been going on in Iran since the war began, one thing is clear: it is a different Iran, but not necessarily a better one. While the contents of this memorandum are not yet known to us, we can still say with some degree of certainty that Trump's announcement to 'let the oil flow' shows a narrow focus on energy markets.

But the effects of this conflict have been more far-reaching than just increased prices at the fuel pumps. Israel has used the war to occupy more of Lebanon and has declared its intention not to withdraw. The nightmare is not over for the people of Lebanon, so the EU must work to halt Israeli expansion in the region through the annexation of Lebanese territory.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, I stand here today with a deep sense of sadness – sadness of having to gather to celebrate the end of a world that should have never begun.

The unilateral and illegal attacks carried out by the United States and Israel that, by the way, you never condemn, have not brought democracy to Iran, and at the contrary, unfortunately, are reinforcing the regime of the ayatollahs. This war has undermined the global rules‑based order, shaken our markets and cost the lives of thousands of innocent people.

We cannot only care about war when oil prices rise. This deal does not bring back the more than 3 000 Iranians who have lost their lives. It doesn't put an end to Netanyahu's annexations of Gaza and the West Bank. It doesn't end the climate of fear and terror in Lebanon. It doesn't disarm disarming Hezbollah and does not end the occupation by Israel of southern Lebanon. It doesn't return to their homes the one million Lebanese who have been displaced.

High Representative, people are crying out to the EU for action, justice and empathy. It starts by developing the Middle East strategy that you told us would begin the moment the war ended. We need you to count with this Parliament, and to carry on international law as your banner.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Haute représentante, toute désescalade militaire est une bonne nouvelle: pour les populations civiles, d’abord; pour nos économies, ensuite, qui subissent déjà les conséquences de l’instabilité régionale sur le commerce, les transports et les prix de l’énergie. Cependant, ne nous trompons pas de diagnostic, car une désescalade n’est pas la paix.

Comment croire à une paix durable lorsque les causes profondes du conflit demeurent intactes? La première menace pour la paix régionale s’appelle le régime iranien: un régime qui oppresse son peuple, finance le Hamas et le Hezbollah, menace Israël et déstabilise l’ensemble du Proche-Orient. La première menace pour la stabilité du Liban s’appelle le Hezbollah: depuis des décennies, cette milice confisque la souveraineté libanaise et condamne le peuple libanais, notamment les chrétiens d’Orient, à l’instabilité permanente. La première menace pour la sécurité maritime mondiale s’appelle le risque de fermeture du détroit d’Ormuz: une telle situation provoquerait une nouvelle explosion des prix de l’énergie, au détriment des peuples européens.

Pendant ce temps, à Paris, Mme Kallas, Jean-Noël Barrot et plusieurs responsables européens célébraient le premier anniversaire de l’Appel de Paris et s’engageaient dans l’après, alors même que le présent demeure instable. Car, oui, on célèbre un anniversaire, mais qu’a-t-on réglé en un an? Le Hamas est toujours là; le Hezbollah est toujours là; le régime iranien poursuit sa politique de déstabilisation; les chrétiens du Liban continuent de vivre sous la menace; et les tensions continuent de peser sur la sécurité énergétique mondiale.

L’Union européenne célèbre un an de déclaration, tandis que les causes profondes du conflit demeurent intactes – pis encore, certains responsables européens semblent davantage préoccupés par les condamnations symboliques que par la désignation des véritables responsables de l’instabilité régionale. À force d’incantations diplomatiques, elle donne parfois le sentiment de confondre communication et stratégie. À écouter certains responsables européens, il suffirait de répéter «solution à deux États» pour faire disparaître le régime de Téhéran, les arsenaux du Hezbollah et le terrorisme du Hamas.

La diplomatie de l’Union européenne n’est pas une formule magique. La paix exige d’abord de traiter les causes de l’instabilité régionale. À force de vouloir commenter les conséquences, elle finit par oublier les causes. Affaiblir les fauteurs de guerre, combattre le terrorisme islamiste, redire le droit des Israéliens et des Européens à la sécurité, garantir la liberté de navigation et restaurer la pleine souveraineté du Liban: voilà les conditions d’une paix véritable. Voilà ce que devrait être votre boussole dans ce monde qui s’embrase.

paragraphs.text: Κυρία Πρόεδρε, στη Μέση Ανατολή και την ευρύτερη περιοχή υπάρχουν σήμερα δύο εκ διαμέτρου αντίθετες πορείες. Από τη μία πλευρά οι δυνάμεις της αστάθειας, του φανατισμού και της βίας, από την άλλη οι δυνάμεις της συνεργασίας, της ασφάλειας και της ανάπτυξης. Υπάρχουν τα ακραία ισλαμικά καθεστώτα, που σε συνεργασία με διάφορες τρομοκρατικές ισλαμικές οργανώσεις προκαλούν το χάος. Υπάρχει όμως και η Κυπριακή Δημοκρατία, μέλος της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης, που αποτελεί το κλειδί στην περιοχή, τη διέξοδο από το χάος.

Μέσα από κάθε κρίση δημιουργούνται και ευκαιρίες. Μία από αυτές είναι το σχήμα συνεργασίας 3+1 μεταξύ της Ελλάδας, της Κύπρου και του Ισραήλ, με τη συμμετοχή των Ηνωμένων Πολιτειών Αμερικής. Μία συνεργασία που δημιουργήθηκε με στόχο την ενίσχυση της σταθερότητας και την ασφάλεια της συνεργασίας στην περιοχή της Ανατολικής Μεσογείου, ιδιαίτερα στους τομείς της ενέργειας, του φυσικού αερίου, της άμυνας και της οικονομίας.
Σε μία εποχή γεωπολιτικών αλλαγών, η θωράκιση της Κυπριακής Δημοκρατίας αποτελεί στρατηγική αναγκαιότητα για την Ευρώπη και τον δυτικό πολιτισμό.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, High‑Representative, Trump and Netanyahu claim that the strikes on Iran, Lebanon and Palestine would deliver security. Instead, an entire region is in flames. None of the ceasefires so far have held and civilians across the Middle East are paying the highest price, so no wonder everybody is a bit sceptical.

And now, the war is spilling into Lebanon: Beirut is under fire, more than a million people have been displaced, hospitals have been destroyed, children killed. Fighting terrorism certainly does not look like this. Lebanon, therefore, must not become a second Gaza.
There are talks of a lasting peace, but can these men that are gambling with the security of the entire world be trusted? We will believe it only when the bombs will stop falling.
Because if these talks fall apart, Europe can no longer be complicit. We must finally mobilise all the tools at our disposal, including the suspension of the Association Agreement with Israel.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señorías, ¿qué celebra Europa? Porque Irán está celebrando que ha ganado y Donald Trump, como no puede celebrar que ha ganado, celebra su 80 cumpleaños montándose su propio «imperio romano», poniendo a sus gladiadores a romperse la cara como se la han roto a Topuria.

¿Qué celebra Europa? ¿Podemos celebrar que hemos impedido un genocidio, que hemos parado una agresión ilegal de los Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán? ¿Podemos celebrar que hemos roto relaciones con Israel, que hemos parado la ocupación del Líbano? No, no podemos celebrar nada de eso. Entonces, ¿qué puede celebrar Europa? ¿Qué celebra usted, señora Kallas? ¿Celebra el cumpleaños de Donald Trump? Entonces, vamos a cantarle: Happy birthday to Trump, happy birthday to Trump, happy birthday, Mr Genocide.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, wie tankt bij de pomp merkt het en aan de kassa voelen we het ook: hoge prijzen vanwege de crisis in het Midden-Oosten. Het aangekondigde staakt-het-vuren maakt hier geen einde aan. De situatie blijft kwetsbaar. Als EU kunnen we niet aan de kant blijven staan. De gevolgen zijn vele malen groter dan enkel onze prijzen aan de kassa.

We moeten leren van deze situatie en we moeten een stoel aan de onderhandelingstafel opeisen. Dat kan alleen als we samen bouwen aan onze weerbaarheid, investeren in onze veiligheid en daadkrachtig buitenlandpolitiek voeren. Zonder deze stappen geven we onze veiligheid en welvaart aan anderen. Dat is een risico dat we ons niet kunnen veroorloven.

Οι επιθέσεις στο Ιράν όχι μόνο δεν έφεραν τα επιθυμητά αποτελέσματα για τον πρόεδρο Trump, αλλά αντίθετα αποσταθεροποίησαν την ευρύτερη περιοχή, την παγκόσμια οικονομία και ισχυροποίησαν το ιρανικό καθεστώς. Οι ισραηλινές επιθέσεις στον Λίβανο αποσταθεροποιούν την κυβέρνησή του, ενώ η ανεξέλεγκτη βία από εποίκους στη Δυτική Όχθη υπονομεύει κάθε προσπάθεια λύσης.

Παρόλ' αυτά, η Ευρώπη παραμένει απούσα, με το Συμβούλιο Υπουργών Εξωτερικών για μια ακόμη φορά να μην μπορεί να συμφωνήσει ακόμα και στα πιο απλά. Αυτό δεν μπορεί να γίνει άλλο αποδεκτό. Χρειαζόμαστε μια Ευρώπη με ισχυρή φωνή στην περιοχή, που θα ενισχύσει την κυβέρνηση του Λιβάνου, δίνοντας νέα ελπίδα στην περιοχή, που θα έχει το θάρρος να υπερασπιστεί το διεθνές δίκαιο απέναντι στις παραβιάσεις της ακροδεξιάς κυβέρνησης Netanyahu και που θα ενισχύσει τις προσπάθειες των Ιρανών για ένα καλύτερο μέλλον.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, we, the Europeans, are paying the cost of the war, and thus any de-escalation may provide a short-term relief.

However, the Iran war has demonstrated two key things. First, the US is no more willing to play a role of the power which is solely responsible for freedom of navigation. Secondly, Europeans' defence capabilities are insufficient to engage in any sort of serious military conflict or even to assist our allies in a reliable way.

Let us put it bluntly: Iran is Europe's 'the emperor has no clothes' moment. So instead of empty talks, our priority should be a rapid build-up of deterrence and also enhance our capabilities to take responsibilities of freedom of foreign trade in cooperation with the US, not against the US.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Die Geschichte des Nahen Ostens ist voll von imperialistischen Interventionen und Machtspielen, deren Resultat Massenmord und Leid der Völker war. So auch jetzt: Erst wird der Iran bombardiert, dann wird ein Deal geschlossen. Erst wird die Region an den Rand eines Flächenbrandes gebracht, und dann feiern sich die Brandstifter als Feuerwehr. Zurück bleiben Zerstörung, Angst und ein gestärktes Regime in Teheran. Den Preis zahlen nicht die Brandstifter, sondern arbeitende Frauen, Jugendliche, all jene, die für Freiheit und soziale Rechte kämpfen.

Und die EU? Mal wieder auf der falschen Seite der Geschichte. Schweigt, wenn das Völkerrecht gebrochen wird. Sie liefert Waffen, stellt Kriegsinfrastruktur bereit und nennt das Verantwortung. Und jetzt soll die nächste Militärmission an der Straße von Hormus vorbereitet werden.

Doch der Nahe Osten braucht keine neuen Bomben, keine weiteren Militärboote, keine geopolitischen Machtspiele. Die Menschen brauchen Frieden, soziale Sicherheit und das Recht auf eine selbstbestimmte Zukunft, frei von imperialistischen Interventionen.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, High‑Representative, on a day when the European Parliament is voting on the final breakthrough for the implementation of the temporary agreement with the United States, we have good news coming from the diplomatic breakthrough in the US and Iran's deal announcement.

We look with hope towards the full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, restoring the free flow of goods and energy supplies that are vital for global economic stability. It is needless to repeat from this House how much preventive diplomacy was needed and how many of the costs we are facing today could have been avoided. Food security, energy security and economic stability were all at stake in this game of war.

Any final agreement with Iran must guarantee that nuclear weapons can never be acquired by authoritarian regimes and that their support for proxy actors responsible for violence and destabilisation across the region is brought to a definitive end.

We must focus on achieving lasting peace in Lebanon, the only remaining multi‑confessional country in the Middle East and the victim of proxy conflicts that Iran sought to wage. Lasting stability requires a sovereign and secure Lebanon, and the full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, il tanto agognato accordo tra gli Stati Uniti e Iran sembra finalmente arrivare. La speranza è che da venerdì si possa aprire una nuova fase di pace e stabilità, dopo mesi di guerra le cui prime vittime sono stati i civili e l'economia europea. Ma quanto durerà? Perché, se una delle condizioni è la fine delle ostilità in Libano, realisticamente rischia di durare molto molto poco.

Anche ieri Israele ha bombardato, rischiando di buttare all'aria tutti gli sforzi diplomatici. La parte più estrema, infatti, continua a forzare la situazione in modo vergognoso, continuando a scegliere la via della forza, dopo più di quattromila morti e un milione e mezzo di sfollati. E, nel frattempo, Netanyahu ieri ha annunciato che non ha intenzione di fermarsi.

Basta! Diciamolo in modo trasversale, da destra a sinistra, senza divisioni. Perché non può esserci pace se il Libano continua a bruciare. E se il cedro del Libano non si spezzerà, questo dipenderà anche da quanto l'Europa saprà recuperare la propria centralità diplomatica nel Mediterraneo e in Medio Oriente.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Haute représentante, l’accord trouvé entre les États-Unis et l’Iran pourra faire taire les armes, mais il ne désarmera pas les menaces. La présidente de la Commission a affirmé hier que l’Europe était prête à apporter sa pierre à l’édifice – c’est aimable… Nous arrivons pour poser la dernière pierre d’un édifice dont nous n’avons pas bâti un seul mur.

La réouverture du détroit d’Ormuz est indispensable, mais l’Union compte-t-elle peser sur ces conditions? Que ferons-nous si Téhéran taxe l’Europe au péage, ménage Washington et nous fait payer aux deux guichets? Quelles garanties avons-nous sur le nucléaire? Quelles garanties sur le financement du terrorisme? Quelles garanties sur la sécurité de nos alliés régionaux? Quelles garanties sur le sort d’un peuple iranien opprimé?

Nous sommes un marché que chacun convoite et une voix que plus personne ne redoute. Le mot crise, autrefois réservé à l’exceptionnel, désigne désormais notre horizon permanent. Car l’Europe s’efface des décisions, puis en absorbe le coût. Les carburants flambent, les engrais flambent, nos entreprises, nos agriculteurs et nos populations encaissent, sans fin. Alors, Madame la Haute représentante, combien de fois entrerons-nous encore en scène après la chute du rideau?

paragraphs.text: Madam President, I thank you, colleagues, for this round of debate. I will just address some of the issues.

MEP Montero, I'm glad you're here: we are not celebrating anything. Like I said in my speech as well, the 60 days that lie ahead is actually the more difficult time to address all these nuclear and other issues in the region, so we are definitely not celebrating. Like I said, we are cautiously optimistic, but we have seen that these ceasefires also don't hold, so we are worried, of course.

MEP Andrews: regarding the labelling or mislabelling of settlement goods, we had the discussion with the foreign ministers yesterday. Of course, I'm not the trade expert, but the agreement was that the Commission should come up with the proposal so that Member States can also discuss them.

About the EU not being seen in the Middle East: we have been constantly engaged with the regional actors, and they are also interested in us being part of the security architecture of the Middle East, because clearly this is balancing also the situation there. And the EU coordinated the consular response to get people out of the region. We have done a lot, but yes, maybe it's not as visible as what some other parties have been doing.

Somebody mentioned that they met with the young people from Palestine and Israel. I also met them in the two-state conference that we had in Paris on Friday and what they were really stressing there, as MEP Demirel was saying, was that people need peace. This is what they are saying. I mean, they might have a different past, but they have a common future, and the issue is how to make it.

I totally agree with those who say that the people who decided to start the war don't really pay the price. I mean, it's paid by regular people on the ground who lose their lives and who lose their homes. And then the issue of refugees comes in place: if you have nowhere to go, then it comes to us.
On Lebanon, we actually have a common stance. We are supporting the Lebanese Armed Forces.
I am over my time, so I can't answer all of these questions, but I say that these are difficult times and we try to do what we can.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, vielen Dank auch dafür, dass Sie sich immer wieder mit meinem eigenen unverhältnismäßigen Mitteilungsbedürfnis auseinandersetzen. Liebe Menschen Europas! Ich möchte dem Kollegen Kelly recht geben, der gesagt hat: Wir müssen uns hier die Fakten anschauen. Und die Fakten sagen, dass das eben noch kein Frieden ist, dass das eine bloße Absichtserklärung zu einem Frieden ist, die wesentliche Punkte, wie etwa den Frieden im Libanon oder das iranische Atomprogramm, außer Acht lässt. Es ist wirklich ein großes Fragezeichen, ob da am Ende eine Einigung zustande kommen wird oder nur eine weitere Runde des Krieges.

Wenn uns das alles etwas zeigt, dann, dass jene recht haben, die die schwache Rolle Europas in diesem ganzen Zusammenhang beklagen. Wir müssen uns als Europäische Union dafür einsetzen, das System des internationalen Rechts, der internationalen Sicherheit zu reformieren und gerade den UN-Sicherheitsrat entweder vollständig neu aufzustellen oder abzuschaffen.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señora Kallas, en política internacional no vence quien bombardea más, sino quien logra sus objetivos.

En el acuerdo entre los Estados Unidos e Irán hay dos grandes derrotados: Israel y Europa. Israel, porque no ha logrado ninguno de sus objetivos. El régimen de los ayatolás se ha reforzado y lo que han logrado los Estados Unidos es menos de lo que estaba dispuesto a dar antes Teherán. Por eso intenta sabotear el acuerdo en el Líbano.

Europa ha perdido porque ha demostrado su irrelevancia, porque ha perdido su autonomía y se ha supeditado a los Estados Unidos. Ha padecido las consecuencias de la guerra en inestabilidad, en inflación, en peor relación con el mundo árabe, con el Sur Global. Y, a diferencia del pasado, cuando sí tenía iniciativa internacional y logró el acuerdo nuclear de 2025, ahora ha desaparecido, no ha estado en las mesas de negociación, Trump ni nos ha llamado.

Tendríamos que seguir el camino del Gobierno de España: apostar por diplomacia, Derecho internacional y desescalada y no por la irrelevancia a la que nos ha llevado la Unión Europea dominada por las derechas.

Pour être crédible, la position de l'Union européenne sur le droit international doit être cohérente, pas à géométrie variable. Mane nustebino Vytenis Andriukaitis, mano kolega, kurį dažnai remiu. Trumpas ir Izraelio premjeras yra personos non grata. Tuo tarpu pagal jį, taip suprasti, Izraelio režimas ir atominio ginklo gamyba – sveikintini. Vien tik Iranas, išvaręs iš savo krašto 7 mln. gyventojų, persekioja kitaminčius, karia žmones. Ką jūs pritariate režimui? Ar jūs norite, kad Iranas sukurtų atominį ginklą? Bet aš noriu pasakyti esminį dalyką: Europa, tu nevaidinti jokios geopolitinės įtakos pasaulyje, ir taikoje taip pat. Dėl taikos pagrindinį vaidmenį atlieka Pakistanas, o ne Europa. Europa kalbasi tik su savimi.

paragraphs.text: Κυρία Πρόεδρε, με τον υποκριτικό τίτλο για «Αποκλιμάκωση στη Μέση Ανατολή», η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση επιχειρεί να κρύψει την πορεία κλιμάκωσης του πολέμου —παρά τους εύθραυστους, προσωρινούς συμβιβασμούς— όπως και τις βαρβαρότητες των συμμάχων της: τη συνεχιζόμενη γενοκτονία του Ισραήλ σε βάρος του παλαιστινιακού λαού, τις ωμότητες εναντίον του λαού του Λιβάνου που μετρά 3 800 νεκρούς, τον βρώμικο πόλεμο ΗΠΑ–Ισραήλ εναντίον του Ιράν, καθώς και τις συνέπειές του για τα εργατικά λαϊκά στρώματα, όπως είναι η περαιτέρω εκτίναξη της ακρίβειας.

Η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση είναι συνένοχη για την πολεμική οικονομία και την προετοιμασία. Με γνώμονα τα συμφέροντα των ομίλων, ενισχύει τις οικονομικές, τις πολιτικές και τις στρατιωτικές σχέσεις με το ισραηλινό κράτος και υιοθετεί τα απαράδεκτα προσχήματα των Ηνωμένων Πολιτειών και του Ισραήλ για τον πόλεμο στο Ιράν. Με τις τοποθετήσεις της, ανάβει το πράσινο φως σε αμερικανική επίθεση στην Κούβα.

Ο ιμπεριαλιστικός πόλεμος, όπως και η δήθεν ειρήνευση με το πιστόλι στον κρόταφο των λαών, είναι όψεις του ίδιου νομίσματος. Η μόνη διέξοδος είναι η πάλη των λαών κόντρα σε κάθε ιμπεριαλιστική συμμαχία, όπως είναι η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση και το ΝΑΤΟ, που αποδεικνύεται καθημερινά ότι δεν είναι άτρωτη.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señora Kallas, el imperialismo mata y lo pagamos los pueblos.

Como alta representante de la Unión para Asuntos Exteriores y Política de Seguridad, usted ha dicho que Israel tiene que rendir cuentas. Efectivamente, tiene que rendir cuentas por cometer un genocidio, por ser un país ocupante de Palestina, por practicar el apartheid.

Por cierto, nos gustaría que, además de decirlo en privado, lo diga en público. Señora Kallas, la Unión Europea tiene que dejar de amparar a Israel. El mismo Israel que quiere romper este tímido alto el fuego, el mismo Israel que ha practicado una ley —que es la ley recientemente aprobada en la Knéset— que pretende asesinar a muchas personas y encarcelarlas simplemente por ejercer su libertad. Esto no es un proceso de paz, como usted ha afirmado. De Cisjordania a Gaza, la situación en Palestina es cada vez peor y la situación en Palestina, si no se arregla ahora, será una vergüenza para la Unión Europea y para la humanidad.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária Kaja Kallas, é verdade que os Estados Unidos e Israel não alcançaram nenhum dos objetivos que utilizaram como pretexto para lançar a agressão ao Irão, mas os povos estão a pagar as consequências dessa agressão, não apenas no Médio Oriente, mas em todo o mundo. A União Europeia mantém a posição de submissão aos Estados Unidos, repetindo este discurso de faz de conta que já referi na intervenção anterior.

O problema, Senhora Comissária Kaka Kallas, é que, enquanto a União Europeia faz de conta, há pessoas a morrer no Irão, há uma nova ocupação no Líbano por parte de Israel, com milhares de mortos e feridos e mais de 1 milhão de deslocados. Há a intensificação das perseguições, dos assassinatos, das ocupações ilegais, terras por colonos israelitas na Cisjordânia, há um genocídio que prossegue em Gaza, há povos a pagar os custos da agressão ao Irão, com o aumento dos preços da energia e dos combustíveis e agora também com o aumento das taxas de juro decidido pelo Banco Central Europeu.

A pergunta que se faz é a seguinte: quando adotará a União Europeia uma posição que condene essa agressão dos Estados Unidos e ponha fim à política genocida de Israel, garantindo o cumprimento e o respeito pelos direitos nacionais do povo palestiniano?

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Es ist interessant, wie schwer es diesem Haus fällt, über das Abkommen, das am Freitag zu erwarten ist, positiv zu sprechen; denn am Ende, egal wie man dazu steht, ist es ein Weg Richtung Frieden. Ich sage Ihnen auch, warum es Ihnen so schwerfällt, positiv darüber zu sprechen: Wir müssen uns nämlich fragen, welchen Einfluss wir darauf gehabt haben.
Welchen Einfluss haben die Protagonisten der EU auf diese Prozesse gehabt? Null. Kein Einfluss auf die Vereinigten Staaten, kein Einfluss auf den Iran, kein Einfluss auf niemanden.
Am Ende muss die Erkenntnis stehen, dass wir hier eine große Debatte führen, aber die EU am Ende auf der internationalen Bühne keinen Einfluss hat. Sie ist kein Partner, mit dem irgendwer rechnet.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, let's summarise the facts: it is the United States who is starting wars and brewing mischief in the Middle East, from the Iraq War started under false pretences to the Iran war started by Netanyahu and Trump.

It is Israel and the United States who commit genocide and war crimes in Gaza, in Lebanon, in Iran. It is Europe who is paying the price with increased costs of oil, gas and fertilisers. And it is Europe who is suffering from migration waves from these conflicts.

My question, Madam High Representative, should we now reward the Israelis with continued cooperation and reward the Americans with a very nice vassal trade deal? Or should we rather speak and trade with decent states from the rest of the world who never attack anyone, who offer much better markets and who uphold United Nations principles? I plead for the second approach. You unfortunately chose the first.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, vreți să contați în tot ceea ce înseamnă pacea la nivel mondial. Aș vrea să vă întreb, atunci când vă gândiți să contați la nivel internațional, cum v-ați apăra dumneavoastră eurodeputații? Am avut un eurodeputat care a fost arestat de către statul israelian când se ducea să ducă ajutoare în Palestina. Același deputat a fost arestat în Franța pentru nu știu ce postare pe Facebook, care nu a dăunat nimănui fără să i se ridice imunitatea. Dumneavoastră nu ați ajutat pe nimeni.

A fost o flotilă de ajutor către Palestina și nu ați intervenit ca să eliberați acei ostatici de către Israel, partenerul dumneavoastră, pe care toată lumea îl desfide pentru crimele împotriva umanității și genocidul pe care îl face în Palestina, în Fâșia Gaza, de zeci de ani.

Dumneavoastră unde sunteți când vreți să contați? Pakistanul v-a luat-o în față. Tot ceea ce se întâmplă în Orientul Mijlociu, se implică Rusia, Statele Unite ale Americii și China. Dumneavoastră nu existați.

paragraphs.text: Tomasz Froelich (ESN), schriftlichDie Aussicht auf Frieden zwischen dem Iran, Israel und den USA ist erfreulich. Zugleich ist Zurückhaltung geboten: Noch ist offen, wie belastbar die jüngsten Vereinbarungen tatsächlich sind. Die Waffenruhe muss nicht nur formal vereinbart, sondern auch eingehalten werden. Dazu gehört, dass die territoriale Integrität des Libanon respektiert wird. Die Inhalte des Abkommens werfen zudem Fragen auf. Denn gemessen an den Kriegszielen der USA ist deren Intervention ein Desaster: Kein Regimewechsel im Iran - stattdessen sitzt die politische Führung in Teheran fester im Sattel als zuvor. Die Straße von Hormus ist zwar wieder offen - allerdings war sie bereits vor der Intervention nicht dauerhaft geschlossen. Die Golfstaaten können sich auf amerikanische Sicherheitsgarantien nicht mehr stützen - für die regionale Ordnung ein schwerwiegender Rückschlag. Und die Atomfrage muss nun neu verhandelt werden - während kurz vor Kriegsbeginn eine Verständigung in Reichweite war.Wir Europäer haben ein Interesse an Stabilität in der Region. Denn wir leiden unter den Kollateralschäden dieses Kriegs - durch höhere Energiepreise, gefährdete Handelsrouten, verstärkte Migrationsbewegungen oder die sicherheitspolitische Instabilität in unmittelbarer Nachbarschaft. Für künftige Stabilität in der Region müssen die maßgeblichen Regionalmächte eingebunden werden: Pakistan, die Türkei, Saudi-Arabien. Für eine tragfähige regionale Sicherheitsordnung braucht es Diplomatie statt militärischer Eskalation.

paragraphs.text: Sandra Gómez López (S&D), por escritoSe cumplen 100 días del conflicto entre Irán y EE.UU. que comenzó con los ataques ilegales y unilaterales de EE.UU. e Israel contra Irán, que ha dejado más de 3.400 muertos, no ha traído democracia y cuya implementación del alto al fuego sigue siendo frágil.Reiteramos la condena de una guerra que no debía haber comenzado y que desestabiliza aún más la región. La situación en Oriente Medio se ha agravado y las principales víctimas son civiles inocentes: se contabilizan más de 72.900 muertos en Gaza, 1.171 muertos en Cisjordania, y cerca de 3.700 y 1,2 millones de desplazados en el Líbano, en un contexto de ocupación israelí de un país soberano y auge del terror Hezbolá. La paz no pasa por incursiones militares y la UE debe utilizar todos los canales diplomáticos para lograr un alto el fuego real además de retomar su compromiso con el cumplimiento del derecho internacional. Solicitamos que la Comisión desarrolle la Estrategia de la UE para Oriente Medio y que se adopten medidas como la suspensión de las disposiciones comerciales del Acuerdo de Asociación entre la UE e Israel, la detención del comercio de armas y que se impongan sanciones.

paragraphs.text: Matjaž Nemec (S&D), pisnoVojna v Iranu je znova razkrila nenačelno držo institucij EU v odnosu do ključnih mednarodnih vprašanj kot tudi pasivno držo Evrope ob dogodkih na Bližnjem vzhodu. Medtem ko je Evropa enotno obsodila kršitve mednarodnega prava z napadom Rusije na Ukrajino, si zatiskamo oči pred genocidom v Palestini. Največji faktor nestabilnosti v regiji ostaja Izrael, ki še naprej napada Libanon in palestinska ozemlja, Evropa pa znova ne ukrepa. Z nekaznovanjem izraelskega režima neposredno podpira nekaznovanost in kršitve mednarodnega prava.Če si EU želi povrniti svoj ugled in kredibilnost, mora najostreje in dosledno obsoditi vsa grozodejstva na Bližnjem vzhodu in kršitve mednarodnega prava, vključno z dejanji Izraela, in proti državi sprejeti ekonomske in politične sankcije.Na drugi strani pozdravljam začasno premirje med ZDA in Iranom, a ob tem ne smemo pozabiti na nezakonito in izsiljeno vojno, ki sta jo ZDA in Izrael začela. Prav tako ob tem ne smemo pozabiti na nedolžne žrtve in ogromno škodo, ki jo je vojna povzročila Iranu. Končanje agresije v Libanonu in v Gazi bo ključno za dolgotrajno premirje, s tem bi se morda lahko odprla nova vrata za začetek mirovnih pogovorov tudi o palestinsko-izraelskem konfliktu. Ob tem mora jasnejše in odločnejše stališče zavzeti tudi Evropa.

paragraphs.text: Good afternoon, dear colleagues, today we are joined by the President of Montenegro, Jakov Milatović.

Dear President, welcome to this Parliament. Thank you for your commitment and your leadership. I am especially pleased that this comes so soon after you hosted us in Montenegro at the first EU–Western Balkans Summit and after I had the honour and privilege to address your Parliament earlier this month.

This is, dear colleagues, Europe's enlargement moment, and Montenegro is leading the way. You have closed nearly half of all the accession chapters. Work has started on drafting the accession treaty. And our parliaments are cooperating closely to align legislation.

In fact, this Parliament has always been a great supporter of Montenegro, and you can count on our continued cooperation as we approach the final stretch to accession. Because we understand that enlargement is not a gift; it is a two-way street that benefits all of us across Europe. That is why we want your voice in this House as we make decisions; your ideas and insights, as we debate the direction of our continent; your expertise and your energy as we work towards a better future for all Europeans.
Montenegro belongs in this Parliament and in our Union. And one day soon we may see Montenegrin Members of the European Parliament joining colleagues in these seats.
We are nearly at the finish line and, when we get there, we will cross it together.
So, dear President, welcome again. I give you the floor.
