paragraphs.text: Madam President of the European Parliament, dear Roberta, honourable Members of the European Parliament, dear Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, dear friends, it is a great honour to address you today in the very heart of European democracy, at the moment when Montenegro is on the verge of achieving one of the most significant goals in our modern history.

I am addressing you on behalf of a remarkable Mediterranean country that has remained faithful to the grand European idea of peace, of freedom and solidarity, as well as the conviction that the peoples of Europe should build a shared future, relying on trust, respect and dignity for every individual.

Twenty years after the restoration of our independence, Montenegro today stands at the doors of the European Union, and this is a historic moment for my country. But also, I believe, a crucial moment for the enlargement policy, as the last country joined the EU almost 15 years ago, while in the meantime one country left the Union. Therefore, this moment is an opportunity for Europe to demonstrate that reforms, democratic development and strategic consistency hold the rightful place within the European club.

In 2006, Montenegro restored its independence peacefully and democratically, and in that moment, we also charted the course for our country's future. We chose to build a European, democratic, civic and open Montenegro, a country based upon the rule of law, strong institutions and a society in which diverse faiths, nations and cultures live together, and that choice has endured for two decades. It has been carried forward by different governments, different parliamentary majorities and different generations of citizens.

For Montenegro, therefore, the European path has never been only a foreign policy choice. It has been a social contract, a national consensus, and a steadfast foundation of values that has guided our country to change and anchored its vision for the future.

Dear friends, our European orientation has been unwavering ever since. Although circumstances have not always been favourable, nor has our journey towards the EU been linear. Indeed, shortly after Montenegro opened its accession talks with the EU, the European Commission President of that time, Mr Juncker, declared that there would be no further enlargement during his mandate. Yet Montenegro stayed on the course.

On that path, there have been some setbacks, there have been some missed opportunities, and there have been periods where reforms took more time than our citizens or our European partners expected. Nevertheless, the European idea has maintained its strength in Montenegro because our citizens, the citizens of Montenegro, have recognised it as the path towards a more prosperous future.

The reforms we are implementing have an impact on every citizen of Montenegro. They pertain to courts that operate with efficiency and fairness, to institutions that serve the public interest, to an economy that ensures prosperous life, and to young people, most importantly, to the young people who should be able to build their future within their own country. The reforms we carry out today shape the generations that will lead our country tomorrow. And that is why, for Montenegro, European Union membership holds profound internal significance. It represents the culmination of a national endeavour and the beginning of a new responsibility for us.

In 2012, as a Master's student at the University of Oxford, I watched Montenegro take a historic step by opening accession negotiations with the EU, just as Ukraine and Moldova did yesterday. Almost 15 years later – and three years after being elected President – I carry a clear mandate from the citizens of Montenegro to complete this journey and to secure our country's membership in the European Union by 2028.

Honourable Members of the European Parliament, much time has passed since the last European Union enlargement in 2013. Even more time has elapsed since the 2003 Thessaloniki summit, when the European perspective of the Western Balkans was confirmed. In the meantime, Europe has changed. The world has changed. War has returned to the European continent. Security challenges have become more complex. Geopolitical challenges have become our daily reality. In such a world, enlargement takes on a new role, not only the role of a policy, but of a European imperative.

Enlargement, dear friends, is an investment in the stability and security of the entire European continent. It is an answer to those who wish to render the European space more vulnerable, more divided and more insecure. It serves as proof of the European Union's political strength and its capacity to shape the future of its own continent. It is a reaffirmation that the European project continues to unite, to inspire and to transform.

Let me remind us all that the enlargement of the European Union to southern Europe in the 1980s, only a few years after some of those countries emerged from decades of military authoritarian regimes, was not merely an act of expansion. It was an investment in stability, democracy and prosperity – not only for southern Europe back then, but for Europe as a whole. And the same logic guided the European project after the fall of the Berlin Wall. By embracing the countries of central and eastern Europe, Europe reunited with itself, healing the divisions of the Cold War and extending the space of peace, freedom and opportunity across the entire continent.

That is why today I am not speaking merely about the accession of one country, my country, Montenegro. I am speaking about the European Union's capacity to fulfil its own promises towards the Western Balkans and uphold the principles upon which it was built. Among those principles one stands out in particular: that progress must be measured by results, and that results must be recognised. Today, Montenegro is ready to serve as a proof of that principle.

We have opened all 33 chapters and have closed 16, so half. The Council of the European Union has begun work on the draft accession treaty with Montenegro, which is an institutional signal that our European finale has become a concrete political and legal process.

Montenegro, dear friends, in many ways already aligns itself strategically with the EU. Montenegro already uses the euro as its official currency. Since 2017, so almost for 10 years now, we have been a reliable member of the NATO alliance, like most of the EU countries. For years, Montenegro has been fully aligned with the common foreign and security policy of the European Union, and since the Russian war against Ukraine, this fact has gained an even greater significance as a testament to the depth of our strategic partnership.

Montenegro has already demonstrated that it knows where we belong. It has shown that it understands the responsibilities that a European future entails. It has proven its strategic reliability, its institutional seriousness and the support of its citizens for EU membership.

Dear friends, the democratic maturity of Montenegro was particularly confirmed by the peaceful transition of power in 2020, while the results of the 2023 presidential and parliamentary elections provided new momentum and new impetus to our European journey. In the years that followed, our institutions have demonstrated that Montenegro possesses the political will and capacity to conclude negotiations and to assume the obligations of a Member State.

However, there is still some work to be done, and we know that. Strengthening the rule of law, independent institutions, and building an even more efficient public administration, while at the same time focusing on our economic convergence with the EU, remain our key tasks. Montenegro enters this final phase with eyes wide open, with a clear awareness of what our responsibilities are and with a very strong determination to bring this mission to its conclusion.

Just 10 days ago, Montenegro hosted a very symbolic and, for us, a very historic EU-Western Balkans Summit. Leaders of EU Member States, of the European institutions and the region all gathered in Montenegro for the very first time in our history. Montenegro, though small in size, has proven itself large enough in vision and capacity, as well as in ambition, to host Europe and to serve as a place where the future of our continent is shaped and discussed.

So if the summit in Thessaloniki opened the European perspective for the Western Balkans back in 2003, the summit in Montenegro, organised a few days ago, confirmed that the enlargement policy has regained its momentum once again, with Montenegro indeed leading the way. In Thessaloniki, Europe gave us a perspective. In Montenegro, we welcomed Europe with hope and determination that, by 2028, Europe will welcome Montenegro as its newest Member State.

Let me come to a conclusion. I believe that this very European Parliament will hold a special place in the history of European enlargement. The last time the European Parliament ratified an accession treaty of a forthcoming Member State was in December 2011, almost 15 years ago. I genuinely hope that you will be doing so during your mandate in the case of Montenegro.

Montenegro's accession to the EU will be our joint victory, a success for Montenegro, a success for the European Union. It will also be an encouragement for the entire Western Balkan region. It will be proof that reforms lead to the goal, that your promises hold credibility and that the common future of Europe remains open to those who share the same values.

Montenegro's accession as the 28th Member State of the EU by 2028 will mark the beginning of the fulfilment of the promise made a while ago, restore confidence in the enlargement policy, contribute to the long‑term stability of the Western Balkans and strengthen Europe's global role in an era daily defined by geopolitical challenges.

Let me be very clear about one thing: Montenegro is not joining the EU in order to become someone else. It is joining because it has always belonged to the European political and cultural space, a space defined by the values of multicultural harmony, dignity and freedom, a space from whose black mountains – as our name says – some of the most noble ideas have risen and found their place in Europe's shared heritage.

Montenegro brings the experience of a society that has preserved multi-ethnic harmony in a region very often burdened by a difficult history. We bring Mediterranean openness as well as the Balkan resilience. We bring a tradition of freedom and a European political orientation. We bring a reliable partnership in matters of security and foreign policy, and we bring the conviction that Europe is strongest when it gathers different traditions and identities around the same values.

So, dear friends, my final message is that Montenegro is ready! Montenegro is ready to assume the responsibilities of a Member State. We are ready to contribute to European policies. We are ready to bind our future to the common European future and we are ready to be the next member of the European Union.

This is a historic opportunity which lies before all of us. For Montenegro, it is a chance to complete a generational endeavour. For the EU, it is a chance to confirm the determination of its own enlargement policy. And for the Western Balkans, it is a chance to see that the European path brings tangible results.

In 1878, at the Congress of Berlin, Montenegro became the 27th internationally recognised state. After a century and a half, the time has come for Montenegro to become the 28th Member State of the EU by 2028. And the time has come to shape history once again – together. So long live Montenegro and long live the European Union!

interventions.text:
Madam President of the European Parliament, dear Roberta, honourable Members of the European Parliament, dear Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, dear friends, it is a great honour to address you today in the very heart of European democracy, at the moment when Montenegro is on the verge of achieving one of the most significant goals in our modern history.

I am addressing you on behalf of a remarkable Mediterranean country that has remained faithful to the grand European idea of peace, of freedom and solidarity, as well as the conviction that the peoples of Europe should build a shared future, relying on trust, respect and dignity for every individual.

Twenty years after the restoration of our independence, Montenegro today stands at the doors of the European Union, and this is a historic moment for my country. But also, I believe, a crucial moment for the enlargement policy, as the last country joined the EU almost 15 years ago, while in the meantime one country left the Union. Therefore, this moment is an opportunity for Europe to demonstrate that reforms, democratic development and strategic consistency hold the rightful place within the European club.

In 2006, Montenegro restored its independence peacefully and democratically, and in that moment, we also charted the course for our country's future. We chose to build a European, democratic, civic and open Montenegro, a country based upon the rule of law, strong institutions and a society in which diverse faiths, nations and cultures live together, and that choice has endured for two decades. It has been carried forward by different governments, different parliamentary majorities and different generations of citizens.

For Montenegro, therefore, the European path has never been only a foreign policy choice. It has been a social contract, a national consensus, and a steadfast foundation of values that has guided our country to change and anchored its vision for the future.

Dear friends, our European orientation has been unwavering ever since. Although circumstances have not always been favourable, nor has our journey towards the EU been linear. Indeed, shortly after Montenegro opened its accession talks with the EU, the European Commission President of that time, Mr Juncker, declared that there would be no further enlargement during his mandate. Yet Montenegro stayed on the course.

On that path, there have been some setbacks, there have been some missed opportunities, and there have been periods where reforms took more time than our citizens or our European partners expected. Nevertheless, the European idea has maintained its strength in Montenegro because our citizens, the citizens of Montenegro, have recognised it as the path towards a more prosperous future.

The reforms we are implementing have an impact on every citizen of Montenegro. They pertain to courts that operate with efficiency and fairness, to institutions that serve the public interest, to an economy that ensures prosperous life, and to young people, most importantly, to the young people who should be able to build their future within their own country. The reforms we carry out today shape the generations that will lead our country tomorrow. And that is why, for Montenegro, European Union membership holds profound internal significance. It represents the culmination of a national endeavour and the beginning of a new responsibility for us.

In 2012, as a Master's student at the University of Oxford, I watched Montenegro take a historic step by opening accession negotiations with the EU, just as Ukraine and Moldova did yesterday. Almost 15 years later – and three years after being elected President – I carry a clear mandate from the citizens of Montenegro to complete this journey and to secure our country's membership in the European Union by 2028.

Honourable Members of the European Parliament, much time has passed since the last European Union enlargement in 2013. Even more time has elapsed since the 2003 Thessaloniki summit, when the European perspective of the Western Balkans was confirmed. In the meantime, Europe has changed. The world has changed. War has returned to the European continent. Security challenges have become more complex. Geopolitical challenges have become our daily reality. In such a world, enlargement takes on a new role, not only the role of a policy, but of a European imperative.

Enlargement, dear friends, is an investment in the stability and security of the entire European continent. It is an answer to those who wish to render the European space more vulnerable, more divided and more insecure. It serves as proof of the European Union's political strength and its capacity to shape the future of its own continent. It is a reaffirmation that the European project continues to unite, to inspire and to transform.

Let me remind us all that the enlargement of the European Union to southern Europe in the 1980s, only a few years after some of those countries emerged from decades of military authoritarian regimes, was not merely an act of expansion. It was an investment in stability, democracy and prosperity – not only for southern Europe back then, but for Europe as a whole. And the same logic guided the European project after the fall of the Berlin Wall. By embracing the countries of central and eastern Europe, Europe reunited with itself, healing the divisions of the Cold War and extending the space of peace, freedom and opportunity across the entire continent.

That is why today I am not speaking merely about the accession of one country, my country, Montenegro. I am speaking about the European Union's capacity to fulfil its own promises towards the Western Balkans and uphold the principles upon which it was built. Among those principles one stands out in particular: that progress must be measured by results, and that results must be recognised. Today, Montenegro is ready to serve as a proof of that principle.

We have opened all 33 chapters and have closed 16, so half. The Council of the European Union has begun work on the draft accession treaty with Montenegro, which is an institutional signal that our European finale has become a concrete political and legal process.

Montenegro, dear friends, in many ways already aligns itself strategically with the EU. Montenegro already uses the euro as its official currency. Since 2017, so almost for 10 years now, we have been a reliable member of the NATO alliance, like most of the EU countries. For years, Montenegro has been fully aligned with the common foreign and security policy of the European Union, and since the Russian war against Ukraine, this fact has gained an even greater significance as a testament to the depth of our strategic partnership.

Montenegro has already demonstrated that it knows where we belong. It has shown that it understands the responsibilities that a European future entails. It has proven its strategic reliability, its institutional seriousness and the support of its citizens for EU membership.

Dear friends, the democratic maturity of Montenegro was particularly confirmed by the peaceful transition of power in 2020, while the results of the 2023 presidential and parliamentary elections provided new momentum and new impetus to our European journey. In the years that followed, our institutions have demonstrated that Montenegro possesses the political will and capacity to conclude negotiations and to assume the obligations of a Member State.

However, there is still some work to be done, and we know that. Strengthening the rule of law, independent institutions, and building an even more efficient public administration, while at the same time focusing on our economic convergence with the EU, remain our key tasks. Montenegro enters this final phase with eyes wide open, with a clear awareness of what our responsibilities are and with a very strong determination to bring this mission to its conclusion.

Just 10 days ago, Montenegro hosted a very symbolic and, for us, a very historic EU-Western Balkans Summit. Leaders of EU Member States, of the European institutions and the region all gathered in Montenegro for the very first time in our history. Montenegro, though small in size, has proven itself large enough in vision and capacity, as well as in ambition, to host Europe and to serve as a place where the future of our continent is shaped and discussed.

So if the summit in Thessaloniki opened the European perspective for the Western Balkans back in 2003, the summit in Montenegro, organised a few days ago, confirmed that the enlargement policy has regained its momentum once again, with Montenegro indeed leading the way. In Thessaloniki, Europe gave us a perspective. In Montenegro, we welcomed Europe with hope and determination that, by 2028, Europe will welcome Montenegro as its newest Member State.

Let me come to a conclusion. I believe that this very European Parliament will hold a special place in the history of European enlargement. The last time the European Parliament ratified an accession treaty of a forthcoming Member State was in December 2011, almost 15 years ago. I genuinely hope that you will be doing so during your mandate in the case of Montenegro.

Montenegro's accession to the EU will be our joint victory, a success for Montenegro, a success for the European Union. It will also be an encouragement for the entire Western Balkan region. It will be proof that reforms lead to the goal, that your promises hold credibility and that the common future of Europe remains open to those who share the same values.

Montenegro's accession as the 28th Member State of the EU by 2028 will mark the beginning of the fulfilment of the promise made a while ago, restore confidence in the enlargement policy, contribute to the long‑term stability of the Western Balkans and strengthen Europe's global role in an era daily defined by geopolitical challenges.

Let me be very clear about one thing: Montenegro is not joining the EU in order to become someone else. It is joining because it has always belonged to the European political and cultural space, a space defined by the values of multicultural harmony, dignity and freedom, a space from whose black mountains – as our name says – some of the most noble ideas have risen and found their place in Europe's shared heritage.

Montenegro brings the experience of a society that has preserved multi-ethnic harmony in a region very often burdened by a difficult history. We bring Mediterranean openness as well as the Balkan resilience. We bring a tradition of freedom and a European political orientation. We bring a reliable partnership in matters of security and foreign policy, and we bring the conviction that Europe is strongest when it gathers different traditions and identities around the same values.

So, dear friends, my final message is that Montenegro is ready! Montenegro is ready to assume the responsibilities of a Member State. We are ready to contribute to European policies. We are ready to bind our future to the common European future and we are ready to be the next member of the European Union.

This is a historic opportunity which lies before all of us. For Montenegro, it is a chance to complete a generational endeavour. For the EU, it is a chance to confirm the determination of its own enlargement policy. And for the Western Balkans, it is a chance to see that the European path brings tangible results.

In 1878, at the Congress of Berlin, Montenegro became the 27th internationally recognised state. After a century and a half, the time has come for Montenegro to become the 28th Member State of the EU by 2028. And the time has come to shape history once again – together. So long live Montenegro and long live the European Union!

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, there has been no parliamentary debate on this resolution, yet it has already stirred some media controversy, so let us be clear about what this proposal does.

It calls on the Commission to present a legislative regulation that addresses the financial shortcomings and ensures predictability for the European political foundations. The proposals we have put forward will benefit all European political foundations, from the left to the right.

This is not a revolutionary shift, and it certainly does not compromise our strict scrutiny or transparency provisions. Furthermore, this has nothing to do with any recent findings of the Authority for European Political Parties and Foundations regarding a specific political party.

Therefore, I kindly ask you to support the resolution, and I also call on the Commission to swiftly propose a revision to the Regulation, and on the Council to support the revision through speedy negotiations. I would like to thank my co-rapporteur, Charles Goerens, for our common work, and the Secretariat.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, comment pérenniser l’indispensable travail des fondations politiques européennes?

Nous voulons le faire en trois phases. La première, c’est la proposition sur laquelle vous allez vous prononcer dans quelques instants. Celle-ci plaide en faveur d’une augmentation du cofinancement des activités et des fondations politiques à charge du budget de l’Union européenne. L’on pourra ainsi mettre fin à la précarité financière desdites fondations. Dans la deuxième phase, nous espérons voir la Commission reprendre l’essentiel de notre texte et déposer une proposition législative. La troisième phase – législative cette fois, et lancée par la Commission –, que nous espérons très prochaine, devrait nous permettre de répondre aux attentes plus que justifiées des fondations, dont le travail d’analyse et de réflexion contribue à enrichir le débat public européen.

Cette procédure s’apparente à l’initiative législative du Parlement européen, que nous revendiquons depuis belle lurette. Ce n’est pas encore le pas décisif et à l’initiative législative, mais c’est un pas dans cette direction. Et je remercie aussi mon corapporteur, Loránt Vincze.

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, we all know how brutally authoritarian regimes silence dissent at home in Iran, Russia, Venezuela, Vietnam and so many other places.

But they also reach into Europe right at this moment, also in your home countries. Chinese overseas police stations in Italy, Croatia, Germany or Ireland. Iranian operatives working with organised crime to plot attacks in Netherlands or Spain. Russian agents intimidating opposition activists on the streets of Poland or Latvia. Moroccan media networks waging smear campaigns to humiliate and sexualise dissidents online. Families threatened, bank accounts frozen, phones hacked, lives put at risk. The danger is everywhere, and all too often those targeted are left to face it alone.

These are not isolated incidents, dear colleagues. This is a deliberate and systematic assault on our security, our sovereignty, our democracy, and our response must be just as systematic. We have to join forces between the EU and Member States and close the gaps between digital and security policy and between migration, justice, interior and foreign affairs in order to name what these regimes want to deny, to document what they seek to hide, to protect those they target, to close the loopholes that they abuse in our systems and to impose consequences for what they do.

With transnational repression, autocrats want to send a chilling message: you are nowhere safe. Our answer has to be loud and stronger: we will no longer tolerate such repression on European soil. This report lays out the plan on how to get there. Implementation needs to come next.
So with this vote, dear colleagues, let's send a clear signal to dissidents, journalists, human rights defenders, diaspora communities: you will be safe, now and here.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, Europe needs to be seen as the strongest soft power on earth. In humanitarian aid, in development aid, when it comes to European businesses, European reliability is the largest on earth. Europe will stay strong in these fields and Europe will remain reliable to other parts of the world.

At the same time, Europe has to tackle, as the report calls it, 'irregular population movements'. It is important that we put the one thing to the other, because no person on earth should be uprooted from its home against its will. And this is so important that we contribute to both – to development aid, to our soft power, as well as to tackling irregular population movements, for the sake of the Europeans, and for the sake of the people who must not be uprooted.

I want to thank, in particular, the negotiators of the political groups for constructive negotiations, tough negotiations, of course, but for seeking common ground and, actually, for achieving common ground. I want to thank everybody contributing to a compromise which led to a proper result, a stable result and a strong message from this very European Parliament that we can send today. That is why I humbly ask the colleagues in this Chamber to give their consent to this report.

paragraphs.text: I have been a Member of the European Parliament; I know that after the votes, it's always the colleagues that you need to discuss with, right?

But anyway, coming to this topic. Europe has, for years, faced cyberattacks, disinformation campaigns and acts of sabotage and disruption. But the frequency and severity of these attacks is unprecedented. Recently, we have experienced also repeated drone incursions into EU airspace and the crash of a Russian drone carrying explosives into a residential building in Romania. These reckless acts underscore the threat that Russia poses to EU citizens, regional stability and international peace, and its readiness to escalate the conflict. These actions seem designed to turn our public opinion away from our steadfast support to Ukraine.

Honourable Members, the statement of 29 May by all 27 Member States on the latest unprovoked violations of the EU airspace by Russia was an undeniable display of unity. Beyond condemnation, we must further strengthen our ability to respond to Russia's provocations reaching our territories. We also need to advance our counter-hybrid agenda. This requires strengthening situational awareness, bolstering resilience, protecting our critical infrastructure and operational readiness to respond.

We must improve our capacity to rapidly attribute hostile acts and raise the costs for Russia for conducting them. Most of all, in the case of Russian drones crossing into EU airspace, we must invest in cheap interceptors to protect our citizens. Shooting a EUR 1 million interceptor missile at the drone that costs EUR 3 000 is not sustainable. We must strengthen the protection of all EU land, air and maritime borders, with particular attention required to the eastern flank.

Important work is already underway, including through the drone capability coalition led by Latvia, Croatia and the Netherlands, and close cooperation with Ukraine is essential, allowing us to draw from their invaluable operational experience. I also welcome the progress made on the Action Plan on Drone and Counter Drone Security. While significant steps have been taken, including increased defence spending across Europe, much more is needed. Leaders will return to this issue in the upcoming European Council later this week.

Honourable Members, as we are preparing for the forthcoming NATO summit, the EU-NATO strategic partnership and reinforced cooperation remains vital to close capability gaps and strengthen collective security. Any hesitation risks inviting further tests of our resolve. NATO remains the cornerstone of the collective defence of its allies and leads the operational military activities. The EU's initiatives enhance overall defence readiness and resilience, in particular on the eastern flank. The EU and NATO must work hand in hand in responding to the incidents, strengthening deterrence and countering hostile narratives through strategic communication.

Honourable Members, let me conclude by emphasising a simple reality: Russia represents the most direct and immediate threat to the security of the European Union, not only through its war of aggression against Ukraine, but also for its systematic use of hybrid tactics against our societies and institutions. We must remain calm, united and firm in our response.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Honourable High Representative, dear colleagues, drones penetrating EU countries' airspace or territorial waters are a problem. They cause warnings to take shelter and avoid movements, causing fear and anxiety among the population, actions that are still necessary since drones hitting residential areas are dangerous, as we saw happening in Romania not long ago. The same goes for how sea drones can be transferred to our shipping and coastal installations, as we saw again in Romania.

Defending against these drones is not without risks either. Shooting down drones with air-to-air missiles is not only very expensive, but also risky to the population when the missiles miss the target or debris from the intercepted drones hit the ground, as we saw happening in Poland some time ago.

As you can see, we are talking about real threats towards our people. So we need to stop these incursions, whether they come by air or by sea. And we need to stop them by tackling the root cause of these incidents. We must remember that whether it is a Russian drone flown on purpose over our airspace, or a Ukrainian drone or uncrewed surface vessel that has strayed from its course due to Russian electronic interference, it all happens due to the Russian illegal aggression on Ukraine.

Russia is at fault here, and since the war is not going well for Russia, these incidents and provocations towards Russia's neighbours will increase. Russia cannot win the Ukrainian battlefield, therefore Putin tries to kill as many Ukrainian civilians as possible and destroy as many cultural sites as possible, as we have seen this week. And if some EU citizens get caught in the crossfire, he couldn't care less.

So we need to end the war in Ukraine as soon as possible. Russia is weakening. Its supporters, like China, are already distancing themselves from the failing dictator and even President Trump's administration starts to see that Putin does not have any cards left.

Now is not the time to hold back. Now it is time to support Ukraine more. The EU's EUR 90 billion loan to Ukraine is just a good start. paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, doamnă comisară, astăzi vreau să vorbesc despre oameni, despre familiile din România care s-au trezit în mijlocul nopții din cauza exploziilor, despre comunitățile de la granița Uniunii Europene care trăiesc de luni de zile sub amenințarea dronelor și despre copilul rănit în propria casă, la Galați, după ce o dronă a lovit blocul în care locuia.

Aceste incidente nu mai pot fi privite ca evenimente izolate. Ele reprezintă o amenințare directă la adresa cetățenilor europeni, a comunităților noastre și a infrastructurii critice din regiunea Mării Negre. Tocmai de aceea am propus această dezbatere și această rezoluție și avem nevoie astăzi de măsuri concrete: un sistem european comun de monitorizare și avertizare timpurie, consolidarea capacităților anti-dronă și de apărare aeriană pe flancul estic, finanțarea din bani europeni a infrastructurii critice și defensive, mecanisme europene care să permită sprijinirea rapidă a comunităților afectate.

Cerem, de asemenea, operaționalizarea rapidă a hubului european de securitate maritimă de la Marea Neagră. Mesajul nostru este simplu: fiecare cetățean european are dreptul să se simtă în siguranță în propria casă.

interventions.speaker_label: Pierre-Romain Thionnet, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Madame la Haute représentante, chers collègues, en premier lieu, je souhaite communiquer notre soutien et assurer de notre solidarité l’ensemble des États ayant été confrontés aux incursions de drones armés dans leur espace aérien. Certains incidents ont même donné lieu à des dommages particulièrement graves sur des habitations et des infrastructures civiles – en Roumanie notamment –, et les populations locales ont été soumises à un stress inhabituel, appelées parfois à se mettre à l’abri – comme cela a été le cas en Finlande récemment.

Dans cette période de tension palpable, alors que le conflit russo-ukrainien vient de dépasser en longueur la durée du premier conflit mondial, notre rôle est double: faire preuve de sang-froid dans la manière dont nous réagissons, d’une part; tirer les enseignements quant aux mesures, procédures et capacités concrètes dont nous faisons usage pour traiter la menace des drones armés, d’autre part.

En matière de communication, certaines surréactions sont plus dommageables que bénéfiques. Qu’avons-nous à gagner à mal nommer les choses et à ne pas les présenter de manière parfaitement factuelle? Pour être très clair, ici: si l’on prend l’immense majorité des derniers incidents, il s’agit ou de drones ukrainiens longue portée qui ont été détournés par les contre-mesures russes ou de drones russes brouillés et déviés par les défenses ukrainiennes.

En bref, la source de ces incidents, si graves soient-ils, réside dans les effets indirects de la guerre. Une guerre dont la responsabilité incombe bien sûr à la décision russe d’envahir l’Ukraine – cela ne fait aucun doute –, mais nous devons veiller à rester précis dans la description de tous les incidents. Si nous ne le faisons pas, les relais de propagande adverses s’en servent pour discréditer notre parole et marteler que la menace russe est un fantasme collectif. Là où nous devons réagir et agir d’urgence, c’est dans notre approche vis-à-vis de la lutte antidrone. Mieux nous saurons réagir, moins nous serons fébriles, plus nous serons crédibles – donc dissuasifs.

Permettez-moi, pour conclure, de souligner le rôle des forces alliées engagées dans la sécurisation du ciel européen sur le flanc est, – en particulier, mais pas uniquement, aux pilotes français de Rafale, qui ont neutralisé il y a quelques jours un drone armé dans l’espace aérien de la Lettonie alliée.

interventions.speaker_label: Reinis Pozņaks, on behalf of the ECR Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the ECR Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, I must start with the obvious. I strongly condemn Russia's provocation, I express my solidarity with those injured in Romania and I call for a stronger action against Russia.

With that said, I believe this is not the response our citizens expect from us anymore. They expect solutions – solutions to protect our people, our critical infrastructure and our economies, especially in affected regions. Many of those solutions have already been identified in the documents produced within this building, but I have the feeling that we are still in the face of denial, as if we have not yet accepted that we will have to live with a very new type of a man-made disaster: bad actors using cheap but destructive technologies against our societies. We like to put the word 'security' in the titles, but far too rarely into the budget lines. It's no more a future threat; it's today's reality, and we need to adapt.

paragraphs.text: Gerbiamasis Pirmininke, gerbiama aukštoji atstove, leiskite išreikšti apgailestavimą nematant pirmininkaujančios valstybės, Kipro, atstovo šioje salėje, kada kalbame apie valstybių ir viso regiono saugumą. Tai yra nepriimtina.

Rusija ir toliau intensyvina hibridinio karo išpuolius prieš Europą, Europos Sąjungos rytinio flango valstybes ir daro tai nesislapstydama, skirdama tam milžiniškus ir vis augančius resursus. Pagrindinis atsakas į šias Rusijos atakas – kuo spartesnis pačios Europos Sąjungos ir NATO gynybinių pajėgumų Europoje stiprinimas. Ypatingai būtini aukštųjų gynybos technologijų sprendimai.

Ne mažiau svarbus yra asimetriškas Europos Sąjungos atsakas, dar griežtesnės finansinės ir ekonominės sankcijos Rusijai, tiesiogiai mažinančios agresorės galimybes tęsti karą ne tik prieš Ukrainą, bet ir vykdyti hibridines atakas prieš Europos Sąjungą. Europos Sąjunga jau priėmė dvidešimt Rusijai skirtų sankcijų paketų. Bet to dar negana. Turime kuo greičiau naikinti pavojingas spragas, likusias spragas ir tinkamai atsakyti į Rusijos išpuolius, kuomet, jai tęsiant karo nusikaltimus, atakuojamas netgi istorinis UNESCO saugomas paveldas.

interventions.speaker_label: Nicolae Ștefănuță, în numele grupului Verts/ALE.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, doamnă Kallas, imaginați-vă că sunteți acasă și locuiți în Galați, în Tulcea sau în una din insulele de pe Dunăre și dintr-o dată, la două noaptea, primiți un mesaj că acum trebuie să coborâți undeva să vă ascundeți, că este grav, că este pericol de moarte, că poți acum... . În acel moment, geopolitica dispare. Nu mai este o situație teoretică, este o situație foarte, foarte practică, imediată, urgentă și rămâne mama care își ia copilul în brațe, bunicul care nu poate coborî repede scările, rămân oamenii care trăiesc în UE și NATO și aud războiul la câțiva kilometri de casă.

Rusia ce face acum? Testează cât acceptăm. Și îmi place cum a dat răspunsul Zelenski ‑ răspunsul o să-l vadă Putin. Nu trebuie să acceptăm nimic. Asta este linia roșie a Europei: nimic. Pur și simplu nimic. Și răspunsul trebuie să fie unul unit, european. Pentru că degeaba unii își cumpără avioane de un fel, alții portavioane de alt fel, dacă nu suntem în stare noi, ca europeni, să oferim un răspuns comun. Pentru că data viitoare când sună telefonul, oamenii să știe că Europa protejează și aici, îi protejează la ei acasă de străini, de ruși, de dușmani.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, Venäjän toistuvat provokaatiot ja droonien tunkeutumiset Romanian, Baltian maiden ja Suomen ilmatilaan ovat vakava haaste Euroopan turvallisuudelle. Ne eivät ole vain yksittäisiä tapauksia, vaan osa toimintaa, jolla testataan Euroopan valmiutta ja yhtenäisyyttä.

Suomelle ja muille Venäjän naapurimaille tällaiset loukkaukset ovat muistutus siitä, että turvallisuutemme on yhteinen. Kun yhden jäsenvaltion turvallisuutta haastetaan, koko Euroopan unionia haastetaan. Siksi EU:n on vahvistettava ilmatilan valvontaa, tiedusteluyhteistyötä ja kykyä torjua uusia uhkia. Samalla meidän on jatkettava vahvaa tukeamme Ukrainalle.

Viestimme Venäjälle on oltava yksiselitteinen. Me emme hyväksy ilmatilamme minkäänlaisia loukkauksia emmekä minkäänlaista pelottelua. Eurooppa seisoo yhtenäisenä, puolustaa suvereniteettiaan ja turvaa jokaisen kansalaisensa turvallisuuden.

paragraphs.text: Vážený pán predsedajúci, Zelenský na Ukrajine oslavuje a obnovuje nacistické jednotky, ktoré vyvraždili Poliakov a Slovákov. A nikomu v europarlamente to nevadí. Minulý mesiac dokonca dostal ocenenie. Takisto je tu dvojaký meter. Všetci hovoria o zločinoch Ruska, ale keď Ukrajinci bombardujú internát na ruskom území, tak to je v poriadku a takisto si to nikto nevšimne. A práve tento dvojaký meter je prekážkou pre rokovania o mieri. A mne to trošku vadí, pretože ja nechcem nasledujúce desaťročia prežiť v Európskej únii neustálym rozprávaním o vojne, o strachu. O tom, že treba dať desiatky, stovky miliárd eur na rakety, na zbrane, na drony alebo poslať na Ukrajinu. Ja chcem žiť v Európe, ktorá bude vychádzať s východnými štátmi mierovo. V kľude budeme vedieť s nimi spolupracovať a budeme sa môcť sústrediť na riešenie hospodárskych problémov Európanov, našich obyvateľov, aby sa im žilo lepšie. Takže, prosím vás, prestaňte neustále rozprávať o vojne a začnime konečne rozprávať o mieri.

interventions.speaker_label: Kaja Kallas, Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy

paragraphs.text: Mr President, thank you, honourable Members, for this first round of debate.

I think it shows that these attacks are not isolated incidents. I mean, there are not drones gone astray, soldiers having wrong maps or pilots mistakenly diverting from their flight plan. This is coordinated and organised, testing our readiness to counter. We really need to respond with unity, increased deterrence and resolve and send a firm message to Moscow that Europe stands together to defend security, stability and our values.

I also agree with Mr Pozņaks, who doesn't seem to be here any more, who said 'not only words but also action', meaning that the budget should also show that we are taking this seriously. As the budget talks are going on, you can also, as Members of Parliament, look into that the budget also goes for these events.

I also want to say to Mr Ștefănuță that I do not have to imagine, because I come from a country that is actually bordering Russia. These things are not isolated incidents countries. I mean, there was Ms Kyllönen, who was saying the same for Finland. These are not isolated incidents. We don't have to imagine what it means when you get the message 'go to a shelter', because this is already the reality.

But also, to the last speaker, I must say that, of course, everybody is supporting peace, but if we have a neighbour like this that hasn't really concealed his goals and threats against the European Union then spending on deterrence is much cheaper than fighting a war.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, dragi colegi, în noaptea zilei de 29 mai, o dronă rusească s-a prăbușit într-o clădire rezidențială din România. Două persoane au fost rănite, iar sute de oameni au fost evacuați. Este primul atac cu o dronă rusească cu victime civile pe teritoriul unui stat membru al Uniunii Europene. Ceea ce s-a întâmplat în România nu este un caz izolat, este un semnal direct că securitatea Uniunii Europene este contestată chiar pe teritoriul nostru, iar o amenințare la adresa unui stat membru este o amenințare la adresa noastră, a tuturor.

Agresiunea Federației Ruse nu mai este o amenințare abstractă. Ea se manifestă aici, în țările noastre, în Uniunea Europeană, printr-un tipar constant de război hibrid: incursiuni ale dronelor, atacuri cibernetice, sabotaj, bruiaj și dezinformare. Prin aceste acțiuni, să înțelegem bine, Federația Rusă testează vigilența noastră și capacitatea de reacție. Răspunsul nostru trebuie să fie clar: Uniunea Europeană își protejează cetățenii.

Trebuie să ne consolidăm capacitățile de apărare, în special împotriva dronelor, și să accelerăm cooperarea cu NATO, inclusiv prin mecanismul de supraveghere al flancului estic. Statele de pe flancul estic sunt în prima linie, ca atare au nevoie de instrumente adecvate pentru a răspunde acestor amenințări tot mai frecvente. Uniunea Europeană trebuie să transmită un mesaj fără echivoc: aceste atacuri și incursiuni nu sunt tolerate. Vom fi din ce în ce mai bine pregătiți, vom proteja cetățenii.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Madam High Representative, colleagues, the Russian provocations and drone incursions are becoming more frequent and more severe. They are presenting a threat to civilian lives and infrastructure, and they are also causing disruptions to our normal everyday operations, including civilian air traffic.
But they are also causing emotional stress among the people, and they have a longer-term economic impact by undermining business and investor confidence.
We must respond, but obviously there is no single silver bullet and no single installation that we could call 'Drone Wall', so we have to take a very complex and layered approach to our response.

We need deterrence. That means that reckless provocations must incur a cost on the perpetrators. We also need to improve radically our situational awareness and our detection capabilities, and we must improve our interception capability. That would do the necessary task. This requires mobilisation of both national and EU assets, and we can also draw on the vast experience that our Ukrainian friends and allies have acquired over the past four years.

paragraphs.text: Domnul președinte, total inacceptabile incursiunile dronelor rusești în România. Dar mai există un subiect care trebuie atins. O dronă maritimă ucraineană, asupra căreia Ucraina a pierdut controlul, a intrat pe teritoriul României și a explodat în portul Constanța.

Faptul că s-a putut pierde controlul asupra ei din cauza atacurilor rusești injuste nu surprinde. Ceea ce surprinde și dezamăgește totodată este reacția mult întârziată a partenerilor și prietenilor ucraineni, care ne-au avertizat de pericolul iminent cu patru ore mai târziu, conform declarațiilor oficiale ale Ministerului Apărării din România.

Dacă drona ucraineană deturnată ar fi ajuns la Oil Terminal, unde există un petrolier plin de combustibil, incendiul ar fi cuprins întregul terminal petrolier, extinzându-se și la depozitul de azotat de amoniu de lângă. O explozie a acestei rezerve de azotat de amoniu ar fi devastat orașul Constanța și ar fi generat sute de mii de victime. Ba mai mult, ar fi băgat România și întreaga Europă în război cu Rusia.

Acest mesaj este pentru prietenii noștri ucraineni, pe care UE îi ajută și-i va mai ajuta și în continuare din banii noștri: ne așteptăm să dați dovadă de seriozitate și respect pentru ajutorul primit și să nu puneți în pericol viețile cetățenilor noștri prin informări întârziate. Așa fac adevărații aliați!

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, doamnă Înaltă Reprezentantă, Federația Rusă a readus de facto războiul la granița Europei. Rusia este astăzi cea mai gravă amenințare la adresa securității noastre comune. Cine neagă această realitate sau refuză să identifice un agresor este fie vândut complet, fie iresponsabil. Și sunt câțiva și în acest legislativ. E ceasul al doisprezecelea pentru Europa și pentru NATO să se trezească la realitate.

Susțin cu toată tăria sprijinul nostru pentru Ucraina, dar acesta devine insuficient. Războiul Rusiei nu mai cunoaște frontiere tradiționale, așa că cer imperios consolidarea imediată a flancului estic și a securității la Marea Neagră, finanțare sporită în viitorul cadru financiar multianual pentru sisteme anti-dronă destinate țărilor expuse și accelerarea creării Centrului de securitate maritimă de la Marea Neagră.

Cooperarea cu Ucraina și Republica Moldova este esențială și avem nevoie urgentă să integrăm expertiza Ucrainei în sistemele noastre de apărare. Securitatea Europei se află și se întâmplă în anii aceștia la granița estică, pentru toți cetățenii Uniunii Europene.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, I welcome this debate and I thank all the colleagues from Romania, Finland, the Baltic States and other countries for making it happen.

But while we speak about the drones, let us not forget about the most powerful weapon Russia has, and it is lies. Russia spread the lies that drones were launched from the Baltic territory. And this is an aggressive attack, designed to create the pretext against the Member States. We can watch, we can condemn, but this will achieve nothing.

Europe needs what I call a black book: a systematic record of every aggressive act Russia commits against the EU – every lie, every drone, every provocation written down. And for every page, a proportional response: hit the economy, hit the elite and tourist visas.

In the fifth year of war, there should be no Russian citizens shopping in Milan or sunbathing in Spain. Even if Russian citizens stopped receiving tourist visas, there would still be legal pathways for asylum seekers and humanitarian visas.
This is not escalation. This is a proportional response.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, il 5 giugno scorso un drone marino ucraino ha colpito una petroliera nel porto di Costanza. I danni sono stati ingenti, ma per fortuna l'incidente non ha coinvolto civili.

Di fronte a questo scenario si sono tutti affrettati a dire che la responsabilità fosse unicamente di Mosca, come nei casi delle incursioni di droni in Finlandia e Paesi baltici, ignorando però un dettaglio fondamentale, e cioè che la Marina ucraina ha ammesso di aver allertato le autorità rumene.

Io vi chiedo: da quando invece l'Ucraina avrebbe il potere di colpire obiettivi commerciali e civili sul suolo dell'Unione europea? Se avete deciso di sacrificare la nostra sovranità, abbiate almeno il coraggio di dirlo chiaramente. State mettendo a rischio le nostre vite per alimentare questo folle conflitto.

Sono più di quattro anni che chiediamo l'istituzione di un mediatore per la pace e invece siamo ancora qui a discutere se i droni sono russi o sono ucraini. Fino a quando si continuerà a sabotare un possibile dialogo? Perché si sta giocando col fuoco, ma a rischiare, come al solito, non sono le élite, sono le vite di milioni di lavoratori e di cittadini che continuano a pagare il prezzo della vostra incapacità. Sono le centinaia di migliaia di vittime che stanno combattendo una guerra fratricida, perché in guerra muoiono i figli del popolo e non delle élite.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, verehrte Kollegen! Wenn der deutsche Luftwaffenchef Neumann erklärt, man sei bereit, heute Nacht gegen Russland zu kämpfen, dann ist das kein Zeichen politischer Stärke, sondern ein Alarmzeichen dafür, wie weit die Debatte bereits verschoben ist.

Europa braucht keine markigen Worte aus Deutschland oder sonst woher, sondern eine nüchterne, vernünftige Sicherheitsstrategie. Die Deutschen wollen keine Eskalationsspirale, keine Kriegswirtschaft und keine neuen Milliarden-Schulden-Kriegsprogramme, während die Infrastruktur, die Wirtschaft und innere Sicherheit zusammenbrechen.

Es ist hochgradig verantwortungslos, über Kämpfe heute Nacht gegen Russland zu palavern. Abschreckung mag zum Geschäft der deutschen Luftwaffe gehören, aber Diplomatie, Deeskalation und der klare Fokus auf nationale Interessen müssen Vorrang haben; früher wussten wir das. Der große Europäer Helmut Schmidt sagte: Lieber tausendmal miteinander reden als eine Minute schießen.

Wir sehen uns in dieser Tradition. Die Alternative für Deutschland, wir sagen klar: Deutschland muss verteidigungsfähig sein, aber wir werden uns nicht in eine Eskalation hineintreiben lassen, die einen Krieg immer wahrscheinlicher macht. Niemals! Die AfD ist Friedenspartei.

paragraphs.text: Ja, Herr Kollege, danke für die Frage. Ich komme nicht aus der Sowjetunion wie die Hohe Vertreterin. Ich komme aber aus der Deutschen Demokratischen Republik, und wir haben gelernt aus unserer Geschichte: Nie wieder! Und ich bin überrascht, dass Sie sich hier den Kriegstreibern in Europa derart andienen, dass Sie so eine irre Frage stellen.

Also, ich meine, was wollen wir denn machen in Europa? Wollen Sie wirklich zum großen Krieg blasen? Und dass die Linke das hier vor versammelter Mannschaft sozusagen mit erklärt, ist schon ein starkes Stück. Sie sollten nochmal in den Geschichtsbüchern nachschauen gehen.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, stimați colegi, în luna mai, o dronă ucraineană a fost găsită de niște pescari greci lângă Lefkada, recuperată ‑ putea să fie detonată în orice moment, vă dați seama ‑ și livrată armatei elene, care a și neutralizat-o. Deci, ea nu a fost detonată de ucraineni.

Mai departe, în luna iunie, 5, o altă dronă a apărut în România, dar aceasta nu era găsită în derivă. În fapt, ea s-a încurcat în niște balize în portul Constanța, după ce a urmat un drum perfect exact astfel încât să ajungă lângă cel mai important depozit de combustibili din România din portul Constanța, Oil Terminal. Nu a ajuns decât la câteva sute de metri. Și totuși, acest drum al ei nu mi se pare drumul unei drone aflate în derivă sau a uneia căreia ucrainenii i-ar fi pierdut controlul.

Deci Ucraina ne-a avertizat că această dronă urmează să fie detonată. De ce ea a fost detonată, iar drona din Grecia nu a fost detonată? De ce Ucraina și-a cerut scuze grecilor, dar românilor nu și-a cerut scuze? Noi nu suntem parteneri, noi nu avem aceleași drepturi în Uniunea Europeană? Nouă nu trebuie să ne ceară scuze și să ne dea explicații Ucraina?

paragraphs.text: Godātais sēdes vadītāj! Kolēģi! Krievija ir teroristiska valsts, kas savu agresīvo mērķu sasniegšanai pastrādā vissmagākos noziegumus. Viņi grauj, iznīcina un nogalina. Aizvakar kristīgā pasaule piedzīvoja to, kā Krievija sapostīja Pečoru klostera katedrāli. Tas ir kā sabumbot Parīzes Dievmātes katedrāli. Šis barbarisms vēlreiz apstiprina, ka Kremlis nav ticības un kristīgo vērtību aizstāvis.

Ukraina gūst panākumus savas teritorijas atbrīvošanā. Slēpjot savas neveiksmes, Krievija plaši attīsta melu, iebiedēšanas un draudu kampaņu pret kaimiņiem. Viņi vērš pret mums radioelektronisko karadarbību, novirza uz mūsu teritorijām dronus. Krievijas radītie drošības apdraudējumi nesamērīgi ietekmē Eiropas Savienības austrumu robežas dalībvalstis.

Es vēlos apsveikt Ukrainu ar pievienošanās sarunu sākumu. Šovasar Eiropai ir jāatver vēl vairākas sarunu sadaļas. Mūsu vēstījums Kremlim ir nelokāms. Mēs atbalstīsim Ukrainu, līdz tā pilnībā iekļausies Eiropas valstu ģimenē.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear Vice-President, colleagues, Russian drones are not lost. They know exactly where they are flying. Over the whole eastern flank, this is a systemic provocation, and the European response must have a common pan-European answer.

I want to name one specific vulnerability: the Ignalina nuclear power plant in Lithuania. There, the nuclear waste that is stored in temporary above-ground facilities is exposed and vulnerable. Can you imagine if something happened now? Any drone incident can trigger consequences similar to the Chernobyl catastrophe, affecting people and nature across the Union. It is very dangerous.

This is precisely why pan-European air and sea defence must move into reality: not 27 separate systems with 27 separate gaps and vulnerabilities, but one coherent integrated shield covering our sky, our Baltic and Black Seas and beyond.
Our call on the Commission and Member States is simple: urgently increase investment in this integrated shield now. The Commission and Member States must finally move from debating to acting.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, korkea edustaja Kallas, vaikka kotimaahani Suomeenkin on harhautunut drooneja, on Ukraina maksanut Venäjän hyökkäyssodan aikana kovimman hinnan puolustaessaan itsenäisyyttään. Samalla se on kuitenkin pystynyt kehittämään poikkeuksellisen vahvaa osaamista droonien torjunnassa.

Unionin tulisi käynnistää välittömästi entistä tiiviimpi yhteistyö Ukrainan kanssa oman droonipuolustuksensa kehittämiseksi. Meidän on hyödynnettävä parhaat käytännöt ja sotaoloissa toimiviksi todetut ratkaisut, jotta unionin turvallisuus voidaan varmistaa. Unionin omaa kehitys- ja tuotantokapasiteettia on vahvistettava yhdessä Ukrainan kanssa. Samalla EU:n on jatkuvasti arvioitava Venäjä-pakotteiden kohdentamista ja todellista vaikuttavuutta.

Kyse on ennen kaikkea koko Euroopan turvallisuudesta. Siksi resursseja rajaturvallisuuteen, droonipuolustukseen ja kyberhyökkäysten torjuntaan on osoitettava riittävästi. Erityisesti tämä koskee EU:n itäisiä jäsenmaita, joiden alueellista koskemattomuutta puolustamalla puolustamme koko Eurooppaa.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, I was running here, but I was listening to the speeches by Ms Kallas, and I totally understand that she can't say anything else except that we are so united.

But of course, the fact is that stating, for example, that the Spanish far-left government is helping Ukraine a lot is a joke. We know it. Ireland is still helping the Russian economy. We are so united, absolutely! I know that you can't say anything else, but we both know that it is a delusion.

Second thing, when we talk about safety in the Baltic states, Finland and Poland, when we look at the situation in Europe, we know that actually those countries have to stick together. paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear Commissioner Kallas, colleagues, Russia’s goal is not to simply breach our airspace, it is to conquer.
It is to conquer by occupying our attention, our confidence and our sense of security. This starts at an individual level, and that is why resilience also starts and begins with people.
We need stronger societal preparedness: security literacy – which is similar to media literacy – crisis awareness and civil preparedness, so that people know how to respond when threats arise.

But this requires proactive, up-to-date, clear and accessible communication from the authorities. Also, before we are in a crisis, when official channels are silent or slow, disinformation will fill in the gaps. And this is again where Russia lurks.
Resilience is built across society, in schools, in communities, public authorities and civil society, not only in barracks.
The stronger and more resilient our people and societies are, the weaker Russia’s provocations become.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, last week, in Latvia, for the first time, a NATO fighter jet shot down a drone crossing in from Russia. This is exactly what we need: our Union's borders are being defended militarily. Just as much, we must protect the people who live on those borders socially and economically. For example, in Latgale, on the EU's eastern border, tourism businesses now report mass cancellations. Hundreds of hotels, guesthouses, campsites, restaurants are now at risk of bankruptcy.

My message to the Commission is clear: border regions in the Baltics, Finland, Poland, Romania bearing the direct consequences of the war need support, and they need it now. EU budget reserves must be mobilised this year. We did it for workers affected by the closure of the Audi plant in Brussels. We did it for regions devastated by floods. Solidarity is not a slogan; it's a founding principle of the European Union.

Vi behöver ge mer stöd till Ukraina, använda deras kunskap när det gäller drönare och se till att vi stärker dem i deras vilja att försvara både sitt eget land och oss.
EU-medborgarna behöver få rätt information vid rätt tid. Vi behöver också gemensam underrättelse, och vi ska se till att vi sätter tillräckligt med pengar på försvar och säkerhet.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, High Representative, I think that what Russia does in these circumstances fits well into their strategy of testing us out. That is what is happening: they look how we are reacting, and if we are not reacting adequately, they will go further.

As a consequence, apart from working on our next sanctions package – where I hope, for instance, that we will include Russian tourists and not issue them visas, but that's another issue – I would, in this concrete case, definitely suggest that Member States agree that we start shooting down these Russian drones prior to reaching our territory.

I think we should support all those bordering Member States and all those who so wish in shooting those approaching drones down while they are still over Ukrainian territory and prior to landing on ours, or perhaps in Ukraine.
I think that would be a clear signal towards Russia: 'We mean it, stop it.' And that is the way forward, I think. Otherwise he will just test us out further.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, Vice-President, recent drone incidents and security violations along the European Union's eastern border, from the Baltic region to Romania, are a serious warning. Russia's aggression does not stop at Ukrainian borders. It directly threatens the security of European Union Member States and NATO allies.

Russia has repeatedly violated the airspace of countries on NATO's eastern border during its war against Ukraine, including by directing drones into neighbouring states. Ukraine has the full right to defend itself. We need stronger European air defence and better protection of critical infrastructure. The recent interception of a drone that entered Estonian airspace showed that NATO air policing works and keeps our citizens safe.
The European Union should adopt, without delay, a strong 21st sanctions package to further weaken Russia's war machine and bring peace closer.

Kiireellistä on vahvistaa EU:n yhteistä toimintakykyä hybridihyökkäyksiin vastaamisessa, ilmapuolustuksessa, kriittisen infrastruktuurin suojaamisessa ja myös välineellistetyn maahanmuuton torjumisessa. Dla naszych mieszkańców zamknięte lotniska, rosyjska agresja, sabotaże, drony to codzienność. To nie newsy telewizyjne. We wrześniu 2025 roku Rosja przeprowadziła kolejne zmasowane ataki dronowe. My na wschodzie Europy mierzymy się z wojną hybrydową bezustannie. Ale nie miejmy złudzeń, celem Putina jest cała Europa. Ale my tu o bezpieczeństwie kraju, o bezpieczeństwie Europy, a wychodzi polski poseł Wąsik i mówi o bezpieczeństwie propagandowych stacji i propagandowych dziennikarzy. I nie ma odwagi odpowiedzieć na pytanie o bezpieczeństwo Polski i Polaków, tylko ucieka. Tchórzostwo.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, doamnă Înaltă Reprezentantă, noaptea de 28 spre 29 mai în acest an, o dronă rusească a lovit un bloc de locuințe în Galați, orașul meu, și a rănit grav o mamă și copilul acesteia. Sute de persoane au fost evacuate. Zeci de mii de oameni panicați și pe bună dreptate, ca urmare a unui atac neprovocat, direcționat, precis pentru că, repet, a lovit centrul orașului Galați.

Acest lucru ne spune câteva lucruri. În primul rând, că există nevoia de un mecanism de solidaritate, pentru că acești oameni trebuie să simtă că există o solidaritate, inclusiv financiară de compensare, dacă e vorba de daune.

Că Rusia trebuie să primească un răspuns foarte dur, ea bombardează de doi ani de zile, la sute de metri de granița României, care este granița Uniunii Europene, care este granița NATO și acest lucru îl face băgând spaima și groaza în zeci de mii de oameni.

Și în al treilea rând, trebuie să le spunem și gălățenilor, și românilor, ca fiecărui cetățean european, că sunt apărați, că sunt protejați și ori de câte ori siguranța lor și a familiilor lor va fi pusă în discuție, Uniunea Europeană și NATO trebuie să intervină, pentru că doar așa le vom da sentimentul de garanție și de certitudine pe care îl merită.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, «La tormenta que se avecina», así tituló Churchill el primer volumen de sus memorias sobre la Segunda Guerra Mundial.

En 1939, la tormenta que se cernía sobre Europa era metafórica. En el año 2026, esta tormenta es muy concreta y llega en forma de drones rusos. En tan solo un año, Rusia ha violado impunemente el espacio aéreo de una decena de países europeos, desde las bases de submarinos franceses en el Atlántico a las centrales eléctricas de Estonia, desde bloques de pisos en Rumanía a aeropuertos civiles en Alemania. Nadie está a salvo de ser el siguiente objetivo de los drones de Putin.

Dron tras dron, los europeos no sabemos hasta cuándo vamos a tolerar ni dónde está nuestra línea roja. Desde Bruselas ya se han activado todos los programas de inversión habidos y por haber. Tenemos los recursos, pero falta lo más importante: la determinación. Ahora es el turno de que los Gobiernos nacionales respondan con contundencia a estas amenazas conjuntamente. En palabras del mismo Churchill: «esta es su hora decisiva».

interventions.text:
Señor presidente, «La tormenta que se avecina», así tituló Churchill el primer volumen de sus memorias sobre la Segunda Guerra Mundial.

En 1939, la tormenta que se cernía sobre Europa era metafórica. En el año 2026, esta tormenta es muy concreta y llega en forma de drones rusos. En tan solo un año, Rusia ha violado impunemente el espacio aéreo de una decena de países europeos, desde las bases de submarinos franceses en el Atlántico a las centrales eléctricas de Estonia, desde bloques de pisos en Rumanía a aeropuertos civiles en Alemania. Nadie está a salvo de ser el siguiente objetivo de los drones de Putin.

Dron tras dron, los europeos no sabemos hasta cuándo vamos a tolerar ni dónde está nuestra línea roja. Desde Bruselas ya se han activado todos los programas de inversión habidos y por haber. Tenemos los recursos, pero falta lo más importante: la determinación. Ahora es el turno de que los Gobiernos nacionales respondan con contundencia a estas amenazas conjuntamente. En palabras del mismo Churchill: «esta es su hora decisiva».

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy

paragraphs.text: Mr President, thank you very much for this debate. It was very interesting, especially the debate between Mr Saramo and Mr Droese (the speaker used the name Neuhoff instead of Droese) regarding what is really at stake. Are you ready to sacrifice some of the countries for the peace for others? I think it was also Churchill who said that, you know, it's like feeding a crocodile, hoping that you will be the last one to be eaten. So, I want to stress that it's actually a threat that is against all of us and we need to be vigilant here.

It is also true what Mr Gahler was saying – that Russia will test how far they can go and they will every time go further if we let them. So, I totally agree that we need to act. I also agree with the last speaker that we need to convince the Member States' governments – because not everywhere is the threat felt equally.

Also, I mean, the interesting part about the history is that, you know, it is said that history does not repeat itself, but it rhymes. So, if we don't know what has happened before, you tend to repeat the mistakes that have been done. Mr Saramo was listing some of the wars that were before the Ukraine war started. I've counted, if we take the last 100 years, at least 19 countries that Russia has attacked. None of these countries has ever attacked Russia. So that is the fundamental problem that we need to deal with.

Ms Kalniete was very well pointing out the attacks of the cultural heritage sites. Yesterday, when we had the discussion with the foreign ministers, actually, this was also raised – why are some countries rolling out the red carpet for Russian cultural representatives to participate at events at the same time when Russia is actually destroying the culture and history of others? The point that you were making them to show that they are the defenders of Christianity – the attacks that took place just two days ago on the 11th century Orthodox monastery really show that this is not the case. They can't be defenders of Christianity when they are attacking such Christian important places.

On Mr Madison running in for his speech and then leaving immediately after his speech, not being concerned about what anybody else has said – you can also say that I said that we are united. I was saying that we need to be united because not all the time we are united on these issues.

Ms Ohisalo was pointing out a very important point, which is the disinformation campaign. So, not only the war that is going on in Ukraine or the drone attacks, but we should also counter the cognitive war that Russia is waging on us – the narratives, the lies that are spread. We have in Europe the FIMI toolbox that we have really developed in order to fight these narratives, and not only in Europe, not only in front of our own publics, but actually also outside, because this is also the fight for the hearts and minds of people to convince.

Also, Ms Henriksson, like I told you, we don't need a new intelligence cell; we need to use the tools we already have. We have INTCEN, we have SIAC – these are good contact points where all the intelligence of the Member States actually also gets to the European level and to the decision-makers on the European level. I think this is very important because you only share intelligence with ones that you trust. That's why this is extremely important.
So, I'm trying to stick to the time so I get good grades from the President. Thank you very much for this debate, and I must say that I really like this new format.

paragraphs.text: Catch-the-eye procedure

interventions.text: Catch-the-eye procedure

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Rosyjskie drony naruszające przestrzeń powietrzną to nie są przecież incydenty i wszyscy na tej sali zdajemy sobie z tego sprawę. To jest szersza strategia rosyjska, która dokładnie sprawdza i testuje naszą determinację, ale również nasze bezpieczeństwo.

Rosja prowadzi jeszcze jeden rodzaj wojny. Wojny o europejskie umysły. Nie ma dnia, żeby ze Wschodu nie płynął taki sygnał i takie powątpiewanie. A po co Europa się zbroi? A po co inwestuje w przemysł zbrojeniowy? Otóż właśnie po to inwestuje, żeby się obronić przed Putinem.

Jestem z Polski i chcę bardzo podziękować za te trzy programy: program SAFE, EDIP i Military Mobility. Tu chodzi o nasze bezpieczeństwo – polskie, europejskie – ale tu chodzi również o europejski przemysł. Jeszcze parę miesięcy temu gdyby ktoś mi powiedział, że amerykańscy żołnierze będą testowali polskie drony, to bym być może w to nie uwierzył. Ale to jest fakt. I mówi się, że siła jest jedynym językiem, który rozumie tyrania. I to prawda. Ta prawda pozostaje aktualna również dzisiaj, bo Putin nie boi się deklaracji. Putin boi się siły, zdolności i determinacji, czyli bezpieczeństwa Europy.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, doamnă comisar, pornesc de la afirmația dumneavoastră - apărare colectivă. Războiul nu a început ieri, a început de patru ani. Am vorbit de zeci de ori aici. Cum apărăm flancul de est? În țara mea, au fost 90 de atacuri la proximitatea graniței. Au căzut 47 de drone, 12 numai în acest an. Ce să răspund eu cetățenilor mei? Și eu m-am născut în acel județ, Galați. Măcar ați luat o măsură de sprijin pentru familia aceea, pentru mama care-și creștea singură copilul și s-a dus noaptea la spital și are o locuință luată pe credit? Cum să creadă cetățenii că îi apărăm?

Doamna comisar, noi avem nevoie aici de fapte, nu de vorbe. S-a pierdut practic partea de negociere, dar cum lăsăm să fim nesiguri că în fiecare zi mai poate să cadă o dronă, nu e suficient să avem sancțiuni. Sancțiunile nu rezolvă protecția. Trebuie să fim apărați cei de pe flancul de est, de NATO și de Uniunea Europeană, de aceea suntem contributori la aceste două instituții.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Russia is testing us. It is testing our borders, our patience and, above all, our political will to react.
Every drone crossing into European airspace is designed to answer one question: how will Europe react? Will it hesitate like it has with supplying arms to Ukraine?

The countries of Europe's eastern frontier understand that there is no room for hesitation when it comes to confronting Russian threats or building credible defence forces. We know the true nature of Russia.

This means that Russia must be met with strength, the only language it understands – the very same strength some countries in Europe have been neglecting for decades. It is high time for all to participate in defence efforts and start treating Russia as it should: a terrorist state that is a threat for Europe.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, as Russia becomes bogged down in Ukraine, the Kremlin will seek more dramatic forms of escalation.

Its goal is to intimidate European societies into reducing support for Ukraine by presenting this as the prize of avoiding a wider war. In reality, Ukraine is exercising its inherent right to self-defence in accordance with international law, including against legitimate war-supporting targets throughout the Russian territory.
Russia alone bears responsibility for all the consequences arising from its illegal war of aggression. Ukraine cannot be expected to limit its lawful self-defence while Russia continues its attacks.

At the same time, Europe must learn from Ukraine and accelerate the development of a genuine European defence union. Our military personnel must go to Ukraine to learn firsthand, and we must invite Ukrainians here to share their unique combat experience, particularly in countering drones and other emerging threats. That is where a true European defence union with Ukraine begins.

paragraphs.text: Г-н Председател, в румънското пристанище в Констанца се взриви украински дрон, но за това беше обвинена Русия. Преди четири години украинска ракета уби двама души в Полша, но за това също беше обвинена Русия. Тези абсурдни обвинения се дължат на факта, че днес за Европейския съюз руснаците са това, което бяха евреите за нацистка Германия - виновни за всичко.

Тази седмица температурите в Страсбург ще надхвърлят 35 градуса и не се съмнявам, че за това също ще бъде обвинена Москва. С безсмислена упоритост колективният Запад не спира да търси врагове там, където ги няма и да налива милиарди в корумпирания режим на Зеленски. Евросъюзът наскоро му подари 90 милиарда евро, а предстои и НАТО да му даде още 20 милиарда.

В моята държава България правителството възнамерява драстично да намали социалните разходи. Така правят и други управляващи в Европа, защото нямало пари, казват. И същите тези управляващи винаги намират пари, които с радост подаряват на режима в Киев. Това наистина е възхвала на глупостта, сътворена не от Еразъм, а от брюкселските началници.

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, παρότι σήμερα συζητάτε για τα drones που εκτοξεύονται στο πλαίσιο της ιμπεριαλιστικής σύγκρουσης ΝΑΤΟ-Ρωσίας, προκλητικά βλέπετε μόνο αυτά που εκτοξεύει η Ρωσία. Κι ενώ, για παράδειγμα, το drone στη Ρουμανία καταγράφηκε ουκρανικό, κάνετε πως δεν ακούσατε ότι στα ανοιχτά του ελληνικού νησιού της Λευκάδας, κυρία Kallas, βρέθηκε επίσης ουκρανικό drone που στόχευε ρωσικά πολεμικά πλοία καθ’ ομολογίαν των Ουκρανών, ενώ η ελληνική κυβέρνηση συγκαλύπτει την όλη υπόθεση.

Αναβαθμίζονται χωρίς προηγούμενο οι κίνδυνοι για τον ελληνικό λαό και τεράστιες είναι οι ευθύνες της ελληνικής κυβέρνησης που τον οδηγεί στο σφαγείο, εμπλέκοντας τη χώρα ολοένα και πιο βαθιά στη στήριξη του καθεστώτος Zelenskyy και στον ιμπεριαλιστικό πόλεμο. Η δε εξαγγελία της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης για ρεσάλτο της ιμπεριαλιστικής επιχείρησης με την ψευδεπίγραφη επωνυμία «ειρήνη» σε ρωσικά πλοία στη Μεσόγειο πολλαπλασιάζει τους κινδύνους.

Ο ιμπεριαλιστικός πόλεμος στην Ουκρανία έχει προ πολλού ξεφύγει των συνόρων της και η Μεσόγειος εξελίσσεται σε πολεμικό πεδίο. Κανένας, λοιπόν, εφησυχασμός και καμία εμπλοκή στα πολεμικά σφαγεία για τα κέρδη και τα συμφέροντα των μονοπωλίων.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, doamnă comisară, „teama”, „incertitudinea”, „nesiguranța” nu mai sunt cuvinte care descriu un război îndepărtat. Sunt sentimente pe care tot mai mulți români au început să le trăiască după ce, de la începutul războiului din Ucraina, am avut zeci de încălcări ale spațiului aerian. Sunetul dronelor, al alarmelor și teama că o noapte obișnuită se poate transforma într-o tragedie au devenit o realitate în România.

Recent, o mamă și fiul ei au fost răniți la Galați, după ce o dronă rusească a lovit propria locuință, iar Rusia nu dă niciun semn că intenționează să se oprească. Dar în apărarea libertății nu există niciodată un efort prea mare. De aceea, doamnă comisară, nu putem trata securitatea flancului estic ca o problemă regională. Este o problemă europeană, iar răspunsul nostru trebuie să fie ferm. Avem nevoie azi și subliniez acest lucru ‑ azi, de capacități militare care să fie în măsură să apere în mod adecvat nu doar România, ci întreaga Uniune Europeană.
