Avem nevoie azi și subliniez acest lucru ‑ azi, de capacități militare care să fie în măsură să apere în mod adecvat nu doar România, ci întreaga Uniune Europeană.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señora vicepresidenta y alta representante de Kaja Kallas, la incursión de drones rusos con violación del espacio aéreo de nada menos que cinco Estados miembros de la Unión Europea —Rumanía, Finlandia y los tres Estados bálticos, incluido el suyo de procedencia— es un ataque y, por consiguiente, una agresión al conjunto de la Unión Europea. Como todos son miembros de la OTAN, podría escalar hasta el artículo 5 del Tratado de Washington. Y, como son miembros de la Unión Europea, apela a la cláusula de defensa mutua y colectiva del artículo 42, apartado 7, del Tratado de Unión Europea.

Pero, mientras eso llega, es mucho lo que se puede hacer y todo lo que se puede hacer ha salido en este debate y en todos los que le preceden. Para empezar, intercambiar inteligencia. En segundo lugar, incrementar la capacidad industrial para proteger mejor y, sobre todo, para disuadir de futuros ataques a los Estados miembros que ya han visto violados su espacio aéreo; integración de las capacidades industriales con valor añadido, con innovación. Y, sobre todo, en el plano militar: un incremento de la movilidad conjunta de la fuerza militar de los Estados miembros de la Unión Europea y, esperablemente, un mecanismo de interoperabilidad de las fuerzas armadas de los Estados miembros de Unión Europea.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, da, o să vă rog frumos să nu ne mai numiți flancul estic. Măcar respectați-ne, după ce v-ați bătut joc de noi în tot acest război și de când am intrat în Uniunea Europeană. Noi suntem România! Și încă ceva, stimată doamnă Kaja Kallas, când vorbiți și atacați pe ceilalți despre istorie, puneți mâna dumneavoastră și învățați istorie. Este rușinos să-i amintiți României despre Churchill, când Churchill este cel care, în octombrie 1944, a dat România pe mâna lui Stalin și a Uniunii Sovietice și ne-a tăiat în bucăți.

Mai mult decât atât, Pactul Ribbentrop-Molotov a dispus ca Basarabia și Bucovina de Nord să fie date. O parte au devenit acum Republica Moldova și acum sunt la ucraineni. Cum este posibil să vorbiți doar de drona din Galați? O dronă cu 50 de kilograme explozibil care nu a distrus blocul așa cum ar fi trebuit să fie și care au recunoscut ucrainenii că a fost trimisă, i-au schimbat traiectoria să ajungă în România? Și nu vorbiți de Constanța cu drona marina a ucrainenilor pe care au explodat-o lângă Oil Terminal, ceea ce înseamnă că vor să ne bage în război. Vă rog frumos să încetați până nu avem o investigație! Eu am cerut Organizației Națiunilor Unite...

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Przede wszystkim atak na jeden z krajów członkowskich Unii Europejskiej jest atakiem na całą Unię Europejską i musimy w tym zakresie wykazywać się stanowczością, determinacją i lojalną odpowiedzią. I tak powinno być zawsze. Tym bardziej, że mamy nasilenie ataków, jeśli chodzi o przestrzeń powietrzną, jeśli chodzi o drony, jeśli chodzi o dywersję, sabotaż, ale także wojnę informacyjną, której przykład przed chwilą widzieliśmy w pełnym putinowskim wydaniu.

Chcę bardzo wyraźnie powiedzieć, pani komisarz, że pracujemy nad mobilnością wojskową. W przyszłym tygodniu dwie komisje: komisja SEDE – Komisja Bezpieczeństwa i Obrony oraz komisja TRAN – Komisja Transportu przygotują swoją propozycję odpowiedzi, odpowiedzi Parlamentu Europejskiego, którą przegłosujemy w lipcu. Więc mobilność wojskowa i cały ten pakiet regulacyjny będzie jednym z elementów naszej stanowczej odpowiedzi na prowokacje.

paragraphs.text: Herr talman! Ryska drönares upprepade kränkningar av europeiskt luftrum är inga olyckshändelser. Tvärtom handlar det om metodiska provokationer. Varje drönare som flyger över Europas gränser är ett budskap från Kreml om att de testar vår vaksamhet, beslutsamhet och viljan att försvara våra demokratier. Under åratal har Ryssland parallellt med kriget i Ukraina flyttat fram sina positioner med cyberattacker, sabotage och desinformation.

Drönarattackerna är en del av samma strategi som syftar till att skapa rädsla, osäkerhet och splittring. Europa måste svara med styrka, aldrig med tvekan. Med enighet, aldrig med eftergifter. Historien lär oss att aggressiva regimer inte stoppas med fromma förhoppningar – de stoppas av motstånd.

Därför måste EU stärka luftförsvaret, öka stödet till Ukraina och tydligt markera att Europas gränser inte är förhandlingsbara. Vi kommer inte att låta oss skrämmas eller backa, och vi kommer aldrig att acceptera att Europas säkerhet dikteras från Moskva.

paragraphs.text: Vilija Blinkevičiūtė (S&D), raštuRusijos provokaciniai veiksmai tampa vis pavojingesni. Pasikartojantys dronų įsiveržimai mūsų Rytinių valstybių narių erdvę nėra atsitiktiniai incidentai. Tai sąmoningi mėginimai išbandyti mūsų budrumą, pasirengimą ir vienybę.Lietuvai ši grėsmė yra ypač aktuali. Rusijos karinė veikla prie mūsų sienų ir netoli strategiškai svarbių objektų kelia rimtą susirūpinimą. Ypatingą dėmesį turime skirti Ignalinos atominės elektrinės teritorijai ir kitai kritinei infrastruktūrai. Net ir vienas incidentas galėtų turėti rimtų pasekmių žmonių saugumui ir aplinkai.Negalime leisti, kad tokie oro erdvės pažeidimai taptų nauja norma. Kiekviena provokacija didina eskalacijos riziką ir silpnina tarptautine teise grindžiamą tvarką.Todėl Europos Sąjunga kartu su NATO privalo stiprinti oro gynybą rytiniame flange, plėsti radarų tinklą, investuoti į kovos su dronais sistemas ir geriau apsaugoti kritinę infrastruktūrą.Europos dangus nėra vieta Rusijos provokacijoms. Mūsų atsakas turi būti vieningas, ryžtingas ir patikimas.

paragraphs.text: Łukasz Kohut (PPE), in writingRussia has been targeting many European countries and attempted to destabilise them. A European Union, we stay united together. This time we show the unity with Romania, Baltic states and Finland. All the drones’ incidents which have happened in these countries were not exactly accidental. It has shown us that we need improvements in our drone detection and defence systems. We should have a speedy implementation of the European Drone Defence Initiative. This is why I voted in favour for this resolution.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Rihards Kols (ECR), in writingRussia’s drone incursions into Romania, Finland and the Baltic states are are deliberate tests of our nerves, our response time and our political seriousness. Each incursion tests NATO’s detection and response, maps our blind spots in low altitude radar coverage, and probes our civil protection. This is how Russia operates on NATO’s eastern flank - probing, jamming, escalating, then studying our hesitation. A drone does not need to hit a military target to achieve its purpose. It is enough to cross the border, trigger confusion, expose gaps in warning systems and leave citizens asking whether the state is ready. Russia’s drone incursions into Romania, the Baltic states and Finland have become the daily edge of war for our region. The eastern flank needs layered counter-drone defence, faster warning systems and a unified response that makes Moscow pay a high and rising price for every provocation.The lesson from these incursions is simple. If you do not harden your air defences, civil protection and critical infrastructure in time, you will be doing it in the middle of a crisis and under information attack at the same time. That is when public trust reaches its breaking point.

paragraphs.text: Mihai Tudose (S&D), în scrisPrin această rezoluție cerem întărirea coerentă a flancului estic al UE și NATO, pe întreaga sa lungime, de la Arctica la Marea Neagră. Este, implicit, o critică a atenției dezechilibrate acordate, până acum, statelor din prima linie din est, cu accent major pe zona Mării Baltice, astfel încât sunt observatori care acuză că s-a ajuns la un flanc estic cu două viteze.În fața amenințărilor aeriene neconvenționale, prioritare sunt protejarea civililor și apărarea infrastructurii critice.E nevoie, în acest sens, de sisteme eficiente de detectare și combatere a dronelor, de finanțare pentru construirea de adăposturi antiaeriene civile și renovarea celor existente, precum și de coordonare și integrare sporite ale structurilor de apărare, protecție civilă și intervenție de urgență.De la solidaritatea pe care Parlamentul European și Consiliul au exprimat-o cu România, în ceea ce privește incursiunile de drone pe teritoriul național, trebuie trecut de urgență la acțiuni concrete pentru rezolvarea vulnerabilităților pe care le-au evidențiat incidentele recente.

paragraphs.text: The next item is the debate on the report by Mr Azmani, on behalf of the Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs, on the common system for the return of third-country nationals staying illegally in the Union (Return Regulation) (COM(2025)0101 – C10‑0047/2025 – 2025/0059(COD)) (A10-0048/2026).
I would like to inform Members that there will be only one round of political group speakers for this debate. Therefore, there is no catch-the-eye procedure and no blue cards will be accepted.

I would like to inform Members that there will be only one round of political group speakers for this debate. Therefore, there is no catch-the-eye procedure and no blue cards will be accepted.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Mr, President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues, first of all, I would like to express my sincere gratitude to everyone who contributed to this file over the past months: the shadows, the secretariat, the legal services, the staff, the Cyprus Presidency, but also the Commissioner, the Commission and all the colleagues who engaged constructively throughout this process.

I am particularly grateful for the constructive cooperation that has characterised these negotiations. This was never going to be an easy file, and I knew that from the moment I was appointed as a rapporteur. There were moments when compromises seemed difficult to reach. However, through hard work, mutual trust and a shared sense of responsibility, we succeeded in delivering a balanced, legally sound and workable outcome. This final text is the product of intensive cooperation between Parliament, the Presidency and the Commission.

The Return Regulation is the last and missing piece of the Migration Pact that just entered into effect. Without an effective return policy, the Migration Pact remains incomplete. At present, only around 28% of third country nationals who have no legal right to remain in the European Union are actually returned to their countries of origin. And this situation places significant pressure on our migration and asylum systems, creates frustration among our citizens and ultimately undermines trust in our common European migration policy.

A credible migration system must rest on two equally important pillars. First, we must provide protection to those who genuinely need it. Second, we must ensure that those who do not have a right to stay effectively return. Without effective returns, the entire migration system risks losing legitimacy. And this is precisely why replacing the outdated Return Directive from 2008 was so necessary. The world has changed significantly since 2008, and our legal framework had to evolve accordingly. The Regulation before us provides a stronger and more harmonised European framework. It establishes clearer obligations for both third country nationals and Member States. It strengthens cooperation between Member States by introducing the European Return Order, an important first step towards mutual recognition of return decisions across the Union.

The Regulation also places a stronger focus on individuals who pose security threats. Ensuring the safety and security of our citizens remains one of our fundamental responsibilities. At the same time, voluntary returns remain the preferred and most sustainable solution. However, where a voluntary return does not take place, Member States must have the necessary tools to ensure that return decisions are effectively enforced. One of these tools is the newly introduced Return Hub and broader possibilities to act where there is a risk of absconding.

An equally important element is cooperation with third countries. For too long, insufficient cooperation from countries of origin has undermined return efforts. This Regulation introduces instruments that can encourage third countries to take back their own nationals. And if we are serious about increasing return rates, this cooperation is indispensable and is a key element for the majority also of this House.

As rapporteur, I have always believed that Europe needs a return system that is not only effective but also fair, legally sound, and fully consistent with our values. I believe this text achieves exactly that. As a rapporteur, I stand fully behind the text, and this demonstrates that effective migration management and respect for the rule of law are not contradictory objectives. On the contrary, they reinforce one another, and I look back with satisfaction on the cooperation among the various shadows over the past months.
Thanks to everyone's commitment and dedication, we have delivered a strong, effective and legally sound outcome. For all those reasons, I encourage colleagues to support this regulation tomorrow.

interventions.speaker_label: Magnus Brunner, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, tomorrow's vote on the Return Regulation comes a few days after the entry into application of the Pact on Migration and Asylum. Finally, there are actually no longer any missing pieces in this whole European reform – our major reform – with which we are bringing our European House in order.

Ten years ago, we did take a lot of responsibility as a European Union, but, as I always like to say, we didn't have a system, we didn't have rules – or we didn't have the right rules – and we didn't have control over what is happening in the European Union.

So now we are actually opening a new chapter with fair rules, with firm rules, with more effective rules, also, that counter abuses with a strong balance between solidarity and responsibility, with better control of our borders, also, thanks to new tools and new technology – the Entry/Exit System, for instance – and also with a stronger and more assertive migration diplomacy.

We have already taken a lot of actions, and it's actually starting to pay off. We've seen a decrease of illegal migration of 55 % in the last two years – on some routes, like the Western Balkan route, even of 90 % in the last three years. But –and that's what tomorrow is about – also, we need to get better in returning, of course, people who are in Europe without any right.

Today, as we know, only slightly more than one out of four people who have no right to stay in the European Union are actually being returned. This is just not acceptable and not sustainable. The citizens in Europe cannot accept, which I totally understand, that people don't respect our rules also. The Return Regulation, I think, is an important answer to the concerns that citizens in Europe actually have.

We will make return swifter, more effective, while also, of course, respecting the people's rights. And it will give us stronger tools to return people who don't cooperate, as you mentioned, with the authorities, if they run away from their obligation, if they do not return voluntarily, or especially if they pose a security risk to the European Union. So this regulation tells everybody that it is us and not the smugglers deciding who can stay in the in the European Union and who must leave.

I would like to thank this House and in particular, of course, you, Mr Azmani, as rapporteur, all the shadow rapporteurs, of course, and the whole negotiating teams also for their work on this key instrument. I think it is really a success.

interventions.speaker_label: François-Xavier Bellamy, au nom du groupe PPE.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, nous y sommes. Demain aura lieu le vote final sur le règlement retour. C'est la fin de plusieurs décennies d'impuissance face à l'immigration illégale et de huit longues années de blocage dans la révision de la directive retour, qui disparaîtra enfin dans quelques jours. Le droit ne protégeait que celui qui avait enfreint la loi. Désormais, nous remettons la règle à l'endroit. Quand moins de 20 % des décisions de retour en Europe sont mises en œuvre aujourd'hui, 100 % pourront l'être demain. Pas dans deux ans comme certains le voulaient, demain.

Demain, nos États retrouveront la possibilité d'expulser. Les délais de rétention seront augmentés sans limite pour les individus qui représentent un danger. Nos policiers et nos gendarmes auront enfin la base légale nécessaire pour lutter contre les passeurs. Un crime, un délit vaudra une interdiction d'entrée. Les recours ne serviront plus à retarder l'expulsion et les centres de retour mettront fin au chantage des régimes qui empêchent le retour de leurs ressortissants. Demain, il sera clair qu'on ne peut s'établir en Europe que si on y a été légalement autorisé. Rien d'exceptionnel là-dedans, simplement le retour à la règle. Nous rendons le pouvoir à nos démocraties et aux citoyens de nos pays la maîtrise de leurs frontières.

Mais il semble que certains voudraient encore interdire ce retour à la normale. Quand la discussion a buté sur cette opposition fondamentale, nous avons assumé nos responsabilités. Et c'est à partir du texte que j'ai proposé, au nom du PPE, que nous voterons demain. Et nous sommes fiers de cela, fiers de ce résultat historique qui montre que, oui, l'Europe peut changer. Que, quand les électeurs le veulent, la politique peut et doit agir pour apporter les résultats concrets dont nos pays ont tant besoin.

Je voudrais remercier tous les élus qui ont rendu possible ce changement. Vous remercier, Monsieur le Commissaire, Lieber Magnus, pour le travail que tu as fait au sein de la Commission. Remercier le Conseil et les gouvernements européens qui, presque tous, veulent tout mettre en œuvre pour appliquer ce nouveau règlement retour. Demain, chers collègues, c'est la seule question qui sera posée à chacun d'entre nous ici, qui veut vraiment rompre avec la faillite actuelle de l'Europe face à l'immigration illégale, cette faillite qui a causé tant de drames? Qui veut vraiment protéger l'état de droit et sortir de l'état de non-droit, qui voit nos États et nos juridictions impuissantes? Qui refuse que le droit d'asile soit détourné comme il l'est aujourd'hui partout? Qui croit que l'Europe peut être fidèle aux principes de la démocratie en répondant aujourd'hui à l'attente si forte des citoyens de nos pays? Chacun est devant ce choix.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Murielle Laurent, au nom du groupe S&D.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, une politique de retour n’est pas un problème en soi. Une démocratie doit mettre en œuvre ses décisions, mais elle se juge aussi à la manière dont elle les fait respecter. Aujourd’hui, nous aurions pu débattre d’un règlement rendant les retours plus efficaces tout en restant fidèle à ce qui fonde l’Union européenne: la dignité humaine. Au lieu de cela, le texte ouvre la voie à la détention des mineurs non accompagnés et de familles avec enfants; il favorise le renvoi vers des pays ne respectant pas les droits fondamentaux; il crée des hubs de retour, ces centres que l’on préfère installer loin de nos frontières pour mieux détourner le regard.

Une politique de retour n’est pas crédible parce qu’elle est plus dure. Elle ne l’est que lorsqu’elle est efficace et conforme à l’état de droit. Quand une politique échoue ailleurs, la droite européenne décide de l’importer en Europe. Certains ici ont choisi l’affichage: ils transforment ce Parlement en caisse de résonance de leur campagne nationale. Mais les vraies questions restent sans réponse: comment renforcer la coopération avec les pays d’origine? Comment rendre les retours plus efficaces?

Une Europe qui renonce à ses principes ne devient pas plus forte, elle devient simplement moins européenne. L’Europe n’a pas besoin de choisir entre l’efficacité et ses valeurs. Ce règlement, lui, fait comme si ce choix était inévitable: c’est précisément là son échec.

interventions.speaker_label: Fabrice Leggeri, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Commissaire Brunner, derrière nos débats sur l’immigration, il y a des visages. Il y a Lola, il y a Philippine, il y a les victimes de Bruxelles, de Solingen, d’Aschaffenbourg, de Munich, de Villach et de Mannheim. Partout en Europe, des familles ont vu leur vie basculer. Nous leur devons la vérité.

Ces drames n’auraient jamais dû se produire – si nos frontières n’avaient pas été transformées en passoire, si les décisions d’éloignement avaient été exécutées, si certains responsables politiques n’avaient pas fermé les yeux pendant des années sur les conséquences de l’immigration illégale… C’est précisément pour cela que l’adoption du règlement sur le retour, demain, constituera une avancée significative.

Depuis trop longtemps, la politique migratoire européenne reposait sur une logique absurde. Tout était fait pour empêcher les expulsions et presque rien pour les rendre effectives. La gauche, les ONG militantes et une partie de la Commission européenne, notamment sous l’impulsion de Mme Ylva Johansson, ont entretenu cette fuite en avant avec la complicité d’une droite dite modérée, qui a trop souvent accompagné ce mouvement au lieu de le combattre.

Pendant des années, Bruxelles a davantage protégé les clandestins contre leur éloignement que les Européens contre les conséquences de l’immigration illégale. Ce texte marque enfin un changement de cap. L’allongement de la durée maximale de rétention administrative à vingt-quatre mois – alors qu’en France certains macronistes s’enorgueillissaient de l’avoir allongé de trois à sept petits mois –, le rétablissement du délit de séjour irrégulier, la fin du caractère automatiquement suspensif de nombreux recours, l’obligation pour les migrants de coopérer à leur éloignement et la création de hubs de retour hors de l’Union européenne étaient encore impensables à Bruxelles il y a quelques années.

Après les règlements sur les pays tiers sûrs et les pays d’origine sûrs, ce vote démontre qu’une autre politique migratoire est possible, lorsque les forces du bon sens de la droite de cet hémicycle travaillent ensemble. Mais ce travail n’est pas terminé. Trop de pays refusent encore de reprendre leurs ressortissants tout en profitant des avantages accordés par l’Union – je pense notamment au régime algérien. Les visas, l’aide financière européenne et les avantages accordés par l’Union doivent désormais être conditionnés à la reprise effective de leurs ressortissants.
Mais regardons aussi nos propres échecs: en France, 1 obligation de quitter le territoire sur 7 est exécutée.

Certains, dans cet hémicycle, appartiennent à des partis qui gouvernent nos pays depuis des décennies et portent une responsabilité directe dans cette situation. Pendant des années, ils ont promis la fermeté et organisé l’impuissance; ils ont promis des expulsions et laissé les clandestins rentrer; ils ont promis le contrôle et laissé prospérer le désordre migratoire.

Nos peuples ne demandent pourtant rien d’extraordinaire: ils demandent simplement que ceux qui n’ont pas le droit d’être ici repartent, que les criminels étrangers soient expulsés et que les décisions de retour deviennent enfin des retours effectifs.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the ECR Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, this House has only two blocks on migration: common sense pro-Europeans and the far left.

The far left never wanted a real return regulation. The far left wanted endless appeals and unused detention. The far left wanted to ban return hubs. The far left opposed unlimited entry bans for terrorists and criminals. In short, they fought to preserve a dysfunctional, paralysed system that returns almost no one.

Why does the far left fight so hard to keep criminals, rapists and Islamists roaming freely on our streets? Whether social democrat, green or communist, they are all far left on migration. And many liberals have joined them.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Commissaire – cher Magnus Brunner –, mes chers collègues, l’Europe s’est construite sur un socle de valeurs solides et une conviction partagée: le respect des droits humains. Le règlement sur le retour soumis au vote demain est contraire à ces valeurs. L’Europe ne doit pas permettre le renvoi de familles avec enfants vers des pays à l’autre bout du monde, avec lesquels elles n’ont aucun lien et sans garantie des droits humains.

Se résoudre à approuver un tel dispositif sous la pression de l’extrême droite serait un aveu d’échec pour l’Europe et une ligne rouge franchie par ce Parlement. En 2024, nous avons abouti sur un ensemble de dix textes à la fois fermes, efficaces et respectueux des droits humains: le pacte sur la migration et l’asile. Aujourd’hui, nous prenons le risque de tout renverser. Nous prenons le risque de mettre à mal l’efficacité du pacte. Il est encore possible d’éviter cela.
Chers collègues, soutenez l’amendement pour protéger les enfants en les excluant de ces renvois, comme la Commission nous l’avait d’ailleurs proposé initialement! L’Europe vaut mieux que cela.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, mes chers collègues, nous avons été nombreux à être choqués par les violences commises par l’ICE aux États-Unis: des familles déchirées, des enfants terrorisés, une logique d’enfermement toujours plus généralisée. Eh bien demain, vos proches, les gens que vous aimez, pourraient vivre les mêmes erreurs.

Nous voyons déjà où mènent les politiques inhumaines. «Vous, Européens, vous nous envoyez ici pour qu’on nous oublie. Car nous ne sommes pas des humains pour vous.» Ce sont les mots qu’un retenu m’a confiés lors de ma visite du centre italien en Albanie. Un endroit où les personnes sont désignées par des numéros, un centre au milieu des montagnes, loin de tout regard, où le registre des incidents fait état de tentatives de suicide chaque semaine.

Voter ce règlement sur le retour, fruit d’une collaboration assumée entre le PPE et l’extrême droite, c’est cautionner cette déshumanisation, c’est approuver l’enfermement de familles vers des centres qui bafouent la dignité humaine, où, par votre volonté, aucun mécanisme de surveillance des droits fondamentaux ne sera créé. Sans contrôle, ces personnes seront seules face à tous les abus possibles, dans de véritables zones de non-droit.
Mes chers collègues, soyez à la hauteur des valeurs qui fondent l’Union européenne. Défendez les droits. Défendez le droit. Votez contre ce règlement.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señor comisario, este Parlamento está a punto de aprobar un Reglamento que permite encerrar a niñas y niños sin haber cometido ningún delito hasta treinta meses y, en algunos casos, de forma indefinida.

Lo llaman Reglamento sobre el Retorno, pero en realidad es el remate de una triple traición. La primera traición fue a los principios. El Pacto sobre Migración y Asilo nació para construir un programa de solidaridad común entre los Estados miembros, pero se ha convertido en el esqueleto perfecto sobre el que montar una maquinaria de deportaciones masivas. Chao a la solidaridad.

La segunda traición fue a los valores. Han pasado de hablar de acogida y de protección para hablar exclusivamente en este Parlamento y en la Comisión de detenciones y de expulsión. Han normalizado acuerdos con Gobiernos que no respetan los derechos humanos. Han externalizado responsabilidades y fronteras. Este Reglamento permite construir centros en terceros países fuera del territorio de la Unión que no respetan los derechos humanos, Guantánamos europeos donde deportar personas fuera de cualquier control judicial efectivo. Y están llegando al punto de sentarse con los talibanes para que formen parte de este sistema que se ha montado aquí, con los talibanes, que son terroristas. ¿Dónde quedan nuestros valores?

La tercera traición ha sido política. La derecha europea ha decidido asumir el marco ideológico de la ultraderecha. Nadie les votó para eso, señores del Partido Popular Europeo, nadie, estoy segura. Han sido secuestrados ideológicamente por la extrema derecha y este Reglamento es el resultado: un ICE europeo para identificar, para detener y para expulsar al estilo de Trump. Ya no es la extrema derecha la que se adapta a Europa, ahora es Europa la que se está adaptando a los ultras.

Lo que vamos a votar no es un Reglamento inocente. No lo es. Es un balance sobre qué queda del proyecto europeo. Porque Europa no nació para levantar una maquinaria de expulsión, ni para distinguir entre qué personas merecen derechos y cuáles pueden ser desechadas. Numerosas instituciones, incluida la ONU, han cuestionado esta norma y, por eso, lo decimos alto y claro: no vamos a parar hasta derogar este Reglamento que es cruel.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Elf Jahre mussten vergehen, bevor man in diesem EU-Elfenbeinturm endlich begonnen hat, die Folgen der unkontrollierten Massenmigration ernst zu nehmen. Elf Jahre auch, in denen Eltern ihre Kinder verloren haben; elf Jahre, in denen Frauen Opfer von Tätern wurden, die niemals hätten hier sein dürfen. Diese Jahre werden in die Geschichte eingehen, und die Verantwortlichen haben sich damit selbst in Stein gemeißelt.

Diese Rückführungsverordnung markiert den Wendepunkt, den ersten Schritt in die richtige Richtung. Nach der morgigen Abstimmung kann auch Deutschland bereits in diesem Sommer potenzielle Abkommenspartner suchen, Rückführungszentren vorbereiten und endlich Druck auf Drittstaaten ausüben, die ihre illegalen Migranten nicht zurücknehmen wollen – über Entwicklungshilfe, Visa und Handelspolitik.

Und wir als AfD werden ganz genau schauen, ob Friedrich Merz das umsetzt und endlich mal sein Wort hält. Der morgige Tag zeigt auch, was für uns Bürger Gutes entstehen kann, wenn man endlich seine parteipolitische Feigheit ablegt.

interventions.speaker_label: Magnus Brunner, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, first of all, thanks very much for the debate.

To make that clear, it has nothing to do with politically being left or right. It has to do with pragmatism, and it is clear that for our migration and asylum systems to work, we need fast returns, effective returns of irregular migrants.

The new return regulation, in my view, does exactly this and gives us control over who can stay in the European Union and who needs to leave the European Union, while, of course, respecting human rights, people's rights, international law, of course – that is also in the regulation.

This is, I think, what the citizens in Europe expect, and this is what we are delivering. I think it's a really important part of the new chapter I was talking about and the new chapter we were working on.

Also, third countries have to play a role, of course. They also have an obligation to re-admit their citizens. And that's why we want to focus on the external dimension more in the next months. We should definitely use all our leverage that we have as a European Union, be it visa, be it trade, be it also financial tools, for example. And we should also develop new ones, definitely.

I think all together we should keep this momentum. There is no time to waste. So as soon as the regulation will be adopted, I will start working very closely with the Member States to apply the new rules.
So thank you very much for the debate again and all the best.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, thank you also to all colleagues for their contributions to this debate.
As expected, we have heard different views across the Parliament today, which I think it's also healthy in a democratic parliament, especially on a file as sensitive and important as return policy.

To colleagues who have expressed concerns regarding fundamental rights, let me be very clear: effective returns and the protection of fundamental rights can go hand in hand. Throughout these negotiations, Parliament worked hard to ensure that this regulation remains fully anchored in the rule of law and our European values.

But a migration system in which return decisions are issued but not implemented is neither fair nor credible. It's unfair to those who genuinely need protection, it's unfair to Member States carrying the burden, and it's really unfair to our citizens who expect European rules to be enforced. We should also be honest that no return system can function without effective cooperation with third countries. This is about shared responsibility and ensuring that migration management works in practice.

And as rapporteur, I firmly believe that the text before us reflects the right balance between effectiveness, legal certainty and fundamental rights. It's the result of months of difficult negotiating and carefully crafted compromises. Legislation is all about finding common ground and delivering workable solutions for Europe. And that has always been my motivation, ever since I worked on migration in the national parliament, and when I came to Brussels in 2019.
I therefore once again invite colleagues to support this regulation tomorrow.

Trzeba skończyć z bezprawiem, a Ci którzy nielegalnie dostali się na teren Unii muszą mieć świadomość, że ich też obowiązuje prawo.

To krok w stronę normalności, w kierunku zerwania ze zbankrutowaną europejską polityką migracyjną, powrotu do zasad, które dla mojego obozu politycznego i dla zdecydowanej większości Polaków od zawsze były oczywiste.W czasie, gdy Bruksela i Berlin forsowały kolejne rozwiązania osłabiające kontrolę nad migracją, my konsekwentnie powtarzaliśmy, że państwo musi kontrolować własne granice. To państwo, a nie przemytnicy ludzi, nie brukselscy urzędnicy, musi decydować o tym, kto może przekroczyć jego granice, kto może pozostać na jego terytorium, a kto powinien je opuścić.Przez lata unijne elity budowały dysfunkcyjny system oparty na absurdalnej logice „Herzlich Willkommen” i „Wir schaffen das”. System, który wpuścił do Europy miliony migrantów, a w którym wykonywana jest zaledwie co czwarta decyzja powrotowa.Przez dekady niewyobrażalne było skuteczne wydalanie nielegalnych migrantów. Niewyobrażalne było, by przestępstwo skutkowało zakazem ponownego wjazdu. Niewyobrażalne było rozbijanie siatek przemytników ludzi, przełamanie szantażu państw odmawiających przyjmowania własnych obywateli czy tworzenie centrów powrotowych poza granicami Unii Europejskiej.Dzisiejsze głosowanie nie rozwiązuje wszystkich problemów. Nie naprawia całego szkodliwego systemu, który przez lata nagradzał nielegalną migrację, a karał państwa próbujące chronić własne granice. Potrzebne są kolejne działania. Potrzebujemy odrzucenia mechanizmu relokacji i przymusowej solidarności.

To państwo, a nie przemytnicy ludzi, nie brukselscy urzędnicy, musi decydować o tym, kto może przekroczyć jego granice, kto może pozostać na jego terytorium, a kto powinien je opuścić.Przez lata unijne elity budowały dysfunkcyjny system oparty na absurdalnej logice „Herzlich Willkommen” i „Wir schaffen das”. System, który wpuścił do Europy miliony migrantów, a w którym wykonywana jest zaledwie co czwarta decyzja powrotowa.Przez dekady niewyobrażalne było skuteczne wydalanie nielegalnych migrantów. Niewyobrażalne było, by przestępstwo skutkowało zakazem ponownego wjazdu. Niewyobrażalne było rozbijanie siatek przemytników ludzi, przełamanie szantażu państw odmawiających przyjmowania własnych obywateli czy tworzenie centrów powrotowych poza granicami Unii Europejskiej.Dzisiejsze głosowanie nie rozwiązuje wszystkich problemów. Nie naprawia całego szkodliwego systemu, który przez lata nagradzał nielegalną migrację, a karał państwa próbujące chronić własne granice. Potrzebne są kolejne działania. Potrzebujemy odrzucenia mechanizmu relokacji i przymusowej solidarności.

paragraphs.text: Katri Kulmuni (Renew), kirjallinenEsitys yhteisen järjestelmän perustamisesta unionissa laittomasti olevien kolmansien maiden kansalaisten palauttamiseksi ei ole kaikilta osin ongelmaton, mutta sen tavoitteet ovat kuitenkin tarpeellisia. Perusongelma tämän kysymyksen kohdalla on se, että turvapaikkajärjestelmää on jo pitkään käytetty siirtolaisuuden väylänä Eurooppaan. Tämä ei ole järjestelmän tarkoitus eikä järjestelmä nykyisellään sellaista kestä, vaan lailliselle ja lähinnä työperäiselle maahanmuutolle on omat kanavansa.Käytännössä esitys helpottaisi laittomasti EU:n alueella olevien henkilöiden palauttamista, kun yhden jäsenmaan tekemä palautuspäätös tunnustettaisiin toisissakin maissa. Esitys mahdollistaa myös EU:n ulkopuolella olevien palautuskeskusten perustamisen. Turvapaikkapolitiikka on silti ensi sijassa jokaisen jäsenmaan omassa päätösvallassa. On myös hyvä muistaa, että jokainen tapaus on tietysti yksilöllinen, ja on pyrittävä ratkaisuihin, joissa erityisesti pienten lasten ja muiden hauraimmassa asemassa olevien ihmisten oikeudet turvataan käytännön tilanteissa.

paragraphs.text: Marcin Sypniewski (ESN), na piśmieRozmawiamy dziś o fundamencie bezpieczeństwa naszych państw. Dotychczasowa unijna polityka powrotów była fikcją- urzędniczą niemocą, którą nielegalni imigranci po prostu wyśmiewali. Czas z tym skończyć.Popieramy ten raport, ponieważ wprowadza on rozwiązania, o które od dawna zabiegamy. Koniec z bezkarnością osób, które odmawiają współpracy, ukrywają dokumenty i podają fałszywe tożsamości. Kto łamie prawo i nie współpracuje, musi ponieść tego natychmiastowe konsekwencje – w tym utratę świadczeń socjalnych i rozszerzenie zakazu wjazdu.Kluczowe jest dla nas drastyczne zaostrzenie przepisów wobec osób stanowiących zagrożenie dla bezpieczeństwa. Możliwość przetrzymywania ich w detencji do 24 miesięcy oraz bezterminowe zakazy wjazdu to jedyna skuteczna metoda ochrony naszych obywateli.Nielegalna imigracja musi spotykać się z twardą, natychmiastową deportacją.

paragraphs.text: Ивайло Вълчев (ECR), в писмена формаУважаеми колеги,Трябва да приемем законодателната резолюция, с която да уредим обща система за връщане на нелегалните имигранти, които пребивават незаконно на територията на Съюза.Това трябваше да се случи много отдавна, но мнозинството в ляво се противопоставяше, въпреки очевидната нужда от мерки срещу нелегалната миграция и репатрирането на нелегалните имигранти. Вместо това те ни предложиха да ги оставим в Европа, да безчинствата, както се случи на коледния базар Кьолн, да застрашават живота на нашите жени и деца.Тази криза с нелегалната миграция доведе до това, че темата стана основна в нашите общества, а те ясно показаха, че искат всеки, който не бяга от война да бъде върнат в родината му. Всеки, който е нарушил нашата граница и е преминал нелегално, да бъде върнат в родината му. Аз съм и ще продължа да бъда застъпник на тази идея, защото Европа има нужда от сигурност и ред. А не от милион нелегални имигранти, които не са лекари и инженери, както ни убеждава левицата, а са хора, които веднага се присъединиха към криминалния контингент. България е държава на първа линия, граница на Европейския съюз. Надявам се този регламент да е стъпката към спирането на нелегалната миграция.Благодаря.

paragraphs.text: Commissioner, both you and I agree that European businesses should spend their time on their customers, on innovation and on creating jobs – not on paperwork. I would like to ask you a question on the 'one in, two out' principle, because that is just about that: you deduct two euros for every euro that is added with legislation, which is added on the costs of SMEs, not least.

This is, of course, from EPP, something that we promised our voters in the election campaign. We have been pushing for that, and happily, we now have a majority in this Chamber because we voted for it together. And that is why I would like to ask you, Commissioner, when the Commission will follow this elected House and work according to the 'one in, two out' principle.

interventions.speaker_label: Valdis Dombrovskis, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, so first, on this 'one in, two out' question, the Commission introduced the 'one in, one out' mechanism to simplify and reduce administrative burdens for businesses in 2022. In 2025, we strengthened our efforts further and also introduced ambitious targets to reduce administrative burdens by at least 25 % for all companies, and by 35 % for SMEs. In terms of magnitude of cost savings, this goes beyond what would be typically achieved using this 'one in, two out' approach.

During 2025, the Commission tabled proposals estimated to cut EUR 15 billion of administrative costs per year, and that is a net result of EUR 15.25 billion of cost savings and EUR 247 million on additional costs, meaning that these savings arising from existing stock of administrative burden are already significantly larger than the net reductions would typically result from 'one in, two out' approach if you look solely at new regulatory costs.

However, what I wanted to emphasise in this regard is also the necessity to follow it through by the co‑legislators. Of the 10 omnibus proposals we note that on a number of omnibus proposals in the legislative process the ambition for simplification is actually substantially watered down. And then we can pursue 'one in, two out' or aim for a 25 % burden reduction, or pursue other approaches – we will not arrive at meaningful burden reduction. So it is very important that what we are putting on the table in terms of ambition for simplification is actually followed through in the legislative process.

In 2025, we strengthened our efforts further and also introduced ambitious targets to reduce administrative burdens by at least 25 % for all companies, and by 35 % for SMEs. In terms of magnitude of cost savings, this goes beyond what would be typically achieved using this 'one in, two out' approach.

During 2025, the Commission tabled proposals estimated to cut EUR 15 billion of administrative costs per year, and that is a net result of EUR 15.25 billion of cost savings and EUR 247 million on additional costs, meaning that these savings arising from existing stock of administrative burden are already significantly larger than the net reductions would typically result from 'one in, two out' approach if you look solely at new regulatory costs.

However, what I wanted to emphasise in this regard is also the necessity to follow it through by the co‑legislators. Of the 10 omnibus proposals we note that on a number of omnibus proposals in the legislative process the ambition for simplification is actually substantially watered down. And then we can pursue 'one in, two out' or aim for a 25 % burden reduction, or pursue other approaches – we will not arrive at meaningful burden reduction. So it is very important that what we are putting on the table in terms of ambition for simplification is actually followed through in the legislative process.

paragraphs.text: Thank you, Commissioner, yes, I think it is really important that we follow through from this House as well. I was the rapporteur for the first omnibus, and there we actually cut more costs than the Commission did. So we did increase in that sense the cost-cutting for businesses.

You say that what you are doing now is more than 'one in, two out', so I would like to ask you, what do you aim for? Is it 'one in, three out' or 'one in, five out'? What can we know about the mandate as such, these five years? What is your aim?
And finally, could we also have it done and calculated on the total regulatory burden, not only on the administrative burden? Because of course, that is what counts for businesses.

interventions.speaker_label: Valdis Dombrovskis, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: On this, what I'm saying, in a sense we are following a different approach. So 'one in, one out' would mean being stable in terms of administrative burden: not adding to it, but also not reducing. So aiming for 25 % reduction of administrative burden and 35 % reduction for SMEs goes substantially beyond it. I'll use this 2025 example: if we have EUR 15 billion reductions, which is a result of EUR 15.25 savings and EUR 247 million increases, 'one in, two out' in the same would translate to EUR 500 million decreases. EUR 15 billion is obviously substantially much more, so that's why we're saying that with this 25 % burden reduction, we are going beyond this approach. But we are measuring it differently; we are measuring it based on existing burden.

Obviously there are also other ways to look at the cost, not only administrative burden. And there have been also certain papers produced by the Danish and Cypriot presidencies of the Council looking at what they call 'the cost of legislation' when we can have this kind of more holistic view, also looking at the adjustment costs. For purposes of simplification, we are focusing on administrative burden because the adjustment costs, more often than not, imply also changes in policies or changes in policies' targets, in a sense something that goes beyond strictly the simplification exercise.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor comisario Dombrovskis, reducir las cargas administrativas para las pequeñas y medianas empresas es un objeto fuera de discusión. Efectivamente, es un objetivo inobjetable pero para que sea importante de verdad es preciso mantener las ayudas. Porque no hay pequeña y mediana empresa que quiera que le reduzcan las cargas administrativas a costa de destruir los programas de los que se ha venido beneficiando, por ejemplo, el programa COSME.

Y, en particular, esto es importante en las regiones menos desarrolladas o en las regiones con dificultades especiales como es el caso de las regiones ultraperiféricas. El programa COSME ha ayudado a las pequeñas y medianas empresas, en regiones ultraperiféricas como Canarias, a su sostenibilidad.

Por tanto, la pregunta es: ¿es posible garantizar la permanencia de esas ayudas que son componentes del pilar social europeo en el próximo marco financiero plurianual y, consiguientemente, en los presupuestos que vienen?

Y la segunda pregunta es: es particularmente importante reducir las cargas administrativas en la pesca artesanal que se queja del cuaderno digital, que es absolutamente incompatible con sus condiciones de trabajo. ¿Alguna vez la Comisión Europea escuchará propuestas tan razonables como reducir esas cargas administrativas a la pesca artesanal?

paragraphs.text: Thank you for those questions. In terms of overall burden reduction, we set our targets very clearly at the beginning: a 25% administrative burden reduction for all companies, 35% for SMEs. We also quantified it, our estimate is that this 25% target corresponds to an annual administrative burden reduction of EUR 37.5 billion.

So the legislative proposals, the ten omnibus proposals and some further simplification proposals which are on the table, they generate savings of some EUR 15 billion. Therefore, one can say we have had a strong start in terms of our simplification agenda, one that is acknowledged by the business community.

But to reach our EUR 37.5 billion burden reduction target, we need to continue with more or less the same pace also going forward. That certainly will mean that we need to put forward more omnibus proposals and two further proposals will actually follow next week on energy products and taxation.
All in all, in this year's Commission work programme, we have more than half of all proposals with a significant simplification dimension, meaning generating net savings of administrative costs.

You also asked when businesses will start to feel all these differences. So far, only three omnibus packages are part of the EU rulebook, so businesses will start feeling those ones. There are political agreements on some more, and further omnibus packages are still in the legislative process and obviously businesses are not feeling the alleviation yet.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar Dombrovskis! Viele Unternehmen in Europa verzweifeln inzwischen an der bürokratischen Last aus Brüssel. Über Jahrzehnte hat europäische Regulierung den Binnenmarkt gestärkt, weil aus 27 nationalen Regeln eine europäische Regel wurde.

Aber spätestens seit dem Green Deal erleben wir eine starke Zunahme von Berichtspflichten, Nachweisen, oft auch ohne erkennbaren Mehrwert. Hinzu kommen Zielkonflikte. Wir wollen zum Beispiel die Energiewende, Klimaschutz und brauchen dafür einen schnellen Netzausbau; gleichzeitig verzögern andere Regelwerke wie etwa die Flora-Fauna-Habitat-Richtlinie und ein ganzes anderes Dutzend an Umweltschutzbestimmungen genau diese Projekte.

Deshalb ist meine Frage an Sie: Sind Sie bereit, vollharmonisierte europäische Regelungen mit Verschlechterungsverbot vorzulegen, die genau solche Zielkonflikte auflösen und für einen – möglicherweise befristeten – Zeitraum konkurrierende Vorschriften zurückstellen, wenn sie etwa den Ausbau überragend wichtiger Infrastruktur verhindern oder verzögern?

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Valdis Dombrovskis, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Thank you for this question. I would say it basically boils down to the question on the pace of permitting for strategic projects, and we have been working a lot on this.

Last December, as part of the Environmental Omnibus, we proposed a regulation streamlining environmental assessments to ensure that project developers across strategic sectors benefit from those accelerated procedures.

We complemented this also with specific rules catering to certain sectors. So the proposed grids package contains significant facilitations which add to those already present in the Renewable Energy Directive. The Industrial Accelerator Act puts forward accelerating permitting, again building on the Net Zero Industry Act, which harmonised industrial permitting with deadlines for procedures, single points of contacts and so on.

The Commission recently also published guidance on certain elements of Natura 2000, the Birds Directive and the Water Framework Directive, increasing the clarity on existing flexibilities and helping more uniform implementation, including during the permitting of these new projects. As a next step, we will be stress-testing the Birds and Habitats Directives to assess whether they remain fit to achieve their objectives in a cost-effective way and reduce any unnecessary administrative burdens.

paragraphs.text: Yes, so thank you for this question. Yes, we are monitoring the impact of our simplification agenda specifically on SMEs and our assessments that out of this EUR 15 billion burden reduction for all companies, SMEs will specifically benefit from a burden reduction of at least EUR 6 billion.

And there are many instances where we make it very tangible for SMEs, like under corporate sustainability reporting: SMEs are exempted from reporting obligations and also, I should say, dealing with this passing-through effect when larger companies or banks impose their reporting requirements on SMEs because they need it for their reporting, so addressing also this issue. Under CBAM: we simplify it for small importers. Under InvestEU: we streamline the procedure for SMEs. Small farmers are set to receive support, so a simplified payment scheme, also streamlined controls. So I can give many examples like this.

And on small mid-caps. Well, you already mention, we had our small mid-caps omnibus, where we are basically extending many of the simplifications which we have for SMEs also to the small mid-caps. So basically, creating a situation where mid-caps or SMEs, when they are growing, they do not face this sudden threshold effect that then suddenly they are subject to the same reporting and other obligations as large companies. So we created this in-between category exactly for this, allowing also our scale-ups to grow and to develop in Europe.

paragraphs.text: Fru formand! Mange tak for det og tak, fordi De er her, Dombrovskis, det må jo næsten være som at være til eksamen og være oppe i fuldt pensum.
SMV'erne i Danmark bruger 7,4 timer om ugen på bureaukrati. Samlet svarer det til 162 millioner timer om året og en regning, der svarer til ca. 53 milliarder danske kroner.

Meget af denne byrde stammer jo ikke fra EU-lovgivningen, men som min erfaring som tidligere formand for Folketingets Europaudvalg ved, så handler det jo om national "gold-plating", altså det, som også hedder overimplementering. Altså når medlemslandene hævder, at de implementerer 1 til 1, men så går de langt, langt længere end det.

Kommissionen nævner gold-plating i Better Regulations-meddelelsen fra april, "One Europe, One Market", og køreplanen, ja, jeg synes, den virker tam, og der mangler klart tilsagn om at stoppe det. Vil Kommissionen forpligte sig konkret på handlingsplanen med bindende nationale mål, og hvordan vil man systematisk afdække, hvor medlemslandene går videre end det, EU kræver?

interventions.speaker_label: Valdis Dombrovskis, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Thank you for this question. Indeed, gold-plating is one of the elements which have been identified also by our leaders as something which harms the smooth functioning of the single market because, if Member States introduce wider, stricter rules or obligations that go beyond the EU's requirements, they are also fragmenting the single market.
Therefore, also in our recent Communication on a simpler, clearer and better enforced EU rulebook, we announced measures to tackle gold-plating through better detection, follow-up and prevention.

On detection, we plan to use consultations, including through implementation dialogues and reality checks. We will also obtain information from enforcement investigations in the context of single market focus areas for enforcement and also systematic issues through our SOLVIT system and so on.

We will also flag potential gold-plating risks to Member States early on, during the transposition period, when Member States are preparing the transposition of directives in which we say 'look, that is gold-plating'.
In terms of follow-up, we will use the Single Market Enforcement Taskforce and also the European Semester.

To improve prevention of gold-plating we are developing a toolkit with criteria for Member States to help identify and avoid gold-plating in the national transposition and implementation of EU legislation.

So we are taking this issue very seriously and will be following up, notably also regarding what we mentioned in the context of a single market, namely areas where gold-plating would amount to breaching EU law. We would also not hesitate to launch infringement procedures to address it also through enforcement.

paragraphs.text: Commissioner, the Commission has rightly committed itself to reducing unnecessary burdens for European businesses. However, many companies are concerned about the implementation of the Empowering Consumers Directive. While they support the objective of combating greenwashing, the current interpretation appears to require even products that were lawfully placed on the market before September 2026 to comply immediately with the new labelling and claims requirements, without a sell‑through or grandfathering period. How does this approach fit with the Commission's commitment to simplification and regulatory predictability for businesses?

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Valdis Dombrovskis, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Concerning this directive on empowering consumers for the green transition, it was enacted by co‑legislators in February 2024, and it will apply from 27 September 2026. So, in a sense, there has been already a phase-in period of two and a half years, allowing Member States and companies to prepare. The Commission provided further guidance on this in May, and we fully recognise the importance of ensuring that the implementation of this directive is proportionate, allowing companies sufficient time to adapt. We are very well aware of the transitional implementation challenges raised in relation to certain what we call 'old stock' products, meaning products already produced prior to the application date.

To address this valid issue, early this year, the Commission organised a workshop with national authorities responsible for enforcing consumer protection rules, and we also took good note of the view of business associations, consumer organisations and enforcement authorities, which are all there. We fully support legal certainty for traders who act in good faith, and we need to avoid disproportionate outcomes, including unnecessary administrative burden or avoidable waste. To achieve this, we are now working with national authorities in developing what is called a common understanding on enforcement, including notably as regards those 'old stock' products. And this common understanding will be published this month or July at the very latest, so ahead of the application date, providing how this 'old stock' issue will be dealt with in a proportionate way.

If you look at the two overarching priorities for this Commission's mandate, which we set, one is competitiveness of the European economy, and another is security and defence, and we are following through on both of those priorities as a matter of urgency.

As I have been mentioning at the beginning, we had made for a strong start in terms of our simplification agenda with 10 omnibus proposals this year, and we intend to continue with pace and purpose going forward. So, from the Commission side, we are certainly continue to pursue this agenda and do not intend to stop, and listen carefully to input, which we are getting from the businesses, from different stakeholders to identify the issues and find the best ways to address them and to reduce excessive and unnecessary administrative burdens.

paragraphs.text: Commissioner Dombrovskis, put yourself in the shoes of the SMEs in Ireland South that I represent. They measure the success of their business, or whether it will survive or not, by the profit margin, the revenue remaining after the SME has deducted its operating costs. They measure KPIs, key performance indicators, in order to survive.

My question to you, Commissioner, is, a year and a half into your role, how do you measure your KPIs? How have you measured them thus far, a year and a half on? How are you measuring them, and what will be the measure of your success and your huge ambition that you have outlined to us by 2029, the end of the mandate? Because, quite frankly, references to omnibus and deep-clearing and everything else that we have heard about, that means nothing to the SMEs of Ireland, who have told the chartered accountants that seven out of ten of them are more pessimistic than six months ago, rising costs are impacting on them, especially labour costs, and the biggest challenge is the topic of this conversation: reducing the regulatory and the compliance burden on them. So, please produce the results of your success.

paragraphs.text: Poštovana predsjedavajuća, povjereniče, europska poduzeća, a posebno mala i srednja poduzeća, danas od Europe ne traže nove strategije i neće mjeriti naš uspjeh prema broju objavljenih akcijskih planova, nego prema tome koliko smo pravila mi doista pojednostavili.

Upravo smo zato u HOUS odboru i predložili cilj da se građevinske dozvole izdaju u roku od 60 dana kroz potpuno digitalizirane procedure, ali i zatražili smo da se predstavi paket za pojednostavljenje stanovanja.

Stoga moje pitanje je vrlo konkretno – s obzirom da nam danas nedostaje preko 10 milijuna stanova za naše mlade ljude, za profesore, vatrogasce, medicinsko osoblje i znamo da nam mladi ljudi sve kasnije i kasnije odlaze od roditelja, zanima me da li će predstojeći paket za pojednostavljenje stanovanja, najavljen za 2027. godinu, uključivati europski cilj izdavanja dozvola u roku od 60 dana te koje konkretne mjere Komisija planira predložiti kako bi države članice ubrzale postupke koji danas usporavaju gradnju prijeko potrebnih stanova jer bez ovih ubrzavanja procedura i umanjenja birokracije nema ni priuštivih stanova za naše mlade.

paragraphs.text: Yes, indeed, that is a very pertinent question. And of course, when we discuss housing, it's traditionally seen as primarily the issue for local governments or regional governments or Member States, and less so of the European Union. But it is now also more on the radar of the European Union because, indeed, access to affordable housing is a issue we see in many Member States.

And that is why we also came forward with the Affordable Housing Action Plan, to see how to address it. And our primary point in this action plan is that it has to be addressed through the supply side. So we need a larger supply of housing and affordable housing, which obviously brings us to the questions of permitting and the possibility to speed up development of this affordable housing.

Well, specifically on housing simplification, we are preparing a housing simplification proposal for the second quarter of 2027, so it's in the pipeline. I cannot at this stage preview the content of this package because it is in the early stages of development. And also, during this European Semester cycle, we were putting, for a number of Member States where we see it particularly acutely, the questions of access to affordable housing also in the country-specific recommendations, and will be engaging with Member States on how they are addressing those recommendations in this regard.

paragraphs.text: Thank you for this question. You mentioned specifically the situation of farmers. That's why we had the agricultural omnibus, where we specifically came with a number of proposals, including simplifying the controls, moving to the principle of one on-site control per year, and so on and so forth, so that is something which is already done. The 'think first' principle – that is something we outlined in our better regulation communication, and obviously it's important that we are applying this moving forward, and as a Commission with this better regulation communication, we are committed to do so.

But it is also important that, during the legislative process, this stays, and also that when we are looking at impacts of also proposals which co-legislators introduced during the legislative process, that the impact of those proposals, substantial amendments is being assessed, so that we do informed decision-making and do not arrive at unintended consequences and unnecessary burdens. So, I think it is our joint responsibility to ensure the quality of European law-making, and that is what we are committing to do.

Maybe just to give you one concrete example on a state of play specifically for farmers, I was mentioning that I am concerned with the state of play of several omnibuses, including a food and feed safety omnibus, where we, for example, proposed record-keeping simplification for farmers as part of this omnibus. Now, in a co-legislative process, this simplified record-keeping for farmers is completely removed.

So, on one hand there is lots of discussions like 'we need simplification', lots of calls on the Commission, 'please come with the proposals'. We come with the proposals and then we see many of those implications just disappearing in the legislative process. That is indeed concerning. And I call on you also as Members who are, you know, willing to push this simplification agenda forward to pay close attention to this – that we are not watering down this simplification agenda also during the legislative process.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, quiero expresar mi agradecimiento a los ponentes alternativos, ha sido un placer trabajar con ellos, y pido el apoyo para las actualizaciones que votaremos mañana en el informe.

En el corazón de todo proceso de adhesión están los estándares democráticos, por eso en cada informe de progreso también deben estarlo. Ser el ponente de Turquía es muy frustrante. Mis colegas que lidian con otros países a veces tienen buenas noticias. Yo llevo diez años sin buenas noticias. De hecho, Turquía es el país candidato cuyos estándares democráticos más se han deteriorado en los últimos años —consecuencia de una absoluta falta de voluntad política de ser coherentes con las ocasionales declaraciones proeuropeas de las autoridades—.

No son declaraciones lo que necesitamos, son hechos y los hechos son tozudos, hasta el punto de que hoy los análisis académicos hablan de Turquía como un puro y duro sistema autoritario. ¿Puede un país autoritario ser candidato a la Unión Europea? Aparentemente sí. Pero un país autoritario nunca será miembro, porque este es todavía un club de democracias maduras y queremos que lo siga siendo.

El año pasado, prominentes figuras de la oposición —algunas desde la cárcel— y la sociedad civil proeuropea me han pedido mantener e incluso reactivar el proceso de adhesión. Es decir, las víctimas del autoritarismo nos piden no matar la esperanza en un futuro democrático para el país. Y ese es el difícil equilibrio del informe.

No matar la esperanza significa diferenciar claramente entre el estatuto de país candidato y el resto de la relación. Ser miembro de la Unión Europea va de democracia y ser socio va de intereses. Lo que no podemos admitir es utilizar las reglas de un juego en la mesa del otro, es decir, olvidando el gravísimo deterioro democrático del país. Por eso el informe es claro: de ninguna manera puede reactivarse ahora el proceso de adhesión, está congelado y por buenas razones.

Lo que nos gustaría, comisaria Kos, desde el Parlamento, es que el Ejecutivo comunitario nos acompañara en nuestras críticas a la situación doméstica del país. El silencio o la debilidad de las declaraciones de la Comisión y el Servicio Exterior, ante situaciones como las detenciones de alcaldes —incluido el de Estambul—, la voladura controlada del principal partido de la oposición y tantos otros pasos antidemocráticos, tienen dos consecuencias: dar vía libre al autoritarismo y aumentar el sentimiento de abandono, de orfandad, de la sociedad civil democrática. Si hay un cambio democrático en el país, nos va a costar decenios recuperar la credibilidad que estamos perdiendo ahora con esa sociedad civil. Y el Parlamento no quiere ser cómplice de ese silencio.

Nos queda la otra parte de la relación: el partenariado y el juego de intereses coincidentes o divergentes. Tenemos que encontrar un esquema de convivencia y buena vecindad con Turquía, pero sin rendir nuestros principios. Por eso, las relaciones con Chipre y Grecia forman parte esencial de cualquier modelo de relación futura. Cualquier acción o declaración agresiva va a ser tenida en cuenta por la Unión Europea.

Se habla mucho del factor seguridad y defensa en el conjunto de las relaciones. El informe reconoce la importancia de Turquía desde este punto de vista, pero también señala como obstáculos graves, además de las imprescindibles buenas relaciones de vecindad, el grado de confianza mutua necesaria para una colaboración en materia de seguridad y defensa que está todavía muy lejos de alcanzarse —como la unión aduanera, vinculada inevitablemente a la certidumbre legal, la independencia judicial, imprescindible para los inversores, o la liberalización de visados, cuya responsabilidad está en manos de las autoridades turcas—.

No obstante, el Parlamento apoya y espera la reanudación de todos los diálogos de alto nivel, la continuidad de los acuerdos migratorios sin forzar retornos a Siria, la agenda de conectividad, la itinerancia o el sistema bancario.
No es un equilibrio fácil, es cierto. Lo único que pido es que no saquemos de la ecuación a una sociedad civil que necesita, más que nunca, a la Unión Europea.

En el corazón de todo proceso de adhesión están los estándares democráticos, por eso en cada informe de progreso también deben estarlo. Ser el ponente de Turquía es muy frustrante. Mis colegas que lidian con otros países a veces tienen buenas noticias. Yo llevo diez años sin buenas noticias. De hecho, Turquía es el país candidato cuyos estándares democráticos más se han deteriorado en los últimos años —consecuencia de una absoluta falta de voluntad política de ser coherentes con las ocasionales declaraciones proeuropeas de las autoridades—.

No son declaraciones lo que necesitamos, son hechos y los hechos son tozudos, hasta el punto de que hoy los análisis académicos hablan de Turquía como un puro y duro sistema autoritario. ¿Puede un país autoritario ser candidato a la Unión Europea? Aparentemente sí. Pero un país autoritario nunca será miembro, porque este es todavía un club de democracias maduras y queremos que lo siga siendo.

El año pasado, prominentes figuras de la oposición —algunas desde la cárcel— y la sociedad civil proeuropea me han pedido mantener e incluso reactivar el proceso de adhesión. Es decir, las víctimas del autoritarismo nos piden no matar la esperanza en un futuro democrático para el país. Y ese es el difícil equilibrio del informe.

No matar la esperanza significa diferenciar claramente entre el estatuto de país candidato y el resto de la relación. Ser miembro de la Unión Europea va de democracia y ser socio va de intereses. Lo que no podemos admitir es utilizar las reglas de un juego en la mesa del otro, es decir, olvidando el gravísimo deterioro democrático del país. Por eso el informe es claro: de ninguna manera puede reactivarse ahora el proceso de adhesión, está congelado y por buenas razones.

Lo que nos gustaría, comisaria Kos, desde el Parlamento, es que el Ejecutivo comunitario nos acompañara en nuestras críticas a la situación doméstica del país. El silencio o la debilidad de las declaraciones de la Comisión y el Servicio Exterior, ante situaciones como las detenciones de alcaldes —incluido el de Estambul—, la voladura controlada del principal partido de la oposición y tantos otros pasos antidemocráticos, tienen dos consecuencias: dar vía libre al autoritarismo y aumentar el sentimiento de abandono, de orfandad, de la sociedad civil democrática. Si hay un cambio democrático en el país, nos va a costar decenios recuperar la credibilidad que estamos perdiendo ahora con esa sociedad civil. Y el Parlamento no quiere ser cómplice de ese silencio.

Nos queda la otra parte de la relación: el partenariado y el juego de intereses coincidentes o divergentes. Tenemos que encontrar un esquema de convivencia y buena vecindad con Turquía, pero sin rendir nuestros principios. Por eso, las relaciones con Chipre y Grecia forman parte esencial de cualquier modelo de relación futura. Cualquier acción o declaración agresiva va a ser tenida en cuenta por la Unión Europea.

Se habla mucho del factor seguridad y defensa en el conjunto de las relaciones. El informe reconoce la importancia de Turquía desde este punto de vista, pero también señala como obstáculos graves, además de las imprescindibles buenas relaciones de vecindad, el grado de confianza mutua necesaria para una colaboración en materia de seguridad y defensa que está todavía muy lejos de alcanzarse —como la unión aduanera, vinculada inevitablemente a la certidumbre legal, la independencia judicial, imprescindible para los inversores, o la liberalización de visados, cuya responsabilidad está en manos de las autoridades turcas—.

No obstante, el Parlamento apoya y espera la reanudación de todos los diálogos de alto nivel, la continuidad de los acuerdos migratorios sin forzar retornos a Siria, la agenda de conectividad, la itinerancia o el sistema bancario.

No es un equilibrio fácil, es cierto. Lo único que pido es que no saquemos de la ecuación a una sociedad civil que necesita, más que nunca, a la Unión Europea.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Marta Kos, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members of the European Parliament, dear rapporteur, Nacho Sánchez Amor, I would like to thank this House, in particular you, dear Nacho, and the Members of the AFET Committee for your comprehensive report on Türkiye.

Your report aligns with the Commission's 2025 Report 2025 and reflects the worrying democratic developments in Türkiye. Türkiye is a key partner, a NATO ally and a candidate country. Both the EU and Türkiye have a mutual interest to deepen cooperation, as the European Parliament has called for many times, and I can say we have advanced along this path.

At the same time, despite Türkiye's strategic goal of joining the EU, this intention has not been accompanied by tangible progress, notably when it comes to fundamental freedoms and the rule of law. On the contrary, we are seeing backsliding, the negative trends that led to the standstill in the accession negotiations in 2018 persist. Since the detention of Istanbul's democratically elected mayor, Mr Ekrem İmamoğlu, arrests and charges have continued to be brought against elected officials, political activists, civil society and business representatives, journalists and others. I have already spoken about these concerns in this House before. On 21 May, a court ruling in Ankara resulted in the removal of the leadership of Türkiye's largest opposition party. These developments give rise to questions about the rule of law, fundamental rights, democratic pluralism and the independence of the judiciary in Türkiye.

As you also noted, Türkiye's continued failure to implement the legally binding rulings of the European Court of Human Rights remains a major issue. Without serious progress on the rule of law, fundamental rights and democracy, there are no prospects to resume accession negotiations.

Our relationship with Türkiye also reflects a broader reality. In a shifting geopolitical landscape, we face common challenges. This is why we need to double down on our our efforts with Türkiye in areas of mutual interest. Following the April 2024 guidance of the European Council and its endorsement of a phased, proportionate and reversible approach to engaging with Türkiye, relations between the EU and Türkiye have experienced a gradual re-engagement in areas of joint interest.

Let me mention some developments. Türkiye continues to host 2.3 million refugees. We continue to cooperate on supporting them and on migration management. Türkiye is the EU's fifth-largest trading partner, with a trade volume almost twice as high as that with Mercosur or India. We are working together with Türkiye on reducing trade barriers, which are now at 14, down from 26 in 2021. We are also looking at ways to improve the implementation of the Customs Union.

Türkiye is a central hub for trade routes between Europe and Asia. Cooperation on the Cross-Regional Connectivity Agenda, in which Türkiye shares an interest, is important for the EU. It can help to better link Europe with the South Caucasus and Central Asia, fostering the EU's competitiveness and regional stability and prosperity.

The European Union has a strategic interest in a stable and secure environment in the Eastern Mediterranean, and in the development of a cooperative and mutually beneficial relationship with Türkiye. Türkiye's own constructive engagement will be instrumental in advancing our cooperation. Progress on the Cyprus issue will be essential to deepen further our cooperation. In this regard, we welcome the efforts by the United Nations Secretary-General's Personal Envoy on Cyprus, Maria Angela Holguín Cuéllar. The EU is ready to play an active role in supporting the UN-led process.

Action is also needed to prevent the circumvention of EU sanctions. Türkiye has engaged constructively on this, but more remains to be done, such as on the issue of false transit of exports and the shadow fleet. I am looking forward to your debate.

interventions.speaker_label: Isabel Wiseler-Lima, au nom du groupe PPE.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, la Turquie est un partenaire important de l'Union alliée au sein de l'OTAN, voisin, avec lequel nous coopérons sur le commerce, la sécurité et la migration. Une relation d'intérêt partagé dans un respect mutuel. Je salue sincèrement l'aspiration européenne de nos interlocuteurs turcs. Elle est réelle. Nous savons toutefois que, pour une partie d'entre eux, l'Europe est d'abord perçue à travers une perspective économique. Or, notre Union est avant tout une communauté de valeurs et c'est sur ce socle que repose une adhésion.

Mais ce n'est pas la voie que privilégient aujourd'hui les autorités gouvernementales. Au vu des évolutions récentes et de la situation non résolue de Chypre, les conditions d'une reprise des négociations qui sont à l'arrêt depuis 2018, ne sont tout simplement pas réunies. Regardons les faits. Les congrès du CHP annulés, le maire d'Istanbul Ekrem İmamoğlu emprisonné, Osman Kavala détenu au mépris de la Cour européenne des droits de l'homme, une presse intimidée, le retrait de la convention d'Istanbul, ce ne sont pas des incidents, c'est une trajectoire. Oui au dialogue, oui à un partenariat exigeant. Mais l'aspiration européenne devra, elle, se traduire en actes, fidèles aux valeurs de nos démocraties libérales. Je vous remercie et remercie également la bonne collaboration avec le rapporteur, M. Sánchez Amor.
