Ma per noi italiani c'è un elemento che conta più di ogni altro: la concretezza dei risultati. L'Albania si sta dimostrando un alleato affidabile e strategico nella lotta all'immigrazione irregolare, grazie al protocollo Italia-Albania voluto fortemente dal governo italiano di centro-destra.

Ho visitato personalmente il centro di Gjadër. È una struttura moderna e che funziona, pienamente operativa. I rimpatri sono in costante aumento, con una crescita tra il 20 e il 30 % annuo e l'obiettivo è raggiungere 10 000 rimpatri annui. Di fronte a questi risultati c'è ancora chi tenta di ostacolare questo modello: certa sinistra ideologica e alcuni magistrati politicizzati che preferiscono bloccare le soluzioni anziché affrontare il problema.

L'Europa decida da che parte stare: dalla parte di chi subisce l'immigrazione illegale o dalla parte di chi la contrasta con coraggio e pragmatismo.

L'Albania ha fatto la sua scelta. Adesso tocca all'Unione europea riconoscere chi con i fatti contribuisce a difendere i nostri confini e la nostra sicurezza.

paragraphs.text: Г-н Председател, г-жо Комисар, колеги, за мен като човек от Балканите и докладчик в сянка за Косово и Северна Македония темата за разширяването е критично важна.

Аз благодаря на докладчика за Косово, г-н Терас. Важно беше да изпратим послание към тази млада страна, че оценяваме нейните усилия и подкрепяме нейния европейски път. Но там българското малцинство вече години наред чака своето признаване и нека властите в Прищина най-сетне да направят промените, гарантиращи правата на нашите братя.

На другия полюс е докладът за Северна Македония. Вчера в Скопие посред бял ден бяха запалени два дипломатически автомобила на българското посолство. По-рано горя културният клуб на България в Битоля, а подпалвачът по-късно беше героизиран от медиите на управляващата партия ДПМНЕ. Това е резултатът от години налагана омраза спрямо българите и България от политици като Мицковски и Силяновска. Това не спира, а ние тук, които претендираме, че представляваме демокрацията и хуманността, е крайно време да осъдим античовешката идеология на македонизма и да защитим правата на българите там. Такава Северна Македония няма място в Европейския съюз, докато не извърши нужните реформи.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, North Macedonia has been a candidate country for over two decades – a lot of time for trust, fatigue and disappointment – yet 71 % of its citizens still strongly support joining the European Union. This dedication deserves a clear European future.

However, further progress on internal reforms is still needed. This is especially true for the rule of law, fighting corruption and the justice system. We see slight progress since the last report, but political leaders in Skopje must show the will to break this deadlock. I urge all parties to work together to pass the necessary constitutional changes. This step is essential to open the first negotiation cluster.

Together, we must speed up the reform agenda. With strong commitment, we can use gradual integration tools. These tools give citizens real EU benefits before full membership. North Macedonia's future is in the European Union, but this path must remain strictly based on merit and delivered reforms.

paragraphs.text: Spoštovana predsednica, spoštovane kolegice in kolegi, cenjena komisarka. Od solunske obljube je minilo že 23 let, od zadnje širitve Evropske unije pa 13. Toda letos končno znova vidimo pripravo prve pristopne pogodbe za članstvo v Evropski uniji.

Črna gora ima zgodovinsko priložnost prekiniti najdaljše obdobje brez širitve Evropske unije in Zahodnemu Balkanu, še posebej pa predsedniku Srbije, gospodu Vučiću, poslati jasno sporočilo: da se demokratične reforme izplačajo in da se širitev Evropske unije dogaja in lahko tudi doseže.

Za prečkanje ciljne črte bo potrebno do konca izvesti reforme na področju vladavine prava in popolno uresničitev vmesnega poročila. Tudi mi na strani Evropske unije moramo opraviti svoj del naloge ter zaščititi Črno goro pred zunanjimi pritiski in tujimi vplivi, začenši s takojšnjo razširitvijo digitalnega enotnega trga na regijo. Čestitke Črni gori na tej poti, skupaj lahko to dosežemo.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, hyvät kollegat, Euroopan parlamentin käsiteltävänä oleva Kosovo-mietintö lähettää tärkeän ja kaksitahoisen viestin. Toisaalta se tunnustaa Kosovon selkeän eurooppalaisen perspektiivin ja kansalaisten vahvan sitoutumisen EU-integraatioon. Toisaalta se tuo esiin huolen poliittisesta umpikujasta, joka on hidastanut uudistuksia ja heikentänyt instituutioiden toimintakykyä.

On selvää, että uskottava EU-lähentyminen perustuu ennen kaikkea kestävään poliittiseen vakauteen, oikeusvaltion vahvistamiseen ja konkreettisiin mitattaviin uudistuksiin. Ilman näitä edellytyksiä eurooppalainen näkymä ei voi toteutua täysimääräisesti.

Samalla meidän on kuitenkin oltava johdonmukaisia. EU:n sitoutuminen Länsi-Balkanin integraatioon on strateginen valinta, eikä sitä pidä heikentää lyhyen aikavälin poliittisilla kriiseillä. Dialogi Kosovon ja Serbian välillä pysyy edelleen keskeisenä osana tätä prosessia, ja sitä pitää kyetä edistämään. Siksi tämä mietintö on oikeassa tasapainottaessaan vaatimukset ja kannusteet, tiukka reformien suhteen, mutta selkeästi sitoutunut Kosovon eurooppalaiseen tulevaisuuteen.

paragraphs.text: Г-н Председател, вчера запалиха коли на българското посолство в Скопие. Пред българското посолство в Скопие по време на палежа има полицаи, които не реагират и извършителят запалва българските дипломатически коли напълно необезпокояван. Но добре, че България вече е в клуба на богатите, красивите и успелите, така че нашите интереси да се уважават и нашата дума да тежи и никой да не си позволява да се гаври с българските интереси и с българите.

Искам да видя как Брюксел ще защити демократичните ценности и правата на българите и на България в Македония. И тъй като другите народи и държави в Европейския съюз не са много наясно с проблематиката на Балканите, нека да го кажа съвсем ясно и точно, за да се знае от всички. В Македония се говори диалект на българския език и в Македония преобладаващата част от населението е от български произход.
Сега ще го кажа и на българския език, който се говори в Македония. „Ова македонска история е вещачка. Тя е фалсификат, що е написан во Белград от сърбо-комунистичките историчари.“

Слушаме красиви думи днес за европейски ценности, за европейското бъдеще на Западните Балкани, а десетки хиляди българи в Северна Македония гледат как правата им се потъпкват системно. А тук официално Европейският съюз гледа настрани.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, Commissioner, enlargement is not a vague ambition. It is a concrete commitment. And let me state it plainly: I support the enlargement of the European Union because it strengthens our Union strategically, politically and economically.

North Macedonia belongs to the European Union. Its European path must not be held hostage by hesitation or artificial obstacles. A credible, merit‑based process means delivering on our promises when conditions are met. But let us also be honest: it is in the direct interest of our current Member States. A larger, more stable and more united Europe brings security, influence and prosperity for all of us.
Finally, we must reject the politics of blockades. Dialogue must be about solving problems, not inventing new ones. If we are serious about Europe's future, we must like it.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Madam President, EU enlargement is a geopolitical necessity, while the accession progress depends only on the candidate countries' fulfilment of the Copenhagen political criteria that ensure their commitment to EU values and the rule of law. Montenegro remains the most advanced candidate country in accession to the EU, and we fully support its steady progress to join the EU. The establishment of the ad hoc working party on Montenegro's accession treaty under the Cyprus Presidency also marks a key step forward.

Further progress remains, though, to be done, especially in electoral reform, media freedom and controversial laws on internal affairs and on the National Security Agency. The strong public support, however, for EU accession in Montenegro is an essential element of this progress, and all political actors should intensify their efforts to deliver the necessary reforms.
As I said this morning to Montenegro's President, it has my group's support and my personal commitment to it becoming the EU's 28th member by 2028.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, je ne vais pas vous faire la danse du ventre, Madame, mais je ne vais pas faire semblant. Pour nous, l’élargissement, c’est non, et je vais vous expliquer pourquoi. Parce que, d’abord, l’Union européenne, c’est une sorte de grande colocation, qu’on a déjà du mal à 27, et donc faire l’élargissement, ça serait difficile.

Alors, j’ai voulu être précis, parce que j’aime bien être technique et factuel. Prenons le Kosovo: c’est un territoire marqué par des trafics d’armes, de drogue, d’êtres humains, mais aussi par les réseaux islamistes, et dont la souveraineté n’est toujours pas reconnue par cinq des États membres – donc, compliqué d’accueillir ce pays-là.
La Bosnie: un pays paralysé par des divisions institutionnelles, confronté au risque de sécession, corruption endémique et influence persistante du crime organisé.

L’Albanie, plaque tournante majeure du trafic de stupéfiants vers l’Europe, dont les réseaux criminels sont régulièrement identifiés par les services de sécurité européens, et qui entretient des liens étroits avec la Turquie d’Erdoğan, dont les intérêts sont souvent contraires aux nôtres.

On pourrait citer la Macédoine du Nord, le Monténégro ou la Serbie, qui restent confrontés aussi à la corruption, aux influences étrangères, aux réseaux criminels. Je vous conseille de lire les rapports d’Europol ou d’Eurojust qui confirment ces dires, même les rapports du Parlement européen.
Donc, commençons à protéger les 27 États membres. Fonctionnons bien à vingt-sept ensemble, et après on pourra regarder l’élargissement, que nous, nous n’appelons pas de nos vœux.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Od lat wszyscy kibicujemy aspiracjom krajów bałkańskich do członkostwa w Unii Europejskiej. Jeszcze niedawno Unia Europejska była widziana oczami mieszkańców Bałkanów jako ziemia obiecana. Niestety, tak już nie jest. Unia Europejska nie jest projektem, który jest gremialnie popierany w tych krajach. Według różnych badań w Serbii poparcie dla Unii spadło poniżej 50%, a w wielu innych krajach również znacząco się obniżyło.

Jednym z tych powodów jest niestety błędna polityka Komisji Europejskiej pod przewodnictwem Urszuli von der Leyen. Kryzys migracyjny, który Unia sama wywołała, oraz polityka Zielonego Ładu, która znacząco podnosi koszty energii i koszty życia w krajach Unii Europejskiej, uderzając także w rolnictwo. Do tego dochodzi nachalna ingerencja w wewnętrzne sprawy, procesy demokratyczne, ale również promocja polityki, jak chociażby LGBT. Ta polityka skutecznie wpycha Bałkany w ręce przede wszystkim Rosji, ale też Chin. Czas, aby Unia Europejska zmieniła podejście od mentora do partnera Bałkanów.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear Commissioner Kos, I want to speak to the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina, not to the ethnic groups. I want to speak to the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I want to tell them: many of your politicians are still caught up in the past. But I can tell you, Europe is all about understanding our past, understanding our often difficult past, but to have a better future, especially for the next generations, for our children.

But what is happening in Bosnia and Herzegovina? Children are going to schools with different entrances. They learn with different schoolbooks, different history books. They call it segregated schools. That is incredible. You have to change that and the people of Bosnia have to tell the politicians they have to change that.

I am afraid – and Commissioner Kos, you know that – I am afraid that people in Bosnia and Herzegovina will need some kind of honest broker to explain to them that the way they are organised now, they will not get into the European Union.

And one word to the Austrians: yes, Bosnia and Herzegovina is also important for us. Austria is a great investor there. We are making money there. So, let's have a European future, not a segregated one.

paragraphs.text: Poštovana predsjedavajuća, kolegice i kolege, pozivam vas da malo sa mnom zamišljate 2038. godinu. Tu je brzi vlak koji juri na relaciji Zagreb – Banja Luka – Sarajevo – Mostar, pa ode skroz preko Podgorice do Tirane. Jadranskim morem patrolira albansko-talijansko-hrvatsko-crnogorsko-slovenska flota znanstvenika i znanstvenica koji čuvaju Jadransko more od zagađenja i klimatskih promjena. Tu je na snazi velik i dalek, snažan dalekovod koji vuče struju s Mediterana, koju proizvode brojni solari, i vodi je skroz tamo negdje do Srbije, Bugarske i Rumunjske. I ono što je najvažnije, zamislimo 2038., upravo je počelo Svjetsko nogometno prvenstvo na zapadnom Balkanu, a ulaznice su pristupačne i dostupne svima.

To je vizija zapadnog Balkana u Europskoj uniji i uvjeren sam da tu viziju dijele mnogi građani i građanke zapadnog Balkana, ali stalno nailaze na prepreke i na otpore. I zato s tom vizijom pozivam sve da još jednom radimo dalje da zapadni Balkan uđe što prije u Europsku uniju.

paragraphs.text: Κυρία Πρόεδρε, διεύρυνση σημαίνει ειρήνη. Εμείς το έχουμε αποδείξει αυτό. Με πρωθυπουργό τον Αλέξη Τσίπρα, η κυβέρνηση της Αριστεράς υπέγραψε τη συμφωνία των Πρεσπών με τη Βόρεια Μακεδονία. Όμως, η ένταξη δεν είναι μόνο γεωπολιτική και οικονομική επιλογή, αλλά και δέσμευση στις αξίες της δημοκρατίας και του κράτους δικαίου.

Στην Αλβανία, χιλιάδες πολίτες διαδηλώνουν εδώ και μέρες με αφορμή την κατασκευή μεγάλου τουριστικού συγκροτήματος σε προστατευόμενη περιοχή, εκφράζοντας σοβαρές ανησυχίες για το περιβάλλον, την έλλειψη διαφάνειας, τα δικαιώματα ιδιοκτησίας και τη διαφθορά.

Για να γίνω χρήσιμος εδώ, Επίτροπε, ζητάμε από την Επιτροπή άμεση και επείγουσα ενημέρωση του Ευρωπαϊκού Κοινοβουλίου για τις εξελίξεις στην Αλβανία, για την τήρηση των κριτηρίων του κράτους δικαίου και της προστασίας του περιβάλλοντος, καθώς και την προέλευση των χρημάτων της επένδυσης, σύμφωνα με την έρευνα που διεξάγει το SPAK, το Συμβούλιο των Εισαγγελέων της Αλβανίας. Θέλουμε να έχουμε άποψη. Αυτή είναι η τοποθέτηση της Αριστεράς.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, I want to say something completely different. As Chair of the Committee on Foreign Affairs, I would first of all like to thank all the rapporteurs and all the shadow rapporteurs and all the others in this House involved in carefully drafting and presenting these five reports. That's hard work. Well done!

But as Chair of our Committee on Foreign Affairs, I would also like to state that I regret that instead of us having individual debates on individual reports on individual countries, five Western Balkan countries have been pooled together under one item. I regret this, and I do hope that this will not be a precedent for the future.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, Commissioner – and, regrettably, no Council on this key topic – we are slowly moving from words to real action on enlargement, but it's too slow. We need a breakthrough – not business as usual! The geopolitical stakes demand it.

To the Council, I would have said: have the courage to embrace innovative proposals; do not reject ideas without offering better alternatives. It's in our own interest. When accession perspectives lack credibility, and the EU's posture is appeasement of the 'dear Alexander' kind, then the status quo becomes an attractive alternative.

In the Western Balkans, it produced an entrenched and dangerously toxic mix of identity politics and state capture. And North Macedonia, regrettably, is no exception. The impasse on its EU path is masking slow undermining of the Ohrid agreement and an excuse to halt reforms citizens actually need. The country's leadership must break the impasse and amend the Constitution. And the Council must make crystal clear to everyone involved: no more delays, no obstruction, no more business as usual.

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, o evropské budoucnosti západního Balkánu mluvíme už roky. Stále dokola posloucháme projevy o společné Evropě a o strategickém významu tohoto regionu pro zajištění naší bezpečnosti. Jenže samotné deklarace nové členské státy nepřivedou. Rumunsko a Bulharsko vstoupily do Evropské unie přibližně dvanáct let po podání přihlášky. Chorvatsko se stalo členem po deseti letech. Albánie však čeká sedmnáct let a Černá Hora dokonce osmnáct let. Přitom právě tyto dvě země dnes patří mezi nejlépe připravené kandidáty na členství. Nikdo nezpochybňuje, že kandidátské země musí plnit přísné podmínky. Nemůžeme ale přehlížet, že během let jsme proces opakovaně měnili, přidávali nové procedury a zvyšovali požadavky. Albánie čekala na zahájení jednání roky navzdory doporučení Evropské komise. Černá Hora během samotných přístupových rozhovorů čelila změně metodiky rozšiřování. To vytváří dojem, že se cílová čára neustále posouvá.

Pokud kandidátské země provádějí reformy, přijímají evropskou legislativu a plní své závazky, musí následovat odpovídající pokrok. Jinak riskujeme ztrátu důvěry občanů v evropskou perspektivu a oslabujeme vlastní vliv v regionu.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, the report on Albania delivers an encouraging message, recognising the country's steady progress in its European path while outlining the challenges that still need to be addressed.
Albania is closely connected to the EU through its people. They study, work, travel and contribute across our continent, creating strong social, cultural and economic ties.
Albania's role in regional energy and transport interconnectivity is particularly valuable. These projects help diversify routes and enhance energy security and cooperation for the entire region.

The report also highlights certain challenges that must be resolved, above all, for the benefit of the Albanians, like effective enforcement of final court decisions. Therefore, I would like to warmly congratulate the Albanian authorities on their decision to return the Iorga House to the Romanian state by September 2026.

This property, which once belonged to Romania, was confiscated during the Communist regime and, despite the final court decision, this restitution has been delayed for years. This restitution, which I strongly advocated for, repairs the Communist injustice and honours our shared Romanian and Albanian history.

paragraphs.text: Г-жо Председател, г-жо Комисар, колеги, България последователно подкрепя страните от Западните Балкани и съседите ни от Северна Македония в европейския им път. Ние бяхме първата държава, признала нейната независимост, и винаги сме отстоявали мястото на Западните Балкани в Европейския съюз.
Но европейската интеграция е процес, основан на доверие и изпълнение на поетите задължения. Конституционните промени и добросъседските отношения не са нови условия, а част от вече договорената рамка.

Не можем да пренебрегваме враждебното отношение, демонстрирано от публични лица и обществени фигури, нито тревожните сигнали за напрежение и агресия. Вчерашния палеж на автомобили на българската дипломатическа мисия в Скопие показва колко е важно институциите последователно да противодействат на всяка форма на омраза и насилие. Защитата на правата на гражданите, самоопределящи се като българи, е въпрос на европейски ценности и върховенство на правото. И по тази тема компромиси не може да има. България е готова да продължи да подкрепя европейската интеграция на Северна Македония, но този процес изисква взаимно уважение и спазване на договореното от всяка страна.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Wir Grüne haben uns immer für den Beitritt von neuen Ländern zur EU ausgesprochen. Diese Unterstützung ist aber an Bedingungen geknüpft, und die Kopenhagener Kriterien sind für uns nicht verhandelbar. Umso verstörender ist es, dass die Kommission wegschaut, wenn Umweltrecht und Rechtsstaatlichkeit infrage gestellt werden.

Ich möchte heute den Mut der Bürgerinnen und Bürger würdigen, die seit 17 Tagen für den Schutz des zukünftigen Natura-2000-Gebietes Vjosa-Narta auf die Straße gehen, denn es braucht Mut, um sich gegen die Kushners und Trumps dieser Welt zu stellen, wenn die eigene Regierung einem mit Repressionen begegnet.

Die Menschen verteidigen nicht nur die einzigartige Natur, sie verteidigen auch demokratische Teilhabe und Rechtsstaatlichkeit, denn Standards müssen erfüllt sein, bevor unumkehrbare Eingriffe vorgenommen werden. Wenn ein Lebensraum zerstört ist, kann man ihn nicht einfach wiederherstellen. Mönchsrobbe, Pelikane, Karettschildkröten, Flamingos – sie verlieren einen ihrer letzten Rückzugsräume.
Ich fordere die Kommission auf, die Einhaltung der Standards sicherzustellen und sich nicht mit Lippenbekenntnissen zufrieden zu geben, während im Vjosa-Delta die Bagger rollen.

paragraphs.text: (Beginn des Redebeitrags in einer Sprache, die keine Amtssprache der EU ist) … Tausende Menschen gehen in Albanien jeden Tag auf die Straße, um die Lagune von Narta zu schützen. Sie kämpfen für eines der wichtigsten Feuchtgebiete im ganzen Mittelmeerraum, Heimat tausender Flamingos und vieler weiterer seltener Tierarten. Die sogenannte Flamingo-Revolution ist dabei weit mehr als eine Umweltbewegung: Sie ist der Protest von Menschen, die nicht mehr akzeptieren wollen, dass wertvolle Natur wirtschaftlichen Großprojekten geopfert wird.

Die albanische Bevölkerung ist mutig. Sie erhebt ihre Stimme für Transparenz, für den Schutz der Umwelt und für eine Zukunft, die nicht nur von wenigen Profiteuren bestimmt wird. Und wir müssen klar sagen: Wo Korruption politische Entscheidungen beeinflusst, geraten Demokratie, Rechtsstaatlichkeit und Naturschutz gleichermaßen unter Druck. Wer Natur zerstört, Korruption duldet und die Interessen der Bevölkerung übergeht, gefährdet dabei auch das Vertrauen in einen europäischen Weg Albaniens.
Europa steht für Rechtsstaatlichkeit, Transparenz und den Schutz unserer gemeinsamen Lebensgrundlage. Die Menschen in Albanien verdienen eine Zukunft in Freiheit, Demokratie und eine intakte Natur.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, to speak about five countries in one minute is quite a challenge, so I will go only with short messages.
First, to Bosnia and Herzegovina: unlock your potential, like your football team, like your football federation. It's time for a federal BiH in a confederal EU.
To Kosovo: the art of compromise is not a sign of weakness, but maturity.
To North Macedonia: you will be more European, not less Macedonian, if you include all national minorities in your constitution.
To Albania: democracy sometimes takes the form of a flamingo. Embrace it.
To Montenegro, we want you in the EU as a sovereign country, proud of your Montenegrin independence and identity, working together on the EU path – government and opposition.
And to us in the European Parliament: we say that we care about the Western Balkans, but it's a shame that we cannot devote enough time to debate each particular country.
I support the gradual integration approach for the Western Balkans, but I don't want to see a gradual disintegration of Parliament's role in the enlargement policy.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária, depois de mais de uma década de torpor, um novo alargamento da União Europeia está finalmente no horizonte, com o Montenegro na vanguarda do processo. O grupo de trabalho ad hoc para a redação do Tratado de Adesão está a funcionar, a negociação de mais dois capítulos foi concluída provisoriamente ontem e hoje podemos testemunhar o compromisso do seu presidente.

Mas estas últimas milhas do caminho serão as mais difíceis. Mais do que nunca, todos os atores políticos terão de saber estar à altura. Todas as reformas terão de contar com a participação ativa da sociedade civil e todas as mudanças terão de passar o teste da implementação. Mais do que nunca, antecipa‑se o crescimento do risco de interferência externa e de polarização associada às eleições de 2027.

Ao mesmo tempo, a União Europeia tem de estar preparada. Tem de ter vontade política para modelos inovadores, sem deixar de cumprir os critérios de Copenhaga, e as suas opiniões públicas têm de ser informadas do contexto, um contexto muito diferente dos anteriores.
Os montenegrinos apoiam generalizadamente um futuro europeu. Se frustrarmos as suas expetativas, é muito mais do que o futuro europeu do Montenegro que está em causa.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, the history of the Balkans is well read across the Europe. Hopefully, the years to come will show how the Balkans region, in all its diversity and uniqueness, will be a stable part of Europe.

The development of the Balkans secures, for its part, the peace of the entire continent. Especially in the current geopolitical situation, EU enlargement also has a security aspect to play. There's no doubt that if the Balkans don't lean towards Europe, they will find support outside Europe – and those players are undemocratic.

At the same time, however, the membership criteria must be strictly followed, especially when it comes to democracy and fighting corruption. And at the same time, we must be realistic: while the EU expands, integration can't just deepen in everything.
We must focus, above all, on the core tasks the EU has, and there is still plenty to do with the basic four rules of freedom so that people, services, money and free movement can function in the EU.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, what is Vjosa-Narta? For Albanians, it is a place where their grandparents fished. It is a place where the first saw flamingos or where they dream of taking their children one day.

For Edi Rama, it is a piggy bank being smashed open to be enjoyed by him and his friends. And his friends are Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner, and they do not care about concreting over rivers or killing one or two flamingos. They want to build a luxury resort for millionaires to make money out of it.

Albanians have been going out on the streets and their demand is clear: of course, they want economic development, but not at all costs. As long as basic needs are not being met – like water, health care, a proper wage – they have the right to question whether public resources are going towards citizens or towards a privileged few.

End of June, I will travel to Albania to listen and to find ideas that we can take home to help Albanians from here. And to the Commissioner, I have one question and that is whether she wants to push the Council to move towards qualified majority voting because this whole accession process is often being blocked because countries can use their veto.

paragraphs.text: Κυρία Πρόεδρε, η έκθεση που συζητάμε σήμερα αναγνωρίζει τόσο τη θέληση της Αλβανίας να γίνει πλήρες μέλος της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης όσο και του Ευρωπαϊκού Κοινοβουλίου να την στηρίξει.

Επί σχεδόν 13 χρόνια, με τη δικαιολογία ότι ο κύριος Rama προσφέρει σταθερότητα και έχει τον λαό μαζί του, oι ευρωπαϊκοί θεσμοί τον στηρίζουν άκριτα. Σήμερα οι Αλβανοί πολίτες διαμαρτύρονται για την έλλειψη δημοκρατίας, την έλλειψη ευημερίας, την καταπάτηση της ιδιοκτησίας, τη χειραγώγηση της δικαιοσύνης, τον εναγκαλισμό της κυβέρνησης με το οργανωμένο έγκλημα και εν τέλει την εγκατάλειψη της χώρας από τους νέους.

Φυσικά, αυτές οι παθογένειες επιβαρύνουν δυσανάλογα τις μειονότητες, και δη την ελληνική που είναι η μεγαλύτερη στη χώρα. Η αποσιώπηση της πραγματικότητας, η ωραιοποίηση της κατάστασης και η ταύτιση σε πολλές περιπτώσεις της Επιτρόπου Kos με τον Αλβανό πρωθυπουργό ερμηνεύεται από μεγάλο μέρος της αλβανικής κοινωνίας όχι ως στήριξη στον αλβανικό λαό να υλοποιήσει το ευρωπαϊκό του όνειρο, αλλά ως στήριξη στον Rama. Πρέπει να είμαστε ξεκάθαροι. Ναι στην ένταξη, χωρίς εκπτώσεις στο ευρωπαϊκό κεκτημένο.

paragraphs.text: Poštovana predsjedavajuća, premda svaka od pet zemalja zapadnog Balkana ima svoj specifičan put prema članstvu, izazovi s kojima se suočavaju često su zajednički i zahtijevaju dosljedan pristup Europske unije.

Zemlje kandidatkinje moraju poštovati temeljne vrijednosti Unije te usklađivati svoje politike s europskima, uključujući zajedničku vanjsku i sigurnosnu politiku. Članstvo u Europskoj uniji donosi mnoga prava i prilike, ali podrazumijeva odgovornost i jasne obveze. Proces pristupanja Uniji mora biti konsenzualan i inkluzivan. Države kandidatkinje trebaju stvoriti uvjete u kojima i oporba i civilno društvo imaju svoje mjesto za stolom.

Nažalost, postoje i destruktivni akteri koji nastoje potkopati proces proširenja. Neovisno o tome dolaze li iz same regije ili izvan nje, takvo ponašanje treba jasno prepoznati i nedvosmisleno osuditi. U posljednje vrijeme svjedočimo novim prijedlozima o budućnosti politike proširenja. Međutim, pristup utemeljen na zaslugama mora ostati u samom središtu procesa proširenja.
Europska unija ipak nije samo pitanje pristupa financijskim sredstvima i jedinstvenom tržištu.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, domani voteremo una relazione che riguarda non solo l'Albania, ma anche la credibilità dell'Europa.

L'Albania ha dimostrato con i fatti di voler appartenere alla famiglia europea, con un percorso di riforme impegnativo, scegliendo con chiarezza il campo della libertà, della cooperazione e della sicurezza euro-atlantica. Per il gruppo dell'ECR, l'allargamento deve basarsi sul merito e sui risultati concreti, e quelli dell'Albania meritano di essere riconosciuti e sostenuti.

Per l'Italia, poi, l'Albania è un partner strategico e un alleato fondamentale per la stabilità dei Balcani e del Mediterraneo. Il rafforzamento della cooperazione tra Roma e Tirana, fortemente voluto dalla Presidente Giorgia Meloni, dimostra che una visione politica chiara può trasformare la vicinanza geografica in una vera alleanza strategica.
Per queste ragioni sosteniamo con convinzione la relazione, perché un'Albania più vicina all'Europa significa un'Europa più forte e più sicura.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, da presidente della delegazione Europa-Albania mi concentrerò soprattutto su questo paese che sta compiendo progressi encomiabili nel suo percorso europeo. In questo Parlamento siamo davvero in tanti a sostenere l'adesione dell'Albania al progetto comunitario, ma per motivi molto diversi da quelli che sono echeggiati in quest'Aula.

Il processo di adesione ci mette di fronte ai nostri doveri e alle nostre scelte, agli standard europei nella crescita equilibrata, nella lotta alla corruzione, per la libertà di stampa, gli altri diritti fondamentali, la tutela dell'ambiente.

A questo fine incoraggio anch'io le autorità albanesi a valorizzare il dialogo con le organizzazioni della società civile, in particolare in queste settimane, sulla valutazione di impatto ambientale di controversi investimenti immobiliari, sulla loro coerenza con l'acquis europeo.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, de Westelijke Balkan hoort bij de Europese toekomst en de vraag die voorligt, is: hoe gaan we die toekomst samen vormgeven? De Westelijke Balkan wacht al te lang op een plek in onze Unie, maar geopolitiek kent geen pauzeknop. Waar Europa aarzelt, ontstaat ruimte voor anderen. De vraag is daarom niet óf we uitbreiden, maar hoe. Een toetredingsverdrag uit 2011 past simpelweg niet bij de geopolitieke realiteit van 2026. De wereld is veranderd en wij moeten dat ook.

We hebben verdragen nodig met een stevige garantie voor de rechtsstaat en democratie. We hebben een proces nodig dat hervormingen beloont en niet alleen afvinkt. We hebben een Europese Unie nodig die helder communiceert naar haar inwoners en zichzelf durft te vernieuwen. Want uitbreiding zonder interne hervorming is geen vooruitgang, maar achterstallig onderhoud dat zich opstapelt.

paragraphs.text: Mevrouw Ter Laak, we staan hier helemaal hetzelfde in. Ik heb een vraag aan u over het probleem dat het hele toetredingsproces vertraagt, en dat gaat erover dat landen op meer dan zeventig momenten een veto mogen uitspreken, waardoor het proces steeds langzamer wordt en langer duurt. We zouden dat kunnen oplossen door naar een gekwalificeerde meerderheid van stemmen te gaan. Volgens mij bent u daar ook voorstander van. Landen moeten dit ook willen, dus ik vraag me af: kan ik op uw steun rekenen om er samen voor te zorgen dat er in ieder geval vanuit Nederland een push komt om te switchen en ons hiervoor hard te maken in het Europees Parlement?

paragraphs.text: Poštovana predsjedavajuća, poštovana povjerenice, kolegice i kolege, vrlo je jasno, ako Europska unija ne bude dovoljno prisutna u svom jugoistočnom susjedstvu, taj prostor neće ostati prazan. Popunit će ga drugi akteri kroz politički utjecaj, kapital bez europskih standarda, dezinformacije i politike koje produbljuju podjele umjesto suradnje. Zato proširenje moramo shvatiti kao strateško pitanje.

Nekoliko riječi o Crnoj Gori. Danas je najdalje odmakla i njezin napredak može biti snažan signal cijeloj regiji. Međutim, od strane Hrvatske želimo uputiti jasnu poruku. Pronalazak nestalih, obeštećenje logorašima, imovinsko-pravna pitanja, promjena imena bazena koji nosi ime čuvara bivšeg logora Morinj, gdje su mučeni hrvatski zarobljenici tijekom Domovinskog rata.

Srbija – pristup temeljen na zaslugama, ali ne ekonomskim, već onim zajedničkim, sigurnosti zajedničke vanjske politike jer nitko istodobno ne može biti posvećen EU integracijama i ignorirati temeljna stajališta o ključnim pitanjima. I da, i ja želim izraziti nezadovoljstvo što o ovako važnom pitanju imamo samo minutu i što imamo zajedničku raspravu o zemljama za koje želimo europsku perspektivu.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señora comisaria, la ampliación es una ambición proclamada de la Unión y tiene una mirada especial a los Balcanes Occidentales. No en vano es una región determinante en la historia de Europa, pero han recibido un debate conjunto situaciones muy distintas, porque no es lo mismo Montenegro que Bosnia y Herzegovina, del mismo modo que no es lo mismo Albania que Kosovo, a la que no reconocen cinco Estados miembros de la Unión a pesar de sus merecimientos, y, por tanto, hace falta un examen individualizado para honrar la cláusula de adhesión de cada país basada en los méritos.

Sin embargo, el elefante en la habitación que falta en este debate es su impacto sobre las instituciones europeas, porque cada adhesión significará un cambio en la distribución de escaños de este Parlamento Europeo y un cambio en las mayorías cualificadas y minorías de bloqueo en el Consejo. Y habrá que ver si se estrena de una vez el artículo 14 del Tratado de la Unión Europea que permite que la Comisión no incorpore mecánicamente un comisario por cada Estado miembro, de modo que pueda haber menos comisarios que Estados miembros. Todo eso habrá que debatirlo alguna vez. Y espero que sea pronto porque, si no, la adhesión no será creíble.

paragraphs.text: Poštovana predsjedavajuća, Crna Gora je među svim državama kandidatkinjama danas najbliže članstvu. Međutim, činjenica je da se ona i dalje suočava s pogubnim i štetnim utjecajem izvana. Kroz političke strukture, vjerske institucije, pokušaje oblikovanja unutarnjih procesa, Srbija sustavno nastoji ograničiti puni razvoj crnogorske suverenosti i usporiti njezin europski put. Pri tome se, posebno kroz velikosrpske proxyje u Crnoj Gori, učestalim provokacijama žele narušiti dobrosusjedski odnosi s Hrvatskom.

Zato je bitno da Crna Gora nastavi rješavati otvorena pitanja, uključujući sudbinu stradalnika Domovinskog rata, pitanja nestalih i povrat imovine. To su pitanja koja nadilaze bilateralne odnose jer se tiču temeljnih europskih vrijednosti, vladavine prava i obveza koje proizlaze iz europske pravne stečevine. Osim toga, ključno je da vlast, u suradnji s oporbom, uskladi zakone u sigurnosnom sektoru s europskim standardima. Sigurnosni sustav ne smije biti politiziran i služiti interesima jedne političke opcije.
Ukratko, želimo Crnu Goru u Europskoj uniji, ali onu europsku, demokratsku i suverenu Crnu Goru koja samostalno odlučuje o svojoj budućnosti, a nije ničije, pa ni srpsko drugo oko u glavi.

paragraphs.text: Gospa predsednica. Spoštovane kolegice in kolegi, današnja debata je pokazala, da je Zahodni Balkan izjemno pomembna regija v Evropi in pravzaprav že zdaj pripada evropskemu prostoru, ne pripada pa Evropski uniji. In zagotovo ima Evropska unija zdravilo za mnoge težave Zahodnega Balkana. In za Zahodni Balkan so najbolj nevarne stvari, kot so nacionalizem in podobno, kar smo v zgodovini že gledali. Iz današnjih debat je bilo tudi razvidno, da bi nekateri radi vsekakor vnesli bilateralna vprašanja kot tisto, kar bi na koncu odločalo o širitvi.

Poseben primer je Severna Makedonija pri tem. Po moje je bila velika napaka, da se leta 2019 ni začelo pogajanj, kajti takrat bi bil to močan signal, da je Severna Makedonija kljub temu nagrajena za tisto, kar je naredila v preteklosti. Ne nazadnje, veliko je bilo narejeno tudi s tem, da je spremenila svoje ime, kar si težko predstavljamo državljani drugih držav, da bi to storili.

Torej bi lahko začeli takrat pogajanja in bi bili mogoče danes v drugačni situaciji. Seveda bi pogajanja trajala, ampak zagotovo bi bil to kar dober signal. Tako da napaka je bila storjena takrat. Ampak kar je bilo, je bilo.

Rad bi se na koncu seveda zahvalil vsem, ki ste imeli konstruktivne debate. Zahvalil bi se tudi poročevalcem iz sence pri mojem poročilu. Zahvalil bi se sekretariatu in nenazadnje bi se rad zahvalil tudi komisarki Marti Kos za izjemno predanost in podporo pri našem skupnem delu.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Noch einmal zu Albanien. Albanien hat schon vor einem Jahrzehnt das Thema Rechtsstaatlichkeit ganz fundamental und gründlich aufgearbeitet, mehr als jeder andere Mitgliedstaat der Europäischen Union, durch den vetting-Prozess, wo von 800 Leuten 500 nicht bestanden haben, durch die Gründung der unabhängigen Ermittlungsbehörde SPAK, die unabhängig von politischem Ansehen aus allen politischen Lagern inzwischen Ermittlungen durchführt.

Ich bin mir auch sicher, dass in der gleichen Härte auch die Beachtung von Eigentumsrechten, von Umweltprüfung, von Flora- und Faunaschutz, von Naturschutz weiterhin und in Zukunft diese Beachtung finden wird. Ich bin mir auch sicher, dass die Natur geschützt wird, so wie das Vjosa-Delta und der Vjosa-Fluss ja auch in der Vergangenheit geschützt worden sind. Ich bin mir sicher, und ich appelliere auch, dass die Behörden und die Regierung diese Themen genauso ernst nehmen, wie auch der Kampf gegen Korruption ernst genommen wird.

Genauso müssen wir aber auch ernst nehmen, dass wirtschaftliche Entwicklung und soziale Fragen in das Zentrum der Politik in Albanien gestellt werden. Das Gesundheitssystem muss reformiert werden, die soziale Sicherheit muss erhöht werden, das Bildungssystem braucht Erneuerung. Das sind alles große Vorhaben. Und alle diese großen Vorhaben können nur durch den europäischen Reformdruck und durch dieses ambitionierte Ziel der Erreichung der europäischen Mitgliedschaft erreicht werden. Albanien ist bereit, mit einer Affengeschwindigkeit diese Reformen durchzuziehen, und das finde ich bewundernswert, weil es natürlich auch nicht nur leichte Reformen sind; und das ist ganz, ganz wichtig.

Lassen Sie mich zum Schluss noch eines sagen: Es ist ganz wichtig, auch solche Projekte wie Roam Like At Home auf den Balkan auszuweiten, weil sie ein Signal sind im täglichen Leben der Menschen im Westbalkan.

Zukunftschancen gehören genutzt, und das ist die große Geschichte von dieser europäischen Erweiterung, weil diese Zukunftschancen auch die Veränderung bringen. Und nicht nur dafür bin ich dankbar, sondern ich bin auch dankbar, dass die Kommissarin hier eine erbitterte Kämpferin für diese Chancen ist.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, colleagues, investing into reconciliation and investing into good bilateral relations is not an easy task.

My very own country, Austria, needed 40 years to admit that we were co‑perpetrators of the Nazi regime and it took us many, many years to invest into good neighbourly relations, to rebuild our relations to our neighbours.

This was not an easy exercise because the first step is to admit historical wrongdoings – not an easy one. But the second one is to show some forgiveness also to your neighbours. This is how we build good bilateral relations.

What is clear is that the protection of minorities is part of the European acquis and needs to be fulfilled. Including minorities – the Bulgarian and others – into the constitution is a clear requirement from the side of the European Union. Just to make that clear: attacks on minority institutions or attacks on diplomatic property is an absolute no go.

Prime Minister Mickoski was very clear. He condemned it with strong words. The perpetrator was arrested and is currently questioned on its motivation. This is how a state needs to react and I think it is good that he did a very clear statement on that publicly.

What is not part of the European acquis is 100 % similar history books. Even after 80 years of Austrian history after the Second World War, this not something we try to achieve or we have achieved with our neighbour states.

I would never dare to question the identity of my neighbouring country. Never. I would never dare to question Bulgarian identity just because you were 500 years under Ottoman rule. This acceptance of neighbours between each other is a fundament of cooperation.

And what I still want to say is that it is also on us, the European Union, to support the platform, to support the dialogue, to rebuild trust, to help with the small steps to rebuild good bilateral relations, in this case between Bulgaria and North Macedonia, but it is the case for the whole region.

It is also our responsibility to put resources on the table, to put personnel on the table and to support the region in reconciliation on all the different matters. We also have a responsibility in this.
I want to thank all the shadow rapporteurs for the constructive work and let's move forward.

This was not an easy exercise because the first step is to admit historical wrongdoings – not an easy one. But the second one is to show some forgiveness also to your neighbours. This is how we build good bilateral relations.

What is clear is that the protection of minorities is part of the European acquis and needs to be fulfilled. Including minorities – the Bulgarian and others – into the constitution is a clear requirement from the side of the European Union. Just to make that clear: attacks on minority institutions or attacks on diplomatic property is an absolute no go.

Prime Minister Mickoski was very clear. He condemned it with strong words. The perpetrator was arrested and is currently questioned on its motivation. This is how a state needs to react and I think it is good that he did a very clear statement on that publicly.

What is not part of the European acquis is 100 % similar history books. Even after 80 years of Austrian history after the Second World War, this not something we try to achieve or we have achieved with our neighbour states.

I would never dare to question the identity of my neighbouring country. Never. I would never dare to question Bulgarian identity just because you were 500 years under Ottoman rule. This acceptance of neighbours between each other is a fundament of cooperation.

And what I still want to say is that it is also on us, the European Union, to support the platform, to support the dialogue, to rebuild trust, to help with the small steps to rebuild good bilateral relations, in this case between Bulgaria and North Macedonia, but it is the case for the whole region.

It is also our responsibility to put resources on the table, to put personnel on the table and to support the region in reconciliation on all the different matters. We also have a responsibility in this.

I want to thank all the shadow rapporteurs for the constructive work and let's move forward.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, to conclude today's debate on the Western Balkans, I would like to emphasise some important issues that have also been discussed here today.

Firstly, the issue of the recognition of Kosovo's statehood by the five non‑recognisers has been unresolved for too long. In order for us to be able to more strongly link and integrate the entire Western Balkan region with the European Union, progress and ultimately a solution are needed to solve this issue. The European Parliament will certainly continue to monitor developments in all important areas when preparing the next report.

The ongoing stalemate and interregnum has had a really negative effect on Kosovo's performance in key critical areas. In my opinion, it is crucial to get the country functioning. This requires the willingness of the parties in political process in Kosovo to find compromises. If you have a functioning government, then we hopefully will have a debate dedicated only to Kosovo next year in this Parliament.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, advocating for EU enlargement is becoming harder and harder, unfortunately.

I would say that it's mainly due to many false narratives and, I'm not afraid to say, disinformation, many of which we've heard today during the debate – narratives that say that actually wanting the candidates to align with the EU acquis, to make some reforms, is interfering with their inner politics and somehow getting them rid of their sovereignty. That's not true, that's not true.

We need to keep our principles. We cannot compromise our own rules, and we cannot divert the weight from them. That would be wrong. But the truth is that we also cannot win the battle over enlargement with paperwork, with immense bureaucracy. We cannot just bury the candidate countries with tons of bureaucracy, hoping that this will somehow enable us to win over our adversaries or our competitors, like China, like Russia and, unfortunately, also like the United States, which all have interests in the Western Balkans.

We're never going to beat them with paperwork, we must admit to that. Our task is not to play the role of an overbearing parent, but to be a partner on the shared journey, the journey built on mutual commitment. And I think this is the best deal for all of us, for the Members and the candidates as well. And I think, and I hope, that this is how Bosnia and Herzegovina will hopefully be able to properly navigate from Dayton to Brussels.

paragraphs.text: Λουκάς Φουρλάς (PPE), γραπτώςΗ ευρωπαϊκή προοπτική των Δυτικών Βαλκανίων αποτελεί στρατηγική αναγκαιότητα για τη σταθερότητα και την ασφάλεια της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης. Η διεύρυνση παραμένει το ισχυρότερο εργαλείο της ΕΕ για την προώθηση της ειρήνης, της δημοκρατίας και του κράτους δικαίου σε μια περιοχή που φέρει βαριές ιστορικές πληγές, αλλά την ίδια στιγμή έχει και μεγάλες δυνατότητες.Ωστόσο, η ευρωπαϊκή πορεία δεν είναι άνευ όρων. Η πρόοδος των χωρών των Δυτικών Βαλκανίων πρέπει να βασίζεται σε πραγματικές μεταρρυθμίσεις. Παράλληλα, η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση οφείλει να παραμείνει αξιόπιστη, συνεπής και δίκαιη, αποφεύγοντας τα διπλά μέτρα και σταθμά.Σε μια εποχή αυξημένων εξωτερικών παρεμβάσεων και αποσταθεροποιητικών επιρροών, η απουσία της Ευρώπης από τα Δυτικά Βαλκάνια θα δημιουργούσε κενό, το οποίο θα σπεύσουν να καλύψουν άλλοι. Η ΕΕ πρέπει να επενδύσει πολιτικά, οικονομικά και θεσμικά στην περιοχή, προσφέροντας ένα σαφές, αξιόπιστο και απαιτητικό ευρωπαϊκό μονοπάτι.Το μέλλον των Δυτικών Βαλκανίων είναι ευρωπαϊκό, αλλά μόνο εφόσον στηρίζεται σε αξίες, κανόνες και αμοιβαίο σεβασμό.

paragraphs.text: Kinga Gál (PfE), írásbanA Parlament Nyugat-Balkánnal foglalkozó plenáris vitáján ismét kiderült, hogy egyértelmű kettős mérce érvényesül a bővítés terén.Az Európai Unió egyre inkább figyelmen kívül hagyja a teljesítményt és a felkészültséget, miközben döntéseit ideológiai és geopolitikai megfontolásokra alapozza. A szuverenista kormányokat bírálják, eredményeiket figyelmen kívül hagyják.Ez a hozzáállás Georgia esetében is látványosan megmutatkozik. A demokratikus választások eredményét sokan nem hajlandók elfogadni, szankciókat követelnek, politikai nyomást gyakorolnak és kívülről akarják felülírni a választók akaratát.Bosznia-Hercegovinában pedig a párbeszéd, a felelős együttműködés és a stabilitás megőrzése lenne a legfontosabb, nincs szükség politikai feszültségkeltésre és kioktatásra.Ukrajnával viszont megnyitották a csatlakozási tárgyalásokat, noha sok feltétel továbbra sem teljesül. Ráadásul Ukrajna csatlakozása komoly aggodalmakat vet fel a tagállamok számára, különösen a mezőgazdaság, a munkaerőpiac és a tagállamok biztonsága tekintetében.Az uniós szerződések és a koppenhágai kritériumok világos irányt szabnak: a bővítésnek érdemalapúnak kell lennie. Ha nem változtatnak ezen a hibás hozzáálláson, az Unió bővítéspolitikája elveszíti hitelességét, miközben a Nyugat-Balkán országait is egyre távolabb sodorják az európai úttól.
